title: Be Ruthless About the Life You Want – Alex Hormozi
speaker: Chris Williamson & Alex Hormozi

sentences.en: Today, we're going to go through as many of your lessons as we can in about three hours, and we're going to see what we can get through.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们打算在大约三个小时内尽可能多地完成你们的经验分享，看看我们能讲多少。

sentences.en: First one, a friendly reminder that in three generations, everyone who knew us will be dead, including the people whose opinions stopped you from doing what you wanted all along.
sentences.zh: 第一条，善意地提醒一下，三代之后，所有认识我们的人都会去世，包括那些一直以来用他们的观点阻止你做你想做的事的人。

sentences.en: Imagine that someone you know achieves every dream and hits every goal they have.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你认识的某个人实现了所有的梦想，达到了所有的目标。

sentences.en: Years later, they get old and die. Two years after that, how much do you care?
sentences.zh: 多年以后，他们老去并离世。在那之后的两年里，你还在乎多少？

sentences.en: About as much as everyone else will if you accomplish your goals and dreams.
sentences.zh: 跟你实现目标和梦想后，其他人对你的在乎程度差不多。

sentences.en: Do it for you.
sentences.zh: 为你自己而活。

sentences.en: So I think about death all the time because it's probably the central theme.
sentences.zh: 所以我一直都在思考死亡，因为它可能核心主题。

sentences.en: It's probably the thing that I think the most about.
sentences.zh: 它可能是我思考最多的事情。

sentences.en: And I think that influences how I see time and also how I think, how it influences agency, like what actions I'm willing to take despite the judgment of others.
sentences.zh: 我认为这影响了我看待时间的方式，也影响了我的思考方式，以及它如何影响行动力，比如尽管有别人的评判，我仍然愿意采取什么行动。

sentences.en: And so a lot of times, it might be because I have more insecurity than everyone that I think like, man, I want to do this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以很多时候，可能是因为我比任何人都更有不安全感，所以我才会想，天哪，我想做这件事。

sentences.en: And then I hear all these other voices of reasons why I shouldn't do it or why somebody else will say like, that's bad or you're bad or like, that's wrong, whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后我听到所有其他反对的声音，说我为什么不该这么做，或者别人会说，这很糟糕，你很糟糕，或者这不对，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And so I think I've had to come up with a lot of these devices to get around my own insecurities, to take action despite those insecurities.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我不得不相出很多这样的方法来克服我自己的不安全感，以便在这些不安全感面前采取行动。

sentences.en: And the biggest one that I think about is that it doesn't matter whether I achieve all of my goals or I don't achieve all of the goals in three generations, I'll be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 我想到的最重要的一点是，无论我是否实现了我所有的目标，或者我没有实现所有的目标，在三代之后，我都会被遗忘。

sentences.en: And the only people who were naysaying against me will also be dead.
sentences.zh: 而那些曾经反对我的人也都会死去。

sentences.en: And so then it's like, just do it for me.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好比，只管为自己去做吧。

sentences.en: And then when I wake up every day, there's only one voice I have to listen to.
sentences.zh: 然后当我每天醒来时，我只需要听从一个声音。

sentences.en: But that means that you need to be able to work out what to do from first principles.
sentences.zh: 但这意味着你需要能够从第一原理出发，弄清楚该做什么。

sentences.en: You now no longer have societal norms or assistance or role models or archetypes or expectations.
sentences.zh: 你不再拥有社会规范、援助、榜样、原型或期望。

sentences.en: And that's also difficult in a different way.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种不同寻常的困难。

sentences.en: I think that the more you flex whatever that muscle is of like independent thinking, the more it becomes the default way that you think.
sentences.zh: 我认为，你锻炼独立思考这种肌肉的次数越多，它就越会成为你默认的思考方式。

sentences.en: And then everyone else's action is to start looking more and more insane to you.
sentences.zh: 然后其他所有人的行为在你看来会开始显得越来越疯狂。

sentences.en: What's an example of that that you can think of?
sentences.zh: 你能想到一个这方面的例子吗？

sentences.en: I mean, shoot, just the most basic ones of living the life that you don't want, not wearing what you want to wear, not dating who you want to date, not living where you want to live.
sentences.zh: 我是说，天哪，最基本的例子就是过着你不想要的生活，不穿你想穿的衣服，不和你想约会的人约会，不住在你想住的地方。

sentences.en: You're living at home and you want to move and your parents say no and you don't make the move or you're dating a girl because she's socially accepted by your friend group.
sentences.zh: 你住在家里，你想搬出去，而你的父母说不，你就没有搬；或者你和某个女孩约会，因为她在你的朋友圈子里是被社会认可的。

sentences.en: She's safe, but there's always some distance in between you, but you're like, I don't want to risk it.
sentences.zh: 她很安全，但你们之间总是保持着一些距离，而你会想，我不想冒这个险。

sentences.en: Or you're in the job and every day you go there and you're like, I mean, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 或者你在做一份工作，每天去那里的时候你都在想，我是说，还行吧。

sentences.en: And the idea of just living an okay life just sounds so terrifying to me that the freedom to fail over and over again is still more fulfilling to me.
sentences.zh: 而那种仅仅过着“还行”的生活的想法对我来说太可怕了，以至于一次又一次经历失败的自由对我来说仍然更有成就感。

sentences.en: At least it feels like it's real than walking through on autopilot.
sentences.zh: 至少它感觉像是真实的，而不是像开着自动驾驶仪走过一生。

sentences.en: And so I think that's a lot of the choices that other people make that seem insane to me now, but didn't seem insane to me a decade ago.
sentences.zh: 所以我想这就是其他人做出的很多选择，现在在我看来显得很疯狂，但在十年前并不觉得疯狂。

sentences.en: You know what I mean? I think it's just like, as you practice taking more agency, taking more responsibility for the decisions, then you just get better and better at it.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？我觉得这就好像，当你练习更有主见、对决策承担更多责任时，你就会在这方面变得越来越熟练。

sentences.en: And then it just seems more and more ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 然后这一切就会显得越来越荒谬。

sentences.en: You're like, they're like, I just can't quit my job.
sentences.zh: 你会听到他们说，我就是辞不了职。

sentences.en: And you're like, why? Like, no, physically, why?
sentences.zh: 而你会问，为什么？我是说，从物理层面来说，为什么？

sentences.en: Like, why can't you quit your job? Like, like, you know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 就像，你为什么不能辞职？就像，你知道我的意思吗？

sentences.en: They start hyperventilating. It's like, you could, could you move in with your parents?
sentences.zh: 他们开始呼吸急促。这就好比，你可以，你能搬去和父母同住吗？

sentences.en: Could you move in with a friend? Could you split rent?
sentences.zh: 你能和朋友合租吗？你能分担房租吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I could, but I mean, other people who are going to die in a hundred years would think what?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我可以，但我的意思是，其他那些再过一百年就会死去的人会怎么想？

sentences.en: And one of my favorite ones is, and I say this all the time to Layla, like whenever we're getting to some sort of like mini complaint.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的一招是，我经常对Layla这么说，每当我们遇到某种微不足道的抱怨时。

sentences.en: It's like, you know, if you zoom out far enough, you can't see the earth.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，你知道，如果你把镜头拉得足够远，你就看不到地球了。

sentences.en: So we're talking about like, oh man, they're going to mess up this order on this vendors.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在谈论，哦天哪，这些供应商要把这个订单搞砸了。

sentences.en: I was like, you know, if you zoom out far enough, you can't see the earth.
sentences.zh: 我就说，你知道的，如果你把镜头拉得足够远，你就看不到地球了。

sentences.en: It's just like, it just puts everything immediately into perspective of how ridiculous some of the things that we're concerned about are.
sentences.zh: 这就像是，它立刻让所有事情都回归到应有的视角，让我们意识到我们所关心的某些事情是多么荒谬。

sentences.en: Sean Puri's got this thing where he says, don't follow what most people do because you don't want the results that most people get.
sentences.zh: Sean Puri说过这样一句话，不要盲目效仿大多数人的做法，因为你并不想得到大多数人那样的结果。

sentences.en: The average person is obese, likely to be divorced and has less than 1k in the bank.
sentences.zh: 普通人超重，很可能会离婚，而且银行存款不到1000美元。

sentences.en: It feels safe to do what everyone else is doing. but it's actually a terrible decision.
sentences.zh: 做大家都做的事感觉很安全，但实际上这是一个糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: It's like the best way to guarantee to not have the life that you want is to do what everyone else is doing.
sentences.zh: 这就好像要保证自己过不上想要的生活，最好的方法就是去做所有其他人都在做的事。

sentences.en: Unless you want what everyone else has, which no one does.
sentences.zh: 除非你想要所有其他人所拥有的东西，而没有人会想要那样。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's being able to think for yourself and treating it like a muscle, I think is a smart way to consider it because in the beginning, it's really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 是的，能够为自己思考并把它当作肌肉来对待，我认为这是一个明智的思考方式，因为一开始，这真的非常非常难。

sentences.en: You've been resting on societal norms and the way you've dealt with past trauma and your parents' expectations and what all of your friends do. and what's accepted and all of this stuff for so long that when it first comes to you needing to step on that muscle, it's like trying to move your ears.
sentences.zh: 你长期以来一直依赖社会规范、你处理过去创伤的方式、你父母的期望、你所有朋友的做法、什么是被接受的以及所有这些东西，以至于当它第一次需要你去调动那块肌肉时，就像试图动你的耳朵一样。

sentences.en: Like all humans have got muscles that can move their ears, but because no one works it as a child, they just atrophy away.
sentences.zh: 就像所有人类都有能动耳朵的肌肉，但因为小时候没有人去锻炼它，它们就那样萎缩了。

sentences.en: And this is the ear muscle of personal growth.
sentences.zh: 这就是个人成长的耳部肌肉。

sentences.en: I think I had a lot of practice with it because I had a, so like a lot of people have many voices that they hear that they feel are judging them, right?
sentences.zh: 我想我在这方面进行了很多练习，因为我有一个，就像很多人听到很多声音，他们觉得这些声音在评判他们，对吧？

sentences.en: They have their friends, they have their uncle, they have their siblings, they have their cousins, coworkers, whatever.
sentences.zh: 他们有朋友，有叔叔，有兄弟姐妹，有表亲，同事，等等。

sentences.en: I think I had just one voice that I heard really loudly.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我只有一个声音，我听得非常大声。

sentences.en: And I was talking to one of our employees the other day, and I was trying to put it in perspective, a younger guy.
sentences.zh: 前几天我和我们的一个员工谈话，我试图把它放在一个视角来看待，那是一个年轻的小伙子。

sentences.en: And I was like, imagine how much you care about your mother's opinion and your father's opinion and all of those other people.
sentences.zh: 我说，想象一下你有多在乎你母亲的意见、你父亲的意见以及所有其他人的意见。

sentences.en: And I was like, and now imagine that there's literally only one, because I had no siblings.
sentences.zh: 我说，现在想象一下，实际上只有一个，因为我没有兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: I basically had no mother. I had just a father.
sentences.zh: 我基本上没有母亲。我只有父亲。

sentences.en: And so like his approval was literally everything.
sentences.zh: 所以他的认可简直就是一切。

sentences.en: And he disapproved of the path that I wanted to take in my life.
sentences.zh: 而他并不赞同我在生活中想走的那条路。

sentences.en: And so I think a lot of these mental faculties or these little frameworks or these isms just came from like, how can I combat this incredibly booming voice in the background?
sentences.zh: 所以我想，所有这些心智能力、这些小框架或这些主义，都来自于，我如何才能对抗背景中这个极其响亮的声音？

sentences.en: Because like when I look at what I was doing at the time, like I was a consultant, I graduated in three years, I took the consulting job, I did all the things.
sentences.zh: 因为当我回顾我当时在做的事情时，我是一个顾问，我三年就毕业了，我接受了咨询工作，我做了所有这些事情。

sentences.en: But the craziest thing was that the moment that my father was most proud of me and he approved of my life the most was when I was the saddest.
sentences.zh: 但最疯狂的是，我父亲对我最骄傲、他对我的生活最认可的时刻，正是我最痛苦的时候。

sentences.en: And so that's when I was like, maybe his approval isn't the right way to feel good about life.
sentences.zh: 所以就在那时我想，也许他的认可并不是对生活感觉良好的正确方式。

sentences.en: And so that started basically the six-month journey from when I decided that I wanted to change my life till when I changed it.
sentences.zh: 于是，这基本上拉开了我从决定改变生活到真正改变它这六个月历程的序幕。

sentences.en: And I think that as you become more able or more potent or higher agency, that timeline between when you decide you want to do something and when you actually do, it just continues to compress, right?
sentences.zh: 我认为，随着你变得更有能力、更有潜力或更有主见，你决定做某事与真正付诸行动之间的那个时间线会不断缩短，对吧？

sentences.en: Like now if I want to change something, I'm like, let's change it.
sentences.zh: 就像现在我想改变什么，我就会说，我们改吧。

sentences.en: Like done. I like, I, we walk out of a thing.
sentences.zh: 就像完成了。我喜欢，我们从一个事情走出来。

sentences.en: I was like, we're never going to do that podcast again, or I don't want to talk to this person again or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 我说，我们再也不做那个播客了，或者我不想再和这个人说话了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Right. Whereas before it's like, okay, I have to, I have to sleep on it.
sentences.zh: 对吧。然而以前的情况是，好吧，我得，我得考虑一晚。

sentences.en: I have to really think about it. And like, how am I going to, it's like, why do I care about how I'm going to say it?
sentences.zh: 我得认真想想。就像，我要怎么去，这就像，我为什么要在乎我要怎么说？

sentences.en: This is what it is done. And it's just like, and that timeline is compressed, but the hardest one for me, like the first one was by far the hardest and everyone since then, the nice thing is that no matter how difficult your circumstances, if you have like the bigger the wall that you have to get through is, as soon as you get past that one big wall, you then can use that wall as the evidence for why you can jump over the next wall, because that will be the biggest one.
sentences.zh: 事情就是这样，搞定。这就像，那条时间线被压缩了，但对我来说最难的一次，第一个绝对是迄今为止最难的，而自那以后遇到的所有人，好的一点是，无论你的环境多么艰难，如果你必须跨过的墙越大，一旦你跨过了那座大墙，你就可以把那堵墙作为你能跳过下一堵墙的证据，因为那将是最大的一堵墙。

sentences.en: And so like, after I did quit my job and left my house and left Baltimore and didn't tell my dad until I was across the country, because I was so afraid, like people think of me as like some big alpha, whatever.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我辞了工作、离开家、离开巴尔的摩、直到我到了大洋彼岸才告诉我父亲之后，因为我太害怕了，人们把我看作是什么大男子主义者，随便吧。

sentences.en: I was like, I was such, I was so afraid of my father's disapproval that I didn't tell him until I physically left the state. like like i'm not like think about that like i wasn't even just one state over i was like five states over and then i was like hey by the way i'm going to california and he was like well let's come over we'll talk about it and i was like i'm in ohio already yeah already yeah then obviously he had a different reaction but like but then after that it was like what do i have to do now it's like oh i gotta i gotta sell strangers and i was like i told my dad i didn't want to do what wanted.
sentences.zh: 我说，我太害怕我父亲的不满，以至于直到我肉身离开这个州我才告诉他。就像，我不像，想想看——我甚至不只是去隔壁的一个州，我当时在五个州之外，然后我说，嘿，顺便说一下，我要去加利福尼亚了，他说，那过来吧，我们谈谈，我说，我已经在大老远了。对，已经在了。然后显然他有了不同的反应，但是，但是在那之后，这就变成了，我现在必须做什么？就像，哦，我得，我得把东西卖给陌生人，然后我说，我告诉过我父亲，我不想做原本想做的事。

sentences.en: How hard could this be? And so like it, it then becomes this one huge proof point.
sentences.zh: 这能有多难？所以它随后变成了这样一个巨大的证明点。

sentences.en: So the bigger that the dragon is that you have to slay, the more evidence you have that you can slay the next dragon.
sentences.zh: 因此，你要屠杀的恶魔越大，你能够屠杀下一个恶魔的证据就越多。

sentences.en: And I think that is, if there's ever been a good point for why getting over the one first hard one. is so hard is that it will then give you the reinforcement that you can do whatever you need to do next.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果要说为什么熬过第一个难关是如此艰难，有一个很好的理由，那就是它会为你接下来需要做任何事情提供信心支持。

sentences.en: Yeah. The life you want is on the other side of a few hard conversations and you're living a life you hate because you're too afraid to have them.
sentences.zh: 是的。你想要的生活就在几次艰难对话的另一边，而你过着自己讨厌的生活，是因为你太害怕进行这些对话了。

sentences.en: I think about that a lot because whenever I feel anxious or insecure or angry or sad, I'm like, what conversation do I need to have that I'm not having?
sentences.zh: 我经常这样想，因为每当我感到焦虑、不安、愤怒或悲伤时，我就会想，我需要进行什么我一直没有进行的对话？

sentences.en: And usually if I just think for not that long, I'm like, this is the conversation I've been putting off.
sentences.zh: 通常，如果我稍微思考一下，我就会得出结论：这就是我一直在拖延的对话。

sentences.en: And then, you know, I'm not the poster child of mental health.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道，我也不是心理健康的模范代表。

sentences.en: And so I'll just call myself a pansy for not having the conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以我会直接骂自己是个懦夫，连个对话都不敢进行。

sentences.en: And then I just have it. And so again, I think it's like, I need to have this conversation and the time between when I have it versus when I know I need to have it, when I actually have it, just because it continues to compress.
sentences.zh: 然后我就去面对了。所以再次说明，我觉得这就像是，我需要进行这场对话，而在我明知需要对话、直到真正进行对话之间的这段时间，我一直在不断缩短它。

sentences.en: And if you've ever had like a breakup or an employee firing, one of the, or a quitting, if you're an employee, like these things that you dread.
sentences.zh: 如果你经历过分手、解雇员工，或者作为员工提出辞职，这些都是你会感到畏惧的事情。

sentences.en: I don't know if you notice it, but like the day you do it, the moment after you do it, I'm like, how many other conversations can I have?
sentences.zh: 我不知道你有没有注意到，但就在你做了这件事的那天，就在你完成的那一刻，我甚至在想：我还能进行多少次这样的对话？

sentences.en: Like I want to be like, I'm like, who else do I need to talk to?
sentences.zh: 就像我想说的是，我还得和谁谈谈？

sentences.en: Yeah, totally. Because the day- Becoming a serial killer for awkward conversations.
sentences.zh: 对，完全是这样。因为每一天——简直成了尴尬对话的连环杀手。

sentences.en: When I, so like the next series of hard conversations that I had after I left home was actually like years later.
sentences.zh: 当我离开家之后，经历的下一批艰难对话，其实已经是多年以后了。

sentences.en: So I had, I had multiple partners in, I said, I had a, I had a partner in one of my gyms.
sentences.zh: 当时我有多个合伙人，我说了，我有一个，我在其中一家健身房有一个合伙人。

sentences.en: I had a partner in four other gyms. I had a partner in a chiro and dental marketing agency.
sentences.zh: 我在其他四家健身房有合伙人。我在一家脊椎指压和牙科营销机构也有合伙人。

sentences.en: And all of them relied on me to make money.
sentences.zh: 他们所有人都靠我来赚钱。

sentences.en: And so all of their livelihoods were still dependent on me, but I was splitting everything.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的生计仍然依赖于我，但我却在分润。

sentences.en: And it was horrible for me at the time. And so I remember when I ended up getting in a DUI and I talked to a performance coach or whatever, and he was like, your stress in these conversations could literally kill you.
sentences.zh: 当时对我来说简直太煎熬了。我记得后来我因为酒驾被抓，然后我找了个表现教练之类的咨询，他说：“你由于这些对话而产生的压力，简直会要了你的命。”

sentences.en: He's like, they almost did. So I got in a head-on collision at 60 miles an hour and I walked away, no injuries.
sentences.zh: 他说：“它们差点就要了你的命。”所以我以每小时60英里的速度迎面相撞，却毫发无损地走了出来。

sentences.en: But it was like my wake up call, but not to stop drinking.
sentences.zh: 但这就像是我的警钟，不过不是为了让我戒酒。

sentences.en: It was my wake up call that I needed to have these conversations.
sentences.zh: 而是提醒我必须进行这些对话的警钟。

sentences.en: And that's what I was avoiding when I was drinking.
sentences.zh: 那正是我借酒浇愁时一直在逃避的东西。

sentences.en: It wasn't the alcohol. It was the things that I'm avoiding that I'm using alcohol to get away from.
sentences.zh: 问题根本不在于酒精。而在于我一直在逃避、并试图用酒精来麻痹的事情。

sentences.en: And so the next day I had the first conversation with the first partner and it was horrible.
sentences.zh: 于是第二天，我跟第一个合伙人进行了第一次对话，过程糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: But the moment I was done, I was like, I got to call the other guy.
sentences.zh: 但就在我谈完的那一刻，我在想：我得给另一个人打电话了。

sentences.en: And I called the other one. I was like, this is how it is.
sentences.zh: 然后我打给另外一个合伙人，我说，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is I had this backstop of my death of like, you almost just died because you wouldn't have this conversation.
sentences.zh: 关键在于，我当时把死亡当成了一种后盾，心想，你差点就没命了，就因为你不敢进行这场对话。

sentences.en: And so then it just gave me this courage to just be like, like, and whatever the reaction was, I was like, I'd rather be alive.
sentences.zh: 然后这就给了我勇气，心想，不管对方反应如何，比起死掉，我宁愿选择活着。

sentences.en: Like that was it. And so it's, it's weird though, because death has been this really recurring theme in my life that like the same thing happened when I was like the only thing that gave me enough balls to stand up to my dad, to be fair, from a distance from the car when I was driving halfway across the country, like, let's not make my, let's not make me into too big of a hero here um was the idea that like i started thinking like every day i was like i hope i don't wake up you know what i mean um and that was the that was that was the thing where i was like this is a big enough problem that like if you don't want to wake up then what have you got to lose exactly and that was it and it was like i have nothing to lose and that was when that was when i think in the last podcast we talked about this where it's like if everybody who's like at the bottom and feels like they have nothing going for them, reframe that as I have nothing going for me, which also means that I have nothing to lose by taking action.
sentences.zh: 当时就是这样。这挺奇怪的，因为死亡一直是我生命中一个不断重复的主题，就像我当年……公平地说，虽然只是在开车逃到大半个国家之外、隔着车打电话的时候，才敢有足够的胆量去顶撞我父亲——咱们别把我塑造成什么超级大英雄——但当时的想法是，我开始每天都琢磨，心想，我真希望自己别再醒过来，你知道我的意思吧。正是那种状态让我觉得，这是一个足够严重的问题，如果你连醒都不想醒了，那你还有什么好失去的呢？事实确实如此，当时我就觉得我一无所有，而这也就是我上次在播客里提到过的，如果你处于社会的底层，觉得自己一无所有，那就换个角度想：既然我一无所有，那就意味着我采取行动也根本没有什么好失去的。

sentences.en: It makes you a much more dangerous person.
sentences.zh: 这会让你变成一个非常危险的人。

sentences.en: And I think that was the flip that I've had repeatedly shown to me in my life that allowed me to take the step that I was afraid to take.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这就是我人生中屡次经历的那个转折点，它让我敢于迈出那些我原本畏惧不前的步子。

sentences.en: Have I told you about the region beta paradox?
sentences.zh: 我跟你说过贝塔区域悖论吗？

sentences.en: Have you seen that one? Okay. So this is interesting.
sentences.zh: 你看过那个吗？好吧。这个很有意思。

sentences.en: So imagine that you had to go a mile or less.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，如果你只需要走一英里或者更短的距离。

sentences.en: And if you did... A mile? A mile. Okay. If you had to travel a mile or less, you would... walk it.
sentences.zh: 如果你要走……一英里？一英里。好吧。如果你需要移动一英里或者更短的距离，你会选择走路。

sentences.en: And if you had to go more than a mile, you would drive it.
sentences.zh: 而如果你要去的地方超过一英里，你就会开车。

sentences.en: So paradoxically, you would go two miles quicker than you would go one mile.
sentences.zh: 所以反常的是，你走两英里所花的时间，反而会比走一英里还要快。

sentences.en: If you follow that rule, the important insight here is that if you only take action when things cross a certain threshold of badness, sometimes better things can feel worse than worse things.
sentences.zh: 如果你遵循那个规则，这里重要的洞察在于，如果你只在事情糟糕到某个特定阈值时才采取行动，有时候，更好的处境反而会感觉比更糟的处境还要糟糕。

sentences.en: So if you look around and you see that people are stuck in region beta, this zone of comfortable complacency, right it's the guy that sticks in his just okay job because his boss isn't too much of a dick but the pay isn't that good and he's not really that passionate but it's all right whatever whatever the person that stays in the acceptable relationship they're not that fired up but they're not really in love and their partner's not really got much alignment with their interests or the person that stays in a crappy apartment and there's a bit of mold in the ceiling but it's cheap and it's in a good area of town or whatever all of these people would be better off if their situations were worse because it would give them the activation energy to kick them out of the bottom and that only regret would be not doing it sooner dude i love that when i see it's funny because if i look back on the instances that were the most painful in my life every single one of them without fail has created a disproportionate gain right like the most painful thing early on was for me was quitting my job and leaving, you know, leaving my dad, basically.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你环顾四周，就会发现人们陷入了贝塔区域，也就是那种舒适的自满区，对吧？就像那种死守着一份马马虎虎的工作的人，因为老板不算太混蛋，但工资也没那么高，他其实也没什么热情，不过也就将就了，随便怎样都行；或者是那种维持着一段食之无味、弃之可惜的亲密关系的人，他们对彼此没有多少激情，也没有坠入爱河，伴侣和他们的兴趣也根本不在一个频道上；或者是一个住在破旧公寓里的人，天花板上甚至有点霉菌，但房租便宜，而且地段在城里还算不错，诸如此类。所有这些人，如果他们的处境能再糟糕一点，其实反而对他们更好，因为那能给他们提供激活能量，把他们从谷底踢出去，而他们唯一的遗憾就是没有早点这么做。老兄，我太喜欢这个观点了。说来也搞笑，如果我回想自己人生中最痛苦的那些时刻，每一个无一例外都带来了不成比例的巨大收获，对吧？比如我早期经历的最痛苦的事，就是辞职并离开，你知道的，基本上就是离开我父亲。

sentences.en: And then that created the, you know, my first, my first business and the gyms and all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 然后那促成了，你知道的，我的第一家公司、健身房以及所有那些业务。

sentences.en: Um, you know, getting into the DUI, the head on collision.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道的，比如卷入酒驾案，还出了正面相撞的车祸。

sentences.en: Um, and like that whole situation got me out of all of these failed partnerships that I wasn't willing to do.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而整件事情让我彻底摆脱了那些我原本不敢主动退出的失败合伙关系。

sentences.en: But in the, in the moment I was like, I'm such a failure.
sentences.zh: 但在当时那一刻，我心想：我真是个十足的失败者。

sentences.en: Like I suck at everything, but that gave me the springboard.
sentences.zh: 就像我对什么都一窍不通，但那却为我提供了跳板。

sentences.en: When I lost everything the first time after that, that then gave me the idea that I needed to change the business model around.
sentences.zh: 在那之后我第一次失去了一切，正是那次经历让我意识到，我必须彻底改变商业模式。

sentences.en: And that's what switched me into the licensing model.
sentences.zh: 正是这个转变让我走向了授权经营的模式。

sentences.en: And then that became the first real fortune.
sentences.zh: 然后这成为了第一笔真正的财富。

sentences.en: This is kind of like alchemy. Yeah. Like turning something which is worse than useless into something that's as precious and useful as possible.
sentences.zh: 这有点像炼金术。是的。就像把比没用还糟的东西，变成尽可能珍贵和有用的东西一样。

sentences.en: I'm sure you know the parable of the man and his son.
sentences.zh: 我敢说你知道塞翁失马的故事。

sentences.en: And then he like buys the son a horse and then it falls and he breaks the leg.
sentences.zh: 然后他给儿子买了一匹马，结果马摔断了腿。

sentences.en: And then they're like, oh, it's so sad. And then the army comes, then the son doesn't die.
sentences.zh: 然后大家就说，哇，太惨了。接着军队来了，儿子因此不用去参军。

sentences.en: And then it's like, oh, it's so great. Right.
sentences.zh: 然后大家又说，哇，太棒了。对吧。

sentences.en: And so it's one of those really interesting ones where like whatever negative situation, and this is probably good for the audience, but like, if you think back to all the negative situations, you had like the really, really bad ones.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常有趣的情况，无论遇到什么负面情况——这对观众可能很有启发——如果你回想所有那些负面情况，尤其是那些非常非常糟糕的。

sentences.en: When you expand the time horizon, most times they become net wins.
sentences.zh: 当你把时间线拉长，大多数时候它们最终都成了净收益。

sentences.en: And so then it just means that like, if you're in a really tough time right now, you just got to wait. and then you get, and then you'll get your reference point back on all the things that changed as a result.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，如果你现在正经历一段非常艰难的时期，你只需要坚持下去。然后你就会，你会从所有因此而改变的事情中重新找到参照系。

sentences.en: Because most times when shit is bad, it can't get worse.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数时候，当情况糟透了的时候，它也没法再坏了。

sentences.en: So then you feel like, well, it can't get worse than this.
sentences.zh: 所以你会觉得，嗯，不会比这更糟了。

sentences.en: And then your action threshold decreases and you take, and you do all the things you know you should have done anyways.
sentences.zh: 然后你的行动门槛就会降低，你会采取行动，把那些你早就知道自己该做的事情全都做了。

sentences.en: And so it's like, we have this big stack of should do's and we just wait until it's two miles.
sentences.zh: 所以这就好像，我们有一大堆该做却没做的事，我们就一直拖着，直到堆得有两英里高。

sentences.en: And then you just, you're like, you just get like the firing conversation.
sentences.zh: 然后你会突然，就像经历了一场解雇员工的谈话。

sentences.en: And you're like, well, I just fired one person or like, I just ended one partnership.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，好吧，我刚刚开除一个人，或者我刚刚结束一段合作关系。

sentences.en: I just broke up with one girl or whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚跟一个女孩分手了，或者诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And you're like, who else do I need to talk to today?
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，今天我还需要找谁谈谈？

sentences.en: And then in like a period of like, you have these rapid periods of growth that happen.
sentences.zh: 接着在一段时间内，你会经历一段快速增长期。

sentences.en: And then you have the next web of comfort because it's way better than you were before.
sentences.zh: 然后你会进入下一个舒适区，因为这比你之前的状况好太多了。

sentences.en: And I think it's, I wonder, this is more just like an open thought, but like, I wonder how long like more successful people stay in that next plateau.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这其实只是一个开放式的想法，我在想那些更成功的人会在下一个平台期停留多久。

sentences.en: Like, I wonder if their threshold for- Action stays low.
sentences.zh: 比如，我很好奇他们对——行动的门槛是不是一直很低。

sentences.en: Yeah. They're like, I'm getting comfortable, like how quickly they get comfortable into like, I need to change, I need to get better.
sentences.zh: 对。他们会觉得，我开始变得安于现状了，他们能以多快的速度察觉到这种舒适，并意识到“我需要改变，我需要变得更好”。

sentences.en: Next one. The heaviest things in life aren't iron and gold, but unmade decisions.
sentences.zh: 下一个。生活中最重的负担不是铁块和黄金，而是未做出的决定。

sentences.en: The reason you are stressed is that you have decisions to make and you're not making them.
sentences.zh: 你感到压力是因为你有决定要做出却迟迟不做。

sentences.en: It's a good quote. You said it. You said it.
sentences.zh: 这是一句好名言。你说的。这是你说的。

sentences.en: I think a lot of times the decisions that we make are predicated on the conversations we need to have.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很多时候我们做出的决定，都取决于我们需要进行的关键对话。

sentences.en: Because usually like that, and what's interesting is like, you can define commitment by eliminating alternatives.
sentences.zh: 因为通常像那样，有趣的是，你可以通过排除其他选项来定义承诺。

sentences.en: So if you're committed, you've eliminated alternative actions.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你是坚定的，你就已经排除了其他行动选项。

sentences.en: Right? Like you can say I'm committed, but until you eliminate other options, you're not committed.
sentences.zh: 对吧？你可以说我很坚定，但在你排除其他选择之前，你根本算不上坚定。

sentences.en: There's always a get out of jail free. Right.
sentences.zh: 总留有一条脱身退路的后路。对吧。

sentences.en: And so a lot of people make decisions to end relationships, to quit their job, to start the new thing, but they don't become committed to the decision until they remove the other options.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人做出了结束关系、辞职、开始新事业的决定，但直到他们切断了其他选择，他们才真正对这个决定做出了承诺。

sentences.en: And then you're forced to take action on it.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会被迫为此采取行动。

sentences.en: And so I think actually defining those two, two different things.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为实际上应该区分这两个不同的概念。

sentences.en: Now you could define, you know, decision is to kill off like dicadere from Latin, but from a, from an, from a colloquial thing, I think there are two different instances.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以给“决定”下定义，比如源自拉丁语的“杀死”（dicadere），但从通俗的角度来看，我认为这是两个不同的阶段。

sentences.en: It's like, I need to change this. And then I do change it.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我需要改变现状。然后我真的去改变了它。

sentences.en: Um, and the making the decision is when it becomes a commitment.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而做出决定的那一刻，它才真正变成了一种承诺。

sentences.en: Why are unmade decisions so heavy? I think, at least for me, it's because I have this hamster wheel on the back of my mind where I keep playing out different scenarios.
sentences.zh: 为什么未做出的决定会这么沉重？我想，至少对我来说，是因为我的脑海里一直有个仓鼠轮在转个不停，我不断地在脑海中模拟不同的情景。

sentences.en: And so I keep thinking like, well, maybe I need to change what I'm currently doing.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是在想，嗯，也许我需要改变我目前正在做的事。

sentences.en: Maybe if I just rethought, like, because I'm a big frame guy.
sentences.zh: 也许我只要重新构思一下，因为我很注重思维框架。

sentences.en: So I'm like, maybe I just need to be thinking about this differently, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我就想，也许我只是需要换个角度来思考这个问题，对吧？

sentences.en: Maybe if I zoom all the way out, the earth doesn't exist.
sentences.zh: 也许当我把视野拉到最远，地球根本就不存在。

sentences.en: So maybe this doesn't matter. Or maybe I'm just making a problem that doesn't exist.
sentences.zh: 所以也许这根本不重要。或者也许我只是在无中生有。

sentences.en: Maybe the best action I should take is nothing, right?
sentences.zh: 也许我应该采取的最佳行动就是什么都不做，对吧？

sentences.en: Like I reframe all those things. but usually it's just because I'm afraid of something and then that's why I'm not making the decision and I think once I name and put a face and it's usually not even a thing that I'm afraid of it's one person's judgment I'm afraid of and then when I name the person then it becomes then it becomes real instead of being this amorphous like people society judgment it's like Tom like do I really care what Tom thinks I guess so it seems like I'm not making this big change my life because of Tom.
sentences.zh: 就像我重新构架所有这些事情一样，但通常这只是因为我害怕某些东西，这就是我迟迟不做决定的原因。我觉得一旦我把它叫出名并给它画个像——通常这甚至不是我害怕的事物本身，而是我害怕某个人的评判——然后当我指名道姓说出那个人是谁时，它就变得真实了，不再是那种模糊不清的人群、社会评判。就像Tom一样，我真的在意Tom怎么想吗？我想是的，看起来我之所以没有在生活中做出这个重大的改变，竟然是因为Tom。

sentences.en: Looks like Tom's more in control of my life than I am.
sentences.zh: 看起来Tom比我更能掌控我的人生。

sentences.en: Dude. So I remember this. When I was 19 years old, I was super angry, like all 19-year-old men, right?
sentences.zh: 老兄。所以我记得这个。当我19岁的时候，我超级愤怒，就像所有19岁的年轻男人一样，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the standard default, right? I was angry at both my parents because I was 19, right?
sentences.zh: 那是标准的默认状态，对吧？我对我爸妈都充满愤怒，因为我当时19岁，对吧？

sentences.en: And I remember blaming them for everything, blaming them for my life, blaming them for not being a better person.
sentences.zh: 我记得把一切都怪罪在他们头上，责怪他们毁了我的生活，责怪他们没让我成为一个更好的人。

sentences.en: I literally blamed them for being a bad person. and I remember realizing that when I blamed them that I gave them control over my life and then the idea that the people that I hated the most at the time were the ones who actually were controlling me was the thing that most sickened me to then actually flip my narrative to actually taking control like that was the one thought process like my mother I'm giving her control over my romantic relate like my mother controls this fuck that i was like no and so like just the idea that somebody who i was disgusted by at the time um had that much power is what gave me the power to start taking action so this hamster wheel thing that continues to distract you i've got this concept called anxiety cost so kind of like opportunity cost yeah um when you have an unmade decision, every single second that you spend thinking about the unmade decision could have been gotten back had you just made the decision.
sentences.zh: 我甚至直接责怪他们让我成了一个糟糕的人。我记得当时我意识到，当我责怪他们的时候，我实际上把主导我人生的权力交给了他们。一想到我当时最痛恨的人竟然在实际控制着我，这种想法让我感到最恶心，于是我彻底扭转了叙事，开始真正掌控自己。这就是当时的整个心路历程——比如我母亲，我竟然把我在恋爱关系上的控制权交给了她……比如我母亲居然能控制这个？去他的，我当时想：门儿都没有！所以，仅仅是一想到一个我当时极其鄙视的人竟然拥有那么大的权力，这种屈辱感就给了我采取行动的力量。因此，这个一直在分你精力的“仓鼠轮”问题，我有一个概念叫作“焦虑成本”——有点类似于机会成本，对吧？嗯……当你有一个悬而未决的决定时，你花在纠结这个未做决定的每一秒钟，如果你早点把决定做了，这些时间本可以白白省回来。

sentences.en: And realizing that it's a justification for eating frogs earlier in the day.
sentences.zh: 并且意识到这只是你在白天拖延、逃避困难任务的借口。

sentences.en: I need to answer that email. The longer that you wait until you answer that email, the more times you will think the thought, I need to answer that email.
sentences.zh: 我需要回那个邮件。你拖延回邮件的时间越长，你脑子里就会反复蹦出这句话：“我需要回那个邮件。”

sentences.en: And if we assume that what truly, truly matters in life is the time and the attention that we spend within that time, your time is being captured and your attention is being captured by a thought that could have been gotten rid of had you have just done it.
sentences.zh: 如果我们认为人生中真正、真正重要的是我们在其中投入的时间和注意力，那么你的时间和注意力就被这样一个念头给劫持了——如果你当时直接把事办了，这个念头本可以彻底消失。

sentences.en: Had you have just had the conversation, broken up with the relationship, left the job, told the father, whatever. done your stretches, cleaned your teeth, had a shower, whatever it is that you needed to do, all of that anxiety cost could have been gotten rid of had you just gone and done it.
sentences.zh: 只要你把话说开了、把恋爱谈分了、把工作辞了、跟父亲摊牌了，不管是什么事。做完你的拉伸、刷了牙、洗了澡，无论你需要做的是什么，只要你直接去把它们做完，所有这些焦虑成本本都可以烟消云散。

sentences.en: You can move through life at seven times the rate of other people by simply changing when you say you're going to make a decision from end of week to end of day.
sentences.zh: 你可以通过简单地把做决定的时间从“周末”提前到“当天”，以普通人七倍的速度经历你的人生。

sentences.en: So think about how that stacks up. So it's like, let's say that there were four decisions that you needed to make.
sentences.zh: 所以想想这积累起来有多夸张。假设有四个决定需要你去做。

sentences.en: If the normal person takes a week to make the decision and then their mind moves on to the next thing that they have anxiety for and start making that decision and decide another week, decide another week, decide another week.
sentences.zh: 如果普通人花一週时间才做一个决定，然后他们的脑子转去想下一个让他们焦虑的事情，开始纠结那个决定，又花一週做决定，再花一週，再花一週。

sentences.en: It's a month to make those four decisions.
sentences.zh: 光是做出这四个决定就要花上一个月。

sentences.en: Whereas the super, the Superman that takes one decision day one, second decision day two, third decision day three, fourth decision day four, they aren't even finished the week yet and they're where the other person is at the end of the month.
sentences.zh: 然而那个超级赛亚人，第一天做一个决定，第二天第二个决定，第三天第三个决定，第四天第四个决定，他们甚至连这一周都还没过完，就已经达到了别人过了一个月的状态。

sentences.en: And like that speed of decision-making, like not paying the attention cost, the opportunity cost of your time, I think it's really profound in terms of how quickly people move through life in terms of achieving the goals that they set out.
sentences.zh: 这种做决定的速度，就像是不在时间上支付注意力成本和机会成本一样，我认为这对于人们在实现自己设定的目标时推进人生速度的影响是极其深远的。

sentences.en: Because people are like, how is that guy so young and he's achieved X, Y, and Z?
sentences.zh: 因为人们总会问：为什么那家伙那么年轻就能达成X、Y、Z成就？

sentences.en: It's like, well, what takes you a month to make a decision, we make it an hour.
sentences.zh: 答案就是：好吧，你花一个月才能做出的决定，我们一个小时就做完了。

sentences.en: And then the next hour, I make another decision that takes you your next month.
sentences.zh: 然后在接下来的一个小时里，我做出另一个足以耗费你接下来一个月的决定。

sentences.en: And so that's how you can go 30 times or 100 times faster than the quote average person who's overweight, has $1,000 in their bank account, and is going to die at 70.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你可以比那个大腹便便、银行账户里只有1000美元、打算在70岁死去的所谓普通人快30倍甚至100倍。

sentences.en: Can you just go back to before you made that first decision with your dad?
sentences.zh: 你能回到你跟你爸做出第一个决定之前的那个状态吗？

sentences.en: Because you've mentioned it, people might look at your, I would say ruthlessness, at least in some regards with decision-making, hiring and firing and making these business decisions.
sentences.zh: 因为你提到过这一点，人们可能会看到你的这种“冷酷无情”——至少在某种程度上，比如在做决定、雇人、炒人和做这些商业决策时表现出的冷酷。

sentences.en: And there's all of these great stories about, and I had this thing and I realized that partner wasn't right.
sentences.zh: 而且有很多关于这方面的精彩故事，比如我遇到了某事，然后我意识到那个合伙人不对劲。

sentences.en: So I got rid of that business. And that's the sort of thing that would tear most people up for six months, 18 months, maybe forever.
sentences.zh: 于是我直接把那个业务给甩了。这种事对大多数人来说可能会让他们纠结六个月、十八个月，甚至一辈子。

sentences.en: And to look at that degree of cutthroatness or at least decisiveness, I think is almost unfathomable for a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 而看到这种程度的冷酷无情，或者至少是果断，对很多人来说简直是不可思议的。

sentences.en: Are you a representative avatar? Is pre-leaving Baltimore Alex a representative avatar for the average person?
sentences.zh: 你是一个具有代表性的典型人物吗？离开巴尔的摩之前的Alex，对于普通人来说是一个有代表性的缩影吗？

sentences.en: I think so. I mean, I was high achieving.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。我的意思是，我曾经是个高成就追求者。

sentences.en: I did well in school. I tried hard. I did those things. but in terms of my risk tolerance and my fear of failure and my insecurities, yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 我在学校表现很好。我付出了努力。我做了那些事情。但就我的风险承受能力、对失败的恐惧以及我的不安全感而言，绝对是的。

sentences.en: I mean, if anything, real talk, I'll bet you that I have more insecurities than most people because those insecurities are what drove me to do well in those things.
sentences.zh: 甚至不如说，说句实在话，我敢打赌我的不安全感比大多数人都要强烈，因为正是这些不安全感驱使我在这些事情上做出了成绩。

sentences.en: Not because I cared about school, but because I cared about what other people thought about me.
sentences.zh: 不是因为我在乎学校本身，而是因为我在乎别人是怎么看我的。

sentences.en: Yeah. Yeah. I've spoken to hundreds and hundreds of high performers.
sentences.zh: 对，确实。我跟成百上千的高绩效人士交流过。

sentences.en: On balance, people are driven way more by fear of insufficiency than they are with some well-balanced, perfect desire to just maximize their greatness in life.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，驱使人们前进的动力，与其说是某种对实现人生伟大意义的平衡、完美的渴望，不如说是对自身能力不足的恐惧。

sentences.en: Like the activation energy for almost everybody is, I'm scared I might be a piece of shit.
sentences.zh: 对几乎所有人来说，启动能量都是：“我害怕自己可能其实是个彻头彻尾的废物。”

sentences.en: What? Hang on. Oh God, I might be a piece of shit.
sentences.zh: 什么？等一下。哦天哪，我可能就是个废物。

sentences.en: I genuinely might be a piece of shit. I need to go and do something so outrageous that I can't be a piece of shit.
sentences.zh: 我发自内心地觉得自己可能就是个废物。我必须去做一些惊天动地的大事，这样我就不可能是个废物了。

sentences.en: There's no way that it could happen. I might be a coward.
sentences.zh: 绝对不能让这种事发生。我可能只是个懦夫。

sentences.en: Oh my God, what can I do to stop myself from being a coward? that's the activation energy it's funny because if you regress fear to its most basic form it's death and death is the greatest motivator and like you can prove it in a simple example it's like if i all of a sudden go up to anybody on the street and i put a gun in their head and i say you know point a gun at their head and i say go do this thing they'll go do it but if i say you can have anything you want if you do this they're willing to go 10 times harder with a gun in their face to not die.
sentences.zh: 我的天哪，我能做些什么来阻止自己成为一个懦夫呢？这就是激活能，这很有趣，因为如果你把恐惧追溯到它最基本的形态，那就是死亡，而死亡是最大的动力，就像你可以通过一个简单的例子证明的那样，如果我突然走到街上的任何人面前，用枪顶着他们的头，你知道的，用枪指着他们的头，然后说，去把这件事做了，他们就会去做；但如果我说，你做这个就能得到你想要的一切，他们更愿意面对顶着脑门儿的枪去拼命，以避免死亡。

sentences.en: And so if you take fear and regress it all the way down to its basis form, like that's what the insecurity is.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你把恐惧一直追溯到它的基本形态，那这就是不安全感的本质。

sentences.en: Like if they, they think I won't be enough.
sentences.zh: 就像他们，他们认为我做得还不够好。

sentences.en: And if they don't think I won't be enough, then this won't happen.
sentences.zh: 如果他们不觉得我做得不够好，那这事就不会发生。

sentences.en: If this won't happen, this won't happen.
sentences.zh: 如果这事不发生，那事就不会发生。

sentences.en: I'll be alone. I'll be dead. But like, if you just regress it all the way down, that's all it is.
sentences.zh: 我会孤单一人。我会死。但如果你一直追溯到底，事情就是这样。

sentences.en: And so like. the biggest achievers in life, I think, have most directly tied them not doing whatever it is that they want to do to death, whether they're consciously aware of it or not.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，生活中最成功的人，无论他们是否有意识地意识到，他们都把不敢做自己想做的事与死亡直接联系在了一起。

sentences.en: And then that's what motivates them harder.
sentences.zh: 然后这就成了他们更努力的动力。

sentences.en: We'll get back to talking to Alex in one minute, but first I need to tell you about Element.
sentences.zh: 我们会在一分钟内继续和 Alex 聊，但首先我需要向你介绍一下 Element。

sentences.en: Element is that they're not afraid of failing.
sentences.zh: Element 就是他们不怕失败。

sentences.en: You're afraid of what other people will think of you if you fail.
sentences.zh: 你害怕的是如果失败了别人会怎么看你。

sentences.en: But if you're afraid of that, imagine what they think of you when you aren't even trying.
sentences.zh: 但如果你害怕这个，想想看当你甚至连试都不试的时候，他们是怎么看你的。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, they aren't. i'm such a dick sometimes um does it is it is it strange to hear your like angry toilet tweets read back to you now in the cold harsh light of day god that was a particularly difficult poo i was cracking right there you know real talk the the tweets that i have people don't know this but the tweets are notes to self yeah so they're just directed at me so that i can look back on them and like be reminders of like, hey, don't do that.
sentences.zh: 哦对，他们根本没看。有时候我真像个混蛋，呃，现在在冷酷严苛的现实光线下回听你那些像是在厕所里发出的愤怒推文，会不会觉得有点奇怪？天哪，那真是一次特别艰难的便秘，我当时简直要崩溃了，你知道的，说真的，我发的那些推文，人们并不知道，但这些推文其实是写给自己的备忘录，是的，所以它们只针对我自己，好让我能回过头来看看它们，就像是提醒自己，嘿，别那么干。

sentences.en: And so like, I think to myself, man, I'm afraid of doing this.
sentences.zh: 所以我在想，天哪，我害怕做这个。

sentences.en: And I'm like, no, I'm not. I'm afraid of what this person's going to think about me.
sentences.zh: 然后我觉得，不，我不是。我害怕这个人会怎么看我。

sentences.en: Because if I were to be able to fail in quiet, in complete isolation, then I wouldn't care.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我能在安静、完全隔离的环境下失败，我就根本不在乎了。

sentences.en: And then I think, well, what if I don't succeed in public?
sentences.zh: 然后我在想，好吧，如果我在大庭广众之下没有成功呢？

sentences.en: What do they think then? Nothing, right?
sentences.zh: 那他们会怎么想？什么都不想，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't think about me at all. And so obviously that comes from the perspective of seeking to gain approval and attention from others anyway.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不会想到我。所以很明显，这无论如何都是出于寻求他人认可和关注的角度。

sentences.en: So it's like, listen, if you're insecure, which everybody is, let's be real, you might as well use the insecurity to get something out of it.
sentences.zh: 所以就像是，听着，如果你缺乏安全感，而每个人都这样，说实话，你不如利用这种不安全感从中捞点好处。

sentences.en: Right? Like one of my favorite things about entrepreneurship is like, use what you've got.
sentences.zh: 对吧？就像我最喜欢创业的一点是，利用你现有的东西。

sentences.en: And so a lot of people think that they need to fix their conditions in order to get like the perfect conditions before they start.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得他们需要先修复自己的条件，在开始之前弄到完美条件。

sentences.en: But the perfect condition is whatever one you're in, because it gives you whatever assets you have, that's the cards that you're dealt.
sentences.zh: 但完美的条件就是你现在所在的那个，因为它给了你你所拥有的任何资产，这就是你拿到手的牌。

sentences.en: And so you just play the hand. And a lot of people have great cards.
sentences.zh: 所以你只要打好这手牌就行。而且很多人都有一手好牌。

sentences.en: It's like, man, I'm so afraid of, it's like, use it.
sentences.zh: 就像是，天哪，我太害怕了，这就好像是，利用它。

sentences.en: It's like, I have nothing. What makes you very dangerous?
sentences.zh: 就像是，我一无所有。是什么让你变得非常危险？

sentences.en: Because you have nothing to lose. One of the really interesting things about, I think about from a business perspective, but it probably applies to everything, is that there's always an advantage and a disadvantage from every position.
sentences.zh: 因为你没有什么可失去的。我觉得从商业角度来看，有一件非常有趣的事，虽然它可能适用于所有事情，那就是无论处于什么位置，总有优势和劣势。

sentences.en: I remember when, I mean, Gym Launch is still a big company and still continues to grow, but in the gym licensing space, there's not many people who can compete with us there.
sentences.zh: 我记得当，我是说 Gym Launch 仍然是一家大公司，并且还在继续发展，但在健身房特许经营领域，没有多少人能与我们竞争。

sentences.en: I would talk to guys who are in the space.
sentences.zh: 我会和业内的人聊天。

sentences.en: I would talk at a conference, whatever, and younger guys would be like, well, I want to be in this space too, and it's not fair because you have this big advantage.
sentences.zh: 我在会议上发言什么的，年轻的小伙子们就会说，我也想进这个领域，这不公平，因为你们有这么大的优势。

sentences.en: And I was like, you have a way bigger advantage than I do.
sentences.zh: 而我会说，你们比我有着更大的优势。

sentences.en: And I was like, because if I were in your position, I would go to every single gym owner and be like, you don't want to be with Jim Launch.
sentences.zh: 我会说，因为如果我在你的位置，我会去找每一个健身房老板，然后说，你可不想跟 Gym Launch 合作。

sentences.en: You don't want to be with Alex. You're just a number to him.
sentences.zh: 你可不想跟 Alex 合作。对他来说你只是个数字。

sentences.en: You're never going to talk to him. You're just a cog in the wheel there.
sentences.zh: 你永远都不会跟他说话。你在那儿只是个微不足道的齿轮。

sentences.en: With me, you're going to get my personalized attention there.
sentences.zh: 而跟我合作，你会得到我个性化的关注。

sentences.en: It's just some employee down the chain that's following some process.
sentences.zh: 那边不过是顺着流程走的一群底层员工罢了。

sentences.en: I was like, but on the flip side, if I'm talking to that same gym owner, then I'm going to say, you don't want to talk to Jimmy.
sentences.zh: 我接着说，但反过来，如果我跟同一个健身房老板谈话，我就会说，你可不想跟 Jimmy 谈。

sentences.en: He lives in his mom's basement. He has no proof that he's good at what he's at.
sentences.zh: 他住在妈妈的地下室里。他没有任何证据证明他擅长自己做的事。

sentences.en: The reason that we're number one in the space is because we've done it so many times and we have a system that we know that if you go on this side, you will get this result on the outside.
sentences.zh: 我们在业内能排第一，是因为我们做过无数次，而且我们有一套系统，我们深知如果你选这边，最终就会得到这个结果。

sentences.en: I was like, there's always a position and there's always an advantage.
sentences.zh: 我当时就觉得，永远都有一个位置，也永远都有一个优势。

sentences.en: I was like, you just have to play the one you've got.
sentences.zh: 我就觉得，你只能打手里现有的牌。

sentences.en: And most people just look at what everyone else's advantages and don't think, which one do I have?
sentences.zh: 而大多数人只是看着别人的优势，却从不想想，我自己有什么优势？

sentences.en: When you're talking about, it's not you that's afraid of failing.
sentences.zh: 当你在纠结时，其实并不是你害怕失败。

sentences.en: You're afraid of other people's opinions about why you're going to fail.
sentences.zh: 你害怕的是别人对你为什么会失败的看法。

sentences.en: Like the reason I think that cynicism is so popular on the internet is that the upside of never trying is never having to feel the pain of failure.
sentences.zh: 就像我觉得网上为什么愤世嫉俗这么流行，因为不尝试的好处就是永远不用体验失败的痛苦。

sentences.en: That's fundamental. It's sour grapes at an existential level, right?
sentences.zh: 这很根本。这是一种存在主义层面的吃不到葡萄说葡萄酸，对吧？

sentences.en: It is a cynicism safety blanket. It is protecting you from ever having to feel the downside of anything.
sentences.zh: 这是一种愤世嫉俗的安全毯。它保护你免于承受任何事情的负面结果。

sentences.en: I will assure my own failure in private so that I never have to face my failure in public.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿私底下确保自己失败，这样就永远不用在大庭广众之下直面失败。

sentences.en: It's kind of like investing. Everyone's afraid of losing money when they invest, but the only guaranteed investment that doesn't work is never investing to begin with.
sentences.zh: 这有点像投资。每个人投资时都怕亏钱，但唯一注定失败的投资，就是从一开始就根本不投资。

sentences.en: And so it's like they take the long failure rather than the short one.
sentences.zh: 所以他们宁愿选择长痛，也不愿短痛。

sentences.en: Right. I mean, it's what it is, right? You just fail long.
sentences.zh: 对吧。我的意思是，事实就是如此，对吧？你只是在慢慢地失败。

sentences.en: And they're like, I prefer that. But that's, I mean, that's, yeah, it's, it's like you and I are going back and forth on trying to figure out how many different ways can I say that either the people that you're worried about judgment are going to die or that you're going to die, or that even if you do achieve the thing, they won't care anyways.
sentences.zh: 他们会说，我更喜欢这样。但那，我是说，那，对吧，这，这就好比你我在讨论，我究竟能用多少种不同的方式来表达——要么是那些你担心会对你评头论足的人会死，要么是你自己会死，或者就算你真的成功了，他们其实也根本不在乎。

sentences.en: Or if you don't do anything, they won't think about you to begin with.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你什么都不做，他们一开始就不会想到你。

sentences.en: And don't you want to be thought about to begin with?
sentences.zh: 难道你从一开始就不想被人惦记吗？

sentences.en: Like, don't you want some level of significance, I just, you're going to die.
sentences.zh: 比如，难道你不想获得某种程度的认可吗？我只是说，你终究会死。

sentences.en: And I think like, I was very grateful. So one of my biggest inspirations or whatever, you know, influences when I was in Baltimore was I would have lunch with my grandfather three times a week.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得，我很感激。我在巴尔的摩时，我最大的灵感来源之一，或者说对我影响很大的人，是我每周有三天会跟我爷爷一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: So he was 90, old guy. So I'll go to the nursing home and we'd have lunch three days a week.
sentences.zh: 他当时90岁了，是个老头。所以我去疗养院，我们一周有三天一起吃午饭。

sentences.en: And listening to him talk about the regrets that you had in life.
sentences.zh: 听他谈论他在生活中曾有过的那些遗憾。

sentences.en: It's so much more painful to watch someone who has no options left.
sentences.zh: 看着一个走投无路的人，那种感觉痛苦得多。

sentences.en: Like he's going to die. I mean, he's going to die tomorrow and he died a couple of years later.
sentences.zh: 就像他快要死了。我是说，他明天就要死了，而且他几年后确实去世了。

sentences.en: I mean, like, and he lost all his mental faculties, you know, almost sadly, basically when I stopped, when I left Baltimore, one of the sad parts is I was one of the only people that kind of like kept him lucid.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，而且他失去了所有的心智能力，你知道的，甚至有点悲哀的是，基本上自我离开巴尔的摩后，令人难过的一点是，我是少数几个能让他保持清醒的人之一。

sentences.en: You know what I mean? And after that, no one really, no one really visited him.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？在那之后，真的没有人，真的没有人去看望他。

sentences.en: No one really did anything. And so I think he, he just rolled downhill.
sentences.zh: 真的没有人做任何事。所以我觉得他，他只是情况越来越糟。

sentences.en: I think the lunches might've been the only thing that he looked forward to.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这些午饭可能是他唯一期盼的事情了。

sentences.en: And seeing someone old with no options and nothing but regret, not that he had everything to regret, he had things that he did really well.
sentences.zh: 看着一个老年人，走投无路，只剩下遗憾——倒不是说他有什么好后悔的，他也有做得非常出色的事情。

sentences.en: And I took those things from him.
sentences.zh: 我从他身上继承了那些东西。

sentences.en: He would repeat the same lessons. Like every lunch, there's a lot of older people kind of repeat a few key lessons.
sentences.zh: 他总是重复同样的教导。就像每次吃午饭时，很多老年人都会重复一些关键的教训。

sentences.en: And everything that he had, he fled during the World World War II.
sentences.zh: 他拥有的所有东西，都在二战期间逃难时丢了。

sentences.en: You know, he fled from the Germans and all that stuff because he had a Jewish sounding last name.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他为了躲避德国人逃跑之类的，因为他有一个听起来像犹太人的姓氏。

sentences.en: He wasn't, but it was enough that he was fleeing, right?
sentences.zh: 他其实不是，但这就足够让他踏上逃亡之路了，对吧？

sentences.en: And he always used to say, he's like, you have two hands and one brain.
sentences.zh: 他总是说，他会说，你长了两只手和一个大脑。

sentences.en: I was like, use them. And that was always this thing that he said to me.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，那就用它们。他总是跟我说这句话。

sentences.en: And I think just like when I would think about the things that he was going up against compared to the things that we're going up against now, it just made me feel like, all right, like this is not as big of a deal as I really think it is.
sentences.zh: 我觉得每当我把他的遭遇和我们现在面临的遭遇做对比时，就会觉得，好吧，这其实没我想象的那么大不了。

sentences.en: I don't have Germans at the, at my door.
sentences.zh: 我的门外又没有德国鬼子。

sentences.en: What were the regrets that you had? Him?
sentences.zh: 他都有什么遗憾？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He would have spent, I mean, again, there's deathbed regrets and then there's real life regrets, but there's things that he would have done differently in terms of the business.
sentences.zh: 他本可以，我是说，话说回来，临终前的遗憾是一回事，现实生活中的遗憾是另一回事，但有些事他在生意上本可以做得不一样。

sentences.en: There's things he would have done differently with his wife.
sentences.zh: 有些事他跟妻子本可以处理得不同。

sentences.en: He got divorced.
sentences.zh: 他离婚了。

sentences.en: He would have done things very differently with his kids, so my mother and her sisters, which actually talking to him about how he raised my mother helped me in some way forgive her for some of the things that I felt were wrongdoings that she had done to me.
sentences.zh: 他对待孩子的方式本可以有很大不同，也就是我母亲和她的姐妹们。事实上，跟他聊聊他是怎么抚养我母亲的，在某种程度上帮我原谅了她，原谅了那些我曾觉得是对我做过的错事。

sentences.en: And so it's funny because, you know, one of my favorite quotes from Blaise Pascal is to understand is to forgive.
sentences.zh: 所以这很有趣，你知道的，我最喜欢布莱士·帕斯卡的一句名言是：去理解就是去原谅。

sentences.en: And like when you, when you, I think there's another saying that I like a lot, which is it's really hard to hate close up.
sentences.zh: 就像当你在，我觉得还有一句我很喜欢的名言，那就是：深入了解之后，你真的很难再去恨一个人。

sentences.en: It's like, if you really see someone and you see all the things that they went through and the things that they, that happened to them to become who they are, then you understand them.
sentences.zh: 这就好比，如果你真正地去看一个人，看到他们经历过的一切，看到他们遭遇过的事，正是这些造就了今天的他们，那你就会理解他们。

sentences.en: And then you understand why they did X, Y, and Z.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会明白他们为什么会做出这样那样的事。

sentences.en: Because if we don't understand, we assume that it's because they're just evil people.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们不理解，我们就会认为那是由于他们骨子里是邪恶的人。

sentences.en: And most people aren't that way. They're this way because they've been reinforced or punished for doing something like that in the past.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人并非如此。他们之所以会这样，是因为他们在过去因为类似的行为不断受到奖励或惩罚。

sentences.en: And especially for her, she was reinforced for acting a certain way over and over and over again to the point that it was core to her character.
sentences.zh: 尤其是对她而言，她因为一而再、再而三地表现出某种行为而不断得到强化，以至于这成了她性格的核心。

sentences.en: And so when that got put on me, I was like, I hate you.
sentences.zh: 所以当这种性格被强加到我身上时，我想的是，我恨你。

sentences.en: You're terrible. You're evil, like blah.
sentences.zh: 你太糟糕了。你很邪恶，巴拉巴拉。

sentences.en: But like when I looked at it on a much longer time horizon of like, she was four years old when she came here, she couldn't speak English.
sentences.zh: 但当我把时间线拉长来看，比如她四岁来到这里时还不会说英语。

sentences.en: She got beat up as a kid, like all these things.
sentences.zh: 她小时候挨过打，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I'm like, you know what? Maybe give her a little grace, you know?
sentences.zh: 我在想，你知道吗？也许对她多一点宽容吧，你知道吗？

sentences.en: And I remember when I came back and it was right around that same time where I realized I was giving this person all this power.
sentences.zh: 我还记得当我回来时，大约就在那个时候，我意识到我一直在赋予这个人所有的权力。

sentences.en: Thank you. she yelled at me for something when I came back home from college my freshman year.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。我大一暑假刚从大学回家时，她因为某事对我大吼大叫。

sentences.en: And it was a standard fight. Here's the button that I pressed to get into the normal fight that we get into.
sentences.zh: 这是一次标准的争吵。这就是我按下的按钮，从而引发了我们之间常有的那场常规争吵。

sentences.en: I just remember she hit the button and I just wasn't that upset.
sentences.zh: 我只记得她按下了那个按钮，而我居然没有那么生气。

sentences.en: And it's like I felt nothing. She hit the button.
sentences.zh: 那种感觉就像是我毫无波澜。她按了那个按钮。

sentences.en: She hit it again harder. And I just remember looking at her and being like, I get it.
sentences.zh: 她更用力地又按了一次。我只记得看着她，然后心里想：我明白了。

sentences.en: I'm sorry. You had a tough, tough life. And then she just broke down and started crying because it was like she felt understood.
sentences.zh: 对不起。你过着一段艰难、极其艰难的人生。然后她就崩溃大哭起来，因为那种感觉就像是她终于被理解了。

sentences.en: And I think, I know that was a roundabout way of getting back to regrets, but he regretted how he had raised her.
sentences.zh: 我想，我知道这是兜了个大圈子才又绕回“遗憾”这个话题，但他确实后悔自己当初是那样抚养她的。

sentences.en: But through his regrets, I got to see why she was the way she was.
sentences.zh: 但通过他的遗憾，我得以看清她为什么会变成那样。

sentences.en: And then it diffused the bomb that was between me and her.
sentences.zh: 然后，我和她之间那颗随时会爆炸的炸弹就这样被拆除了。

sentences.en: Did I tell you that story Douglas Murray told me about regrets from Christopher Hitchens?
sentences.zh: 我给你讲过道格拉斯·穆雷跟我讲的关于克里斯托弗·希钦斯的遗憾的故事吗？

sentences.en: Brilliant. So Christopher Hitchens, one of the new atheists, was sat in some British pub with Douglas Murray when Douglas is young and you know you can imagine it's some musty Chesterfield sofa he's probably got a cigarette in his mouth and a glass of scotch or something and uh Douglas is vacillating between these two different choices that he needs to make and he is um complaining lamenting the fact that I have this thing but I have this thing and if I do this thing I can't do this thing and and what what do i do and apparently hitch like sat back and douglas in life we must choose our regrets and i was like fuck so i'm three manhattans deep in douglas murray's apartment in manhattan at two in the morning and he sneaks off to the toilet and i quickly write this down because i know that my like half cut alcohol brain isn't going to remember it so i've noted down.
sentences.zh: 太精彩了。克里斯托弗·希钦斯，新无神论者之一，有一次在一家英国酒吧里，和年轻时的道格拉斯·穆雷坐在一起，你可以想象那是一个发霉的切斯特菲尔德沙发，他嘴里可能叼着一支烟，手里端着一杯苏格兰威士忌什么的，然后啊，道格拉斯正在他需要做出的两个不同选择之间举棋不定，他正在，呃，抱怨、哀叹着说：我既有这个机会，又有那个机会，如果我选了这个，就没法选那个，然后，我到底该怎么办啊？据说希钦往后一靠，说道：“道格拉斯，在生活中，我们必须选择我们的遗憾。”我当时想：我靠！当时我在曼哈顿道格拉斯·穆雷的公寓里，已经喝了三杯曼哈顿鸡尾酒，时间是凌晨两点，他悄悄溜去洗手间，我赶紧把这话记下来，因为我知道我那半醉的酒精大脑根本记不住，所以我把它记了下来。

sentences.en: That was all the trigger that I needed, which is also a good argument for noting things down.
sentences.zh: 这就是我需要的全部触发点，这也顺便证明了把事情记下来的重要性。

sentences.en: And I must have reflected on that for a year.
sentences.zh: 我肯定反思了整整一年。

sentences.en: I must have thought about it for a year.
sentences.zh: 我肯定琢磨了它整整一年。

sentences.en: In life, we must choose our regrets. What the fuck does that mean?
sentences.zh: 在生活中，我们必须选择我们的遗憾。这他妈到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Okay. First off, in an existence where opportunity cost is baked in because you don't get to split test life, and by doing a thing, you can't do a different thing.
sentences.zh: 好吧。首先，在一个本身就内嵌了机会成本的存在中，因为你无法对人生进行拆分测试，当你选择做一件事时，你就无法去做另一件事。

sentences.en: I have the choice between going to the gym and going to the theme park.
sentences.zh: 我有两个选择：去健身房还是去主题公园。

sentences.en: If I go to the gym, therefore, I can't go to the theme park.
sentences.zh: 如果我去健身房，因此，我就不能去主题公园。

sentences.en: Even if the decision of going to the gym was the right call, I will always have the open loop of, yeah, but what if I'd gone to the theme park?
sentences.zh: 即便去健身房这个决定是正确的选择，我的心里也永远会留有一个悬念：是的，但如果我去了主题公园会怎样呢？

sentences.en: You can't ever know, right? Okay. So that means that fundamentally regrets are baked in to our existence.
sentences.zh: 你永远无法知道，对吧？好吧。这意味着，从根本上讲，遗憾是内嵌于我们的存在之中的。

sentences.en: And I'd always thought that the reason I had a regret was due to some suboptimal decision I'd made.
sentences.zh: 我以前一直以为，我之所以会有遗憾，是因为我做出了一些不够完美的决定。

sentences.en: If only I'd made this decision better, I could have ameliorated the regret.
sentences.zh: 要是我当初把这个决定做得更好一点，我本可以减轻这种遗憾。

sentences.en: Okay, so regrets are an unavoidable part of being a human, and they're a byproduct of opportunity cost, which you can't get away from.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所以遗憾是身为人类无法避免的一部分，它们是机会成本的副产品，而你根本无法摆脱。

sentences.en: But what does it mean that you have to choose your regrets?
sentences.zh: 但“你必须选择你的遗憾”到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: Okay, well, if regrets are inevitable, if they're going to happen no matter what, an easy way to look at the decision is, rather than which do I want to do, which regret could I live with?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果遗憾是不可避免的，如果无论如何它们都会发生，那么看待这个决定的一种简单方法是：比起我想做什么，我究竟能与哪种遗憾和平共处？

sentences.en: Because there are certain regrets that you can't bear living with.
sentences.zh: 因为有些遗憾你是无法忍受与之共存的。

sentences.en: Now, you can bear living with them, but they're going to be worse than other ones.
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，你其实也能忍受与它们共存，但它们带来的痛苦会比其他遗憾更深。

sentences.en: So what is the difference between I need to have a difficult decision, I need to have a difficult conversation with my boss about leaving to go and do this thing, or I need to, that's the regret, that's one regret of the sitting down and seeing them face to face and telling them you're going to leave their small mom and pop business and you're the main salesperson and it's going to be terrible and they're going to cry and you're going to feel like a piece of shit.
sentences.zh: 那么，我需要做一个艰难的决定，我需要和老板进行一次艰难的谈话，告诉他我要辞职去干这件事，这有什么区别呢？这就是遗憾，这就是那种坐在他们对面，看着他们的眼睛，告诉他们你要离开他们苦心经营的小生意，而你又是那里的核心销售人员，这感觉糟透了，他们会哭，你会觉得自己像个混蛋。

sentences.en: That's one regret. Another regret is looking back at a decade that you waste in a job that you fucking hate.
sentences.zh: 这是一种遗憾。另一种遗憾是回首往事，发现自己把十年光阴浪费在了一份你极其厌恶的工作上。

sentences.en: Yeah. so in life you have to choose your regrets i love that as a decision making frame because it also jumpstarts our fear engine because rather than saying like what do i want it's what i what do i hate least You and so we get to run it so then you get to use your run away from engine rather than you go towards to it yeah the mouse and the cheese again yeah and was it you was telling me that yeah with the cat i mean yep so i'm just gonna butcher what you told me um but why don't you share that like how much yeah yeah this was on our last episode so this is sequel for the people that were listening um jordan peterson talks about the study where they starve a rat and they put it into a tube they waft the smell of cheese in from the front and there's a spring attached to the rat's tail so they can work out how hard it's pulling how hard it's pulling is a proxy for desire for how much it wants it you'd think this rat is starving it's going to pull as hard as it can so it waft the smell of cheese in and it runs towards it and whatever they do another iteration of the study this time they waft the smell of cheese in from the front and the smell of a cat in from behind yeah it pulls harder yeah why because not only in life do you want to run towards something you want but you want to run away from something that you fear.
sentences.zh: 没错。所以人生中你必须做出选择，我喜欢把这当作一种决策框架，因为它也能启动我们的恐惧引擎，因为与其问自己“我想要什么”，不如问“我最不想要什么”。这样我们就能利用“逃离”的引擎，而不是“奔向”的引擎。又是老鼠和奶酪的例子，对吧？是你跟我讲的这个关于猫的故事吗？我可能会把你讲的内容复述得乱七八糟，但你为什么不分享一下呢？这是我们上一期的内容，所以这对听众来说算是续集。Jordan Peterson 谈到过一个研究，他们让老鼠挨饿，然后把它放进管子里，从前面飘来奶酪的香味，老鼠尾巴上连着弹簧，这样他们就能算出它拉力有多大，拉力大小代表了欲望的强弱。你可能会觉得这只老鼠饿坏了，它会拼命往前拉。于是他们飘来奶酪的香味，它就向着奶酪跑去。不管他们怎么做，在研究的另一轮迭代中，这次他们从前面飘来奶酪的香味，从后面飘来猫的气味。结果它拉得更用力了。为什么？因为在生活中，你不仅想奔向你想要的东西，还想逃离你恐惧的东西。

sentences.en: And this ties into your, the three most common traits of very successful people, superiority complex, massive crippling insufficiency, and impulse control.
sentences.zh: 这与你提到的成功人士最常见的三个特质有关：优越感、巨大的不足感，以及冲动控制。

sentences.en: So superiority complex, I can achieve this thing.
sentences.zh: 所以优越感就是：我可以实现这个目标。

sentences.en: That's the cheese.
sentences.zh: 那就是奶酪。

sentences.en: Crippling sense of insufficiency. I fear the cat.
sentences.zh: 巨大的不足感。我害怕那只猫。

sentences.en: Impulse control. I'm in a tube. There is only one direction I can go.
sentences.zh: 冲动控制。我身处管子之中，我只能向一个方向前进。

sentences.en: I don't need to make a choice. Yep.
sentences.zh: 我不需要做选择。没错。

sentences.en: I love this a lot as a frame for decision making because that, like, think about the decision that we were just talking about, right?
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢把这个作为决策框架，因为，想想我们刚才讨论的那个决定，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's like, I'm the sales guy and I stay.
sentences.zh: 就像，我是那个销售人员，我留下来。

sentences.en: And like, if you were to frame it in upsides, it's like, upside is I keep these friends, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你从收益的角度来衡量，收益就是我保住了这些朋友，对吧？

sentences.en: And I want to leave so that I can start this business, right?
sentences.zh: 我想离开是为了创业，对吧？

sentences.en: Those are the upsides. But when you think about it in terms of like, I wasted a decade of my life not living the life I want.
sentences.zh: 这些是收益。但当你从“我浪费了十年生命，没有过上我想要的生活”这个角度去思考时。

sentences.en: To me, I mean, even when I say it, It sounds more motivating, even though it's the exact same thing.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，即使只是说出来，听起来也更有动力，尽管本质上是一回事。

sentences.en: It's like losing $100 versus gaining $100.
sentences.zh: 就像损失100美元和获得100美元的区别。

sentences.en: People have three times higher loss aversion.
sentences.zh: 人们的损失厌恶心理是收益的三倍。

sentences.en: And so it's like, if you can't get yourself to do something, think about it from the perspective of what you have to lose rather than what you have to gain.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你无法让自己去做某事，试着从你必须失去什么的角度去思考，而不是从你能获得什么的角度。

sentences.en: You've got a quote that I love. My biggest fear is getting to the end of my life and thinking I wasn't good enough.
sentences.zh: 你有一句我很喜欢的名言：“我最大的恐惧是走到生命尽头时，觉得我做得还不够好。”

sentences.en: What's that mean?
sentences.zh: 那是什么意思？

sentences.en: And I'll define good enough as I could have tried harder.
sentences.zh: 我会把“足够好”定义为“我本可以更努力”。

sentences.en: Like I want to leave everything on the field. and one of the things that has helped me a lot i mean in the quote that went unbelievably viral um do you want me to do it again do i need to do it again you don't gain confidence by saying shouting affirmations in the mirror but by stack giving yourself a stack of undeniable proof that you are who you say you are outwork yourself out and again a lot of the tweets that i have are notes to self because like like i have a you know, I have a big presentation coming up.
sentences.zh: 就像我想在赛场上倾尽所有。有一件事对我帮助很大，就是那条在网上疯传的语录。你想让我再复述一遍吗？我需要再讲一遍吗？你无法通过对着镜子大喊大叫来获得自信，而是通过不断给自己积累无可辩驳的证据，证明你就是你所说的那个人。超越自我，再次强调，我的很多推文都是写给自己的备忘录，因为我有一场重要的演讲要进行。

sentences.en: We got 500,000 people who are registered for this book launch that are coming out.
sentences.zh: 这次新书发布会有50万人注册参加。

sentences.en: And I'm thinking to myself, it's like, how can I guarantee that when I step off stage, no matter what happens, I feel like I've accomplished, that I've done a good job, that I can look at myself in the mirror and say, good work.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我该如何保证当我走下舞台时，无论发生什么，我都觉得我完成了任务，我做得很好，我可以看着镜子里的自己说：“干得漂亮”。

sentences.en: And when I was younger, I used to have no way to do that.
sentences.zh: 年轻的时候，我根本做不到这一点。

sentences.en: And that's because I measured everything on outcomes.
sentences.zh: 那是因为我用结果来衡量一切。

sentences.en: But I feel like because I've gotten a little bit more experienced, I do have a way to win now, but it's hard. and the way that I win is when I finish and I say that there's nothing else I could have done and so that means that like the reason that I feel confident about this book that's coming out is I wrote 19 drafts of the book for full rewrites end to end to make the book I did six hours a day my first six hours from 6 a.m. till noon every day for two years to get this book to where it is now and when I was done with the book I was like there's nothing else I can do to this like this is it there's nothing else like I can't make it simpler I can't make it shorter I can't cut it I can't add a visual that I should have added.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得因为我积累了一些经验，我现在确实有办法赢了，但这很难。我获胜的方式是，当我结束时，我说我已尽我所能，没有任何遗憾。所以，我对即将出版的这本书感到自信的原因是，我写了19个草稿，从头到尾彻底重写，为了写好这本书，我连续两年每天工作六个小时，从早上6点到中午，才把这本书打磨到现在的样子。当我写完的时候，我觉得我再也无法改进它了，就是这样，没法更简单了，没法更短了，没法删减了，也没法再加什么我本该加的插图了。

sentences.en: It's done. And so to the same degree with the presentation that I have, I gave myself this framework of like, okay, well, if I were to speak in front of 10,000 people, I would probably spend. a good amount of time prepping the presentation to make sure it was good.
sentences.zh: 它完成了。同样，对于我那场演讲，我给自己设定了一个框架：如果我要在1万人面前演讲，我可能会花大量时间准备，确保它足够好。

sentences.en: I was like, well, I'm going to speak in front of 500,000.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，我要在50万人面前演讲。

sentences.en: I was like, so I can rationalize spending 50 times the amount of work and effort and time to make this thing exceptional.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以合理化地投入50倍的工作量、精力和时间，让这件事变得卓越。

sentences.en: Because I mean, the numbers are hard to fathom, but that is the numbers.
sentences.zh: 因为这些数字很难想象，但事实就是如此。

sentences.en: Like if I had a 10,000, that's what I would do.
sentences.zh: 如果观众是1万人，我就会那样做。

sentences.en: And so it allowed me to take a presentation and I have 900 slides that I'm going to get through in 60 minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以这让我能够准备一场演讲，我有900张幻灯片，要在60分钟内讲完。

sentences.en: And I have now every single day, I do a full draft of the, I'd say the presentation in my head.
sentences.zh: 现在我每天都在脑海里完整地过一遍演讲稿。

sentences.en: And then I do a second run where I say it out loud and I record it.
sentences.zh: 然后我进行第二次演练，大声说出来并录音。

sentences.en: And then after I record it, I play the recording with the slides up and I fix or add every slide where I stumble or there's something that should be there or visual.
sentences.zh: 录音后，我一边看着幻灯片一边播放录音，修正或添加任何我卡壳的地方，或者补充应该有的内容或视觉效果。

sentences.en: And I keep going until now, right now, we can change out.
sentences.zh: 我不断重复，直到现在，我们可以进行调整。

sentences.en: And there's not much else I can do to it.
sentences.zh: 已经没有什么我可以再做的了。

sentences.en: And so I'll still continue to do that from now until the day that it happens, but I probably won't have as many changes because I should just keep nailing it.
sentences.zh: 所以从现在到演讲那天，我还会继续这样做，但可能不会有太多改动，因为我应该已经掌握得炉火纯青了。

sentences.en: And then when I get up there, it doesn't matter if the tech doesn't work or if the book shopping page cart doesn't work or whatever it is, because I'll be able to step off stage and look in the mirror and be like, you did everything you could.
sentences.zh: 然后当我走上台时，即使技术出了问题，或者购书页面坏了，或者发生了什么意外，都没关系，因为我走下舞台时可以看着镜子说：你已经尽力了。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is like, no one else will know that because I know that like, I could not do that.
sentences.zh: 问题是，没人会知道这一点，因为我知道我无法做得更好了。

sentences.en: And I probably, like, you know, a lot of people were like, dude, you have so much goodwill.
sentences.zh: 可能很多人会说，伙计，你已经有这么好的口碑了。

sentences.en: You could probably just say like, here's, you know, here's the book.
sentences.zh: 你可能只需要说一句“这是我的书”就行了。

sentences.en: Um, but I would know. And if I, if I believe what I say I do, which is that I'm the ultimate judge, jury and executioner of my own self-esteem, then I'm the only person who can say good job or not.
sentences.zh: 但我自己心里清楚。如果我相信我所说的，即我是自己自尊心的最终法官、陪审团和执行者，那么我是唯一能评价我做得好不好的人。

sentences.en: And unfortunately I have incredibly high standards.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我的标准高得离谱。

sentences.en: And so I can either just always feel like a failure because I always fall short of my own standards, or I can create a standard that I willingly and consciously accept, which is that I will do enough work that there is nothing left to be done.
sentences.zh: 所以我要么总是觉得自己是个失败者，因为我总是达不到自己的标准，要么我可以设定一个我心甘情愿且有意识接受的标准，那就是：我投入了足够多的工作，以至于再也没有什么可以做的了。

sentences.en: And that means that I can also do fewer things, which means I have to be more selective about the things that I choose to do.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我也可以少做一些事情，这意味着我必须对自己选择做的事情更加挑剔。

sentences.en: But when I do them, they will be done well and they will be done right.
sentences.zh: 但当我做这些事时，它们会被做得很好，做得正确。

sentences.en: They say that true hell is when the person that you are meets the person that you could have been.
sentences.zh: 人们说，真正的地狱是当你遇见了那个本可以成为的自己。

sentences.en: Yeah. And a lot of the time, I think we look at sports stars.
sentences.zh: 没错。很多时候，我想我们看着体育明星。

sentences.en: I'm watching this quarterback on Netflix at the moment.
sentences.zh: 我最近在Netflix上看那个四分卫的纪录片。

sentences.en: And Patrick Mahomes is just this artist.
sentences.zh: Patrick Mahomes 简直是个艺术家。

sentences.en: He's halfway between a warrior and a savant and an artist and a musician and everything rolled together.
sentences.zh: 他介于战士、天才、艺术家和音乐家之间，集所有特质于一身。

sentences.en: The reason that we love seeing behind the scenes with stuff like that is it is somebody at the absolute zenith of their capacity.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢看幕后花絮的原因是，那是某人处于其能力的绝对巅峰。

sentences.en: And they are putting everything that they can into making this as good as possible.
sentences.zh: 他们正竭尽全力让事情变得尽可能完美。

sentences.en: And I think that I sometimes find myself getting, I certainly did before I had the podcast.
sentences.zh: 我想我有时会发现自己，在做播客之前确实如此。

sentences.en: I was wistful that I have the raw materials to work very hard at things.
sentences.zh: 我曾渴望拥有那种可以为某事拼尽全力的原始动力。

sentences.en: And I'd never had a pursuit that I could have applied it to.
sentences.zh: 但我从未有过一个可以让我投入这种动力的追求。

sentences.en: There was nothing. I remember the first time I ever heard Peterson say, work as hard as you can at one thing for a year and see what happens.
sentences.zh: 什么都没有。我记得第一次听到 Peterson 说“在一件事上全力以赴一年，看看会发生什么”。

sentences.en: And I'd never had a thing that I could work.
sentences.zh: 但我从未有过那样一件事可以让我全力以赴。

sentences.en: I could work hard at business, but the line between your inputs and your outcomes is so meandering and messy that I can always excuse away good or bad performances as not being on me.
sentences.zh: 我可以在商业上努力工作，但投入与产出之间的界限是如此曲折和混乱，以至于我总是可以把表现的好坏归咎于非我所能控制的因素。

sentences.en: And for the most part, I would take responsibility for the bad ones and not take responsibility for the good ones because that's how I'm wired.
sentences.zh: 大多数时候，我会为糟糕的表现负责，却不会为好的表现邀功，因为我的思维方式就是这样。

sentences.en: But I never had something that was linear, close to linear.
sentences.zh: 但我从未有过一件线性的、接近线性的事情。

sentences.en: I'm like, I put an hour in and I get an hour out or more than an hour out and it's direct.
sentences.zh: 就像我投入一小时，就能得到一小时或更多的产出，这是直接的。

sentences.en: And then about three years ago, I had this conversation with Dean, my video guy.
sentences.zh: 大约三年前，我和我的视频制作人 Dean 谈过。

sentences.en: I was like, I want to turn pro. I read Stephen Pressfield, War of Art, and then I read Turning Pro.
sentences.zh: 我说，我想成为职业选手。我读了 Stephen Pressfield 的《艺术之战》，然后读了《成为职业选手》。

sentences.en: I want to turn pro with the show. What's that mean?
sentences.zh: 我想让这个节目变得专业。那是什么意思？

sentences.en: What would it mean if I treated this pursuit like an athlete does?
sentences.zh: 如果我像运动员那样对待这个追求，意味着什么？

sentences.en: So an athlete, they review game tape and they do mindset work and they've got a sports psychologist and they look at what they eat and they look at what they drink and they go to bed on time and they're hanging around with people that are growth-minded and they're getting the right coaches and then all the rest, everything is done. in order to facilitate performance in the thing that they say they care about.
sentences.zh: 运动员会复盘比赛录像，进行心态训练，有运动心理学家，关注饮食，关注饮水，按时睡觉，与志同道合的人交往，聘请合适的教练，其余的一切，都是为了促进他们所关心的那件事的表现。

sentences.en: But everybody has the opportunity to do that.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都有机会这样做。

sentences.en: You just need to define what the thing is.
sentences.zh: 你只需要定义那件事是什么。

sentences.en: I'm never going to be Patrick Mahomes, right?
sentences.zh: 我永远不会成为 Patrick Mahomes，对吧？

sentences.en: No. But I managed to find my thing and then nearly kill myself in dedication toward it.
sentences.zh: 不会。但我设法找到了我的目标，并几乎为此献出了生命。

sentences.en: There's a photo that I put up on my Instagram a little while ago, two weeks after I ruptured my Achilles.
sentences.zh: 我前段时间在 Instagram 上发了一张照片，那是我跟腱断裂两周后。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, I saw that. and I'm in a boot and I've got the laptop on my lap and we've created this arm that'll bring the mic to me because I didn't want to stop doing the podcast because I'd made this commitment.
sentences.zh: 没错，我看到了。我穿着护具，腿上放着笔记本电脑，我们做了一个支架把麦克风送到我面前，因为我不想停止做播客，因为我做出了承诺。

sentences.en: I'm going to turn pro. And for three years, we haven't missed a single episode three times a week, three times a week, three times a week for three years now.
sentences.zh: 我要成为职业选手。三年来，我们从未错过任何一期节目，每周三次，每周三次，每周三次，坚持了三年。

sentences.en: And before that, it was two a week for a year.
sentences.zh: 在那之前，是一年每周两次。

sentences.en: And before that, it was one a week for a year.
sentences.zh: 再之前，是一年每周一次。

sentences.en: And it just keeps on ramping up. And the opportunity to commit yourself fully to something that you care about is beyond a blessing.
sentences.zh: 而且它还在不断增加。能够全身心地投入到你关心的事情中，这简直是莫大的福分。

sentences.en: And when you do it, the way that you feel once you know that you've worked hard is great.
sentences.zh: 当你这样做的时候，一旦你知道自己努力过了，那种感觉太棒了。

sentences.en: And we said before we started, you've got this big thing coming up, which I'm super proud of you for managing to achieve, even though it hasn't happened yet.
sentences.zh: 我们在开始前说过，你有一件大事要发生，我为你能够实现它感到非常自豪，尽管它还没发生。

sentences.en: The difference between being nervous and being excited before you do something is your level of preparation in advance of it.
sentences.zh: 在做某事之前，紧张和兴奋的区别在于你提前准备的程度。

sentences.en: If you step out on stage or in front of half a million people on a webinar, which is the craziest sentence I've ever said, if you step out on stage in front of half a million people and you've done absolutely everything, there's nothing to fear.
sentences.zh: 如果你走上舞台，或者在网络研讨会上面对50万人——这是我这辈子说过最疯狂的话——如果你面对50万人走上舞台，而你已经做了所有准备，那就没什么好怕的了。

sentences.en: And that's why it's not about what everyone else will think, because when I'm on stage making that presentation, the only person whose voice I'll hear is mine.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这与别人怎么想无关，因为当我在台上做演讲时，我唯一能听到的声音就是我自己的。

sentences.en: And I will know if I have done everything in my control to be prepared or not.
sentences.zh: 我会知道我是否已经尽我所能做好了准备。

sentences.en: And what's the best thing that comes out?
sentences.zh: 如果没做好准备会怎样？

sentences.en: I didn't do everything that I could to prepare, and I managed to fluke my performance.
sentences.zh: 我没有尽我所能去准备，但我侥幸表现得还行。

sentences.en: I managed to close my eyes, throw the dart, and oh, wow, it hit the bullseye.
sentences.zh: 我闭上眼睛，扔出飞镖，哇，竟然中了靶心。

sentences.en: You'll even know that. There'll even be guilt.
sentences.zh: 你甚至会知道这一点。甚至会有负罪感。

sentences.en: You won't even be able to fully enjoy your success because you'll have tarnished it with your lack of input.
sentences.zh: 你甚至无法完全享受你的成功，因为你的投入不足已经玷污了它。

sentences.en: And what's interesting is that when you start defining your own success that way, it actually starts to feel under your own control.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，当你开始以这种方式定义自己的成功时，它实际上开始感觉在你的掌控之中了。

sentences.en: But the downside is you realize that you can do very few things.
sentences.zh: 但缺点是你意识到你能做的事情非常少。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden life feels very short because you're like, shoot, there's like not that many things I can do before I die if I'm going to actually do my best.
sentences.zh: 突然间，人生感觉很短暂，因为你会想，天哪，如果我要真正做到最好，在我死之前我能做的事情并不多。

sentences.en: And what was interesting is I was talking to a CEO friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，我和一位 CEO 朋友聊过。

sentences.en: He's a public CEO. And he was like, I need to start making content, right?
sentences.zh: 他是一家上市公司的 CEO。他说，我需要开始创作内容，对吧？

sentences.en: I'm like, managing a billion dollar company.
sentences.zh: 我说，管理着一家十亿美元的公司。

sentences.en: I was like, you're doing okay, man. But because of that type of person, he's like, I need to be doing better with my content, right?
sentences.zh: 我说，你做得挺好的，伙计。但因为他是那种人，他说，我需要在内容创作上做得更好，对吧？

sentences.en: He's got a few hundred thousand followers.
sentences.zh: 他有几十万粉丝。

sentences.en: Anyways. And so I was like, all right, well, how many pieces of content you're putting out a week?
sentences.zh: 总之。我说，好吧，你每周发布多少内容？

sentences.en: And he was like, well, I mean, I put out one a day.
sentences.zh: 他说，嗯，我每天发布一条。

sentences.en: And I was like, dude, I was like, we put out 300 a week.
sentences.zh: 我说，伙计，我们每周发布300条。
