sentences.en: And he just, he didn't even respond. He just took, he just like pursed his lips and nodded.
sentences.zh: 他甚至没有回应。他只是抿了抿嘴，点了点头。

sentences.en: He was like, thank you for resetting my minimum standard.
sentences.zh: 他说，谢谢你重置了我的最低标准。

sentences.en: It's always like, And I'm sure when you talk to Phil Heath and he talks about the volume that is required in order to gain muscle and how dialed in he is with food and all the other things.
sentences.zh: 总是这样。我相信当你和 Phil Heath 交谈时，他谈到为了增肌所需的训练量，以及他在饮食和其他方面是多么严谨。

sentences.en: Just the amount of sheer work, like the biggest change in, or I'll say biggest reason that I've had significantly larger returns or outcomes that have happened later on in my career and they continue to get bigger and bigger is because the minimum standard for how much work I know I can do on something has multiplied a hundredfold.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是纯粹的工作量，我职业生涯后期获得巨大回报或成果的最大原因，就是我知道自己在某件事上可以投入的工作量的最低标准已经翻了一百倍。

sentences.en: Like I look at the first presentations, I was telling Quinn this earlier, I look at the first presentations I ever gave.
sentences.zh: 就像我看着我最初的演讲，我之前跟 Quinn 提过，我看着我做过的第一次演讲。

sentences.en: And I remember thinking to myself when I had this, I was like, this is a good presentation.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时心想，这是一个很好的演讲。

sentences.en: It's like 25 slides with like a heading and like three bullets on each slide and being like, man, this is good.
sentences.zh: 大约25张幻灯片，每张有一个标题和三个要点，心想，天哪，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I'm like, this is a, this is, this is a pittance.
sentences.zh: 我现在觉得，这简直是九牛一毛。

sentences.en: This is like an afternoon. But in my mind, if I spent a whole day on something, that was like a lot of work. now it's I you know I like using this term like measuring hundreds which is like measuring hundreds of hours how many hundreds of hours have you put towards something If you do that, I promise you the thing that you're making will get a lot better.
sentences.zh: 这就像一个下午的工作量。但在当时，如果我花了一整天做某事，那就算是很努力了。现在我喜欢用“测量百小时”这个词，也就是测量投入了多少百小时。如果你这样做，我保证你做出来的东西会好得多。

sentences.en: And you'll also see how much more you're capable of, which is what I think like my undertone of listening to what you were just saying with the podcast is like, the more you do, the more you realize you can do.
sentences.zh: 你也会看到你还有多大的潜力，这就是我觉得听你刚才说播客时的潜台词，你做得越多，你越意识到你能做到的更多。

sentences.en: And so what happens is you're actually, even though you're, you're going pro right now, you're like, dude, next year I'm going pro because this is now just a minimum standard.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的事情是，即使你现在正在走向专业，你会想，伙计，明年我会更专业，因为这现在只是最低标准。

sentences.en: Of course I work out three days a week. Of course I do three podcasts a week, but dude, once we have the reality TV show and we have the full crew and we have the headquarter, Like, cause then the path gets lit of where you're going to go because you're so singularly focused and you know, you have no other distractions.
sentences.zh: 当然我每周锻炼三次。当然我每周做三次播客，但伙计，一旦我们有了真人秀，有了完整的团队，有了总部，因为那时你前进的道路就清晰了，因为你如此专注，你知道，你没有其他干扰。

sentences.en: The attention cost isn't, you're not paying that down anymore.
sentences.zh: 注意力成本不再是你在支付的东西了。

sentences.en: And you're just like, how many times can I repeat this effort?
sentences.zh: 你只是在想，我能重复多少次这种努力？

sentences.en: And then that's when you start unlocking mastery, right?
sentences.zh: 那时你才开始解锁大师境界，对吧？

sentences.en: Like I have this process for creating presentations.
sentences.zh: 比如我有一套制作演讲的流程。

sentences.en: And before we turned on the mics, we were talking about it, but it's like, I've done a handful of presentations in my life and I've gotten decent at making them. but the process now is so refined which is like it is game tape it is I make the thing I do the thing in my head I do it out loud I watch the recording I edit the thing I do it in my head I do it out loud I watch the recording I edit the thing and I just keep doing it until it's glass Dude I listen to I listen to every podcast that I did for probably the first two and a half years I listen back every single time but at the time I didn't cringe because I thought you crushed it anybody can go back and listen to episode one with Stuart Morton in my old office in Newcastle upon Tyne, and you'll notice every other sentence that he says, I go, mm-hmm, mm-hmm, mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 在打开麦克风之前，我们谈过这个，但我这辈子做过不少演讲，制作演讲的水平也还不错。但现在的流程非常精炼，就是复盘录像，我制作它，在脑海里演练，大声说出来，观看录音，编辑它，在脑海里演练，大声说出来，观看录音，编辑它，我一直重复直到它完美无瑕。伙计，我听了我前两年半做的每一个播客，我每次都回听，但当时我并没有感到尴尬，因为我觉得你做得太棒了。任何人都可以回去听我和 Stuart Morton 在纽卡斯尔老办公室录的第一集，你会注意到他说的每隔一句话，我就说“嗯哼，嗯哼，嗯哼”。

sentences.en: It's fucking infuriating. It's absolutely catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 这简直太令人恼火了。这绝对是灾难性的。

sentences.en: My accent's terrible. Everything, everything, everything about it is awful.

Let's see what happens when you have 30 other things every single week vying for your attention. now let's see how committed you are this is my favorite analogy for this which is the woman in the red dress but you know every many people have seen the matrix if you haven't seen the matrix you don't need to have seen it to understand the analogy so neo is going through the training program the protagonist morpheus is his his educator his his teacher and the education program only has one objective and so he's walking through the city people are going left and right he's bumping into people going through like crowded new york and then all of a sudden it's kind of a black and white, palish look.

sentences.zh: 突然，这个红衣女郎进入了画面，你忍不住盯着这个红衣女郎看，她简直是个尤物。

sentences.en: And Morpheus is talking to Neo, trying to teach him something.
sentences.zh: Morpheus 正在和 Neo 说话，试图教他东西。

sentences.zh: 当他说话时，他说，Neo，你是看着我，还是在看那个红衣女郎？

sentences.zh: 他说，再看一遍。他回头看，发现是史密斯探员用枪指着他的头。

sentences.en: And he says, freeze. And then everything freezes in the frame.
sentences.zh: 他说，别动。然后画面里的一切都静止了。

sentences.en: And he's like, if you're not one of us, you're one of them.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果你不是我们的人，你就是他们的人。

sentences.en: And I see that as the opportunities that we have to say no to every day.
sentences.zh: 我把这看作是我们每天必须拒绝的机会。

sentences.en: It's like another woman in the red dress.
sentences.zh: 就像另一个红衣女郎。

sentences.zh: 这已经成为我们在内部使用的术语，对吧？

sentences.en: It's like, it's a woman in the red dress.
sentences.zh: 就像，这是一个红衣女郎。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is that the more successful you become or the more able you become. the hotter the woman in the red dress is, right?
sentences.zh: 问题是，你变得越成功，或者你能力越强，红衣女郎就越迷人，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you got a homeless girl that you're walking, you know, past on the street, she's like all dirty, but she's got a red dress on.
sentences.zh: 就像你走在街上经过一个无家可归的女孩，她很脏，但她穿着红裙子。

sentences.en: You're like, the thing is, is that that homeless girl, when you were in your apartment, actually looks like- It's pretty hot.
sentences.zh: 你会觉得，问题是，那个无家可归的女孩，当你在公寓里时，实际上看起来……挺火辣的。

sentences.en: Yeah, right. She's like, you know, I'm not, you know, I could, you know, right?
sentences.zh: 是的，对吧。她就像，你知道，我不是，我可以，你知道，对吧？

sentences.en: But then the better you get, the bigger the opportunities.
sentences.zh: 但你越优秀，机会就越大。

sentences.en: And that's where you have, not your hypothetical 10, but what about your hypothetical 100?
sentences.zh: 这就是你拥有的，不是你假设的10个，而是你假设的100个？

sentences.en: And I had a mentor say this to me right as we sold gym launch.
sentences.zh: 我在卖掉 Gym Launch 时，一位导师对我说了这句话。

sentences.en: He said, Alex, that you know now that if it's not a billion, it's not worth your time.
sentences.zh: 他说，Alex，你知道现在如果不是十亿级别的生意，就不值得你花时间。

sentences.en: And that was such a single, a great razor for all decisions.
sentences.zh: 这对于所有决策来说是一个非常棒的准则。

sentences.en: And so people, they're like, hey, we should do this endorsement.
sentences.zh: 所以人们会说，嘿，我们应该做这个代言。

sentences.en: Hey, we should partner with this, whatever.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我们应该和这个合作，等等。

sentences.zh: 我们收到了多少交易？每个月有3000家公司联系我们寻求合作。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying you shouldn't apply, by all means go to acquisition.com and apply if you have an awesome business um but but the point is is that like your no muscle isn't really a no muscle it's just a yes muscle for the one thing that matters most yeah heroes and villains always have the same backstory pain the difference is what they choose to do about it villain says the world hurt me i'll hurt it back the hero says the world hurt me i'm not gonna let it hurt anybody else heroes use pain villains are used by it and full kudos here this is a permutation of what uh donald miller said um who's a great writer and he has a number of books and he he talked about the first element the second element of that quote is the part that i added to it um about heroes using pain and villains being used by it and so one of the things for people who are not where they want to be is that they have pain like oodles of pain.
sentences.zh: 我不是说你不应该申请，如果你的生意很棒，一定要去 acquisition.com 申请，但重点是，你的“拒绝肌肉”并不是真正的拒绝肌肉，它只是为了最重要的一件事而准备的“接受肌肉”。英雄和反派总是有相同的背景故事：痛苦。区别在于他们选择如何处理它。反派说：世界伤害了我，我要报复它。英雄说：世界伤害了我，我不会让它伤害任何人。英雄利用痛苦，反派被痛苦所利用。这里要向 Donald Miller 致敬，他是一位伟大的作家，有很多著作，他谈到了这个语录的第一个要素，第二个要素是我加进去的，关于英雄利用痛苦而反派被痛苦利用。所以对于那些还没达到目标的人来说，他们有痛苦，大量的痛苦。

sentences.en: And I remember when I was starting out, I was looking for passion.
sentences.zh: 我记得刚开始的时候，我在寻找激情。

sentences.en: I was looking for purpose. I was like, I just want to find something that I'm motivated by.
sentences.zh: 我在寻找目标。我当时想，我只是想找到一些能激励我的东西。

sentences.en: But it's the cat and the cheese. It's like, we're looking for cheese, but we have all these cat behind us and all we have to do is look and remember that they're behind us and chasing us.
sentences.zh: 但这就是猫和奶酪的故事。我们是在寻找奶酪，但我们身后有这么多猫，我们所要做的就是回头记住它们就在我们身后追赶我们。

sentences.en: And so if you have the cat and you're staying in your current situation, you're being used by the cat, right?
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有那只猫，而你还待在目前的环境中，你就是被猫利用了，对吧？

sentences.en: You're being used by the business owner who doesn't treat you well and you're in this job that you don't really want to be in, right?
sentences.zh: 你被那个不善待你的老板利用了，你正处于一份你并不真正想做的工作中，对吧？

sentences.en: Or you're being used by the situation or the context of the relationship that you're in with the girl that you're like not that into, right?
sentences.zh: 或者你正被你所处的环境，或者你与那个你其实并不怎么喜欢的女孩之间的关系所利用，对吧？

sentences.en: Versus saying like, this is terrible.
sentences.zh: 而不是说：这太糟糕了。

sentences.en: And because of this terribleness, I now have something that I can run away from.
sentences.zh: 正因为这种糟糕，我才有了可以逃离的东西。

sentences.en: And then like, rather than not looking at the knife or trying to take painkillers to not feel the pain, it's like completely sobering up, taking the knife and twisting it in your own heart and being like, I'm going to fucking do something about this.
sentences.zh: 与其不去正视那把刀，或者试图通过吃止痛药来麻痹痛苦，不如彻底清醒过来，拿起那把刀，亲手刺进自己的心脏，然后对自己说：我一定要为此做点什么。

sentences.en: And I think that that's what the heroes, like if we're heroes in our own story, it's not avoiding pain.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是英雄所为，如果我们是自己故事里的英雄，那绝不是去逃避痛苦。

sentences.en: It's choosing from the very beginning, the alchemy, which is like, you have these terrible situations.
sentences.zh: 而是从一开始就选择炼金术，也就是：你拥有这些糟糕的处境。

sentences.en: It's like, and you have the opportunity to turn them into magic and skip or shortcut all the growth you're going to have in a really short period of time simply by twisting the knife and being like, I'm going to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 你可以把它们变成魔法，通过刺向自己那一刀，并下定决心改变现状，从而在极短的时间内跳过或缩短你本该经历的成长过程。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think because people presume in the beginning that passion and purpose and meaning and joy and fulfillment are the things that get people going.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为是因为人们一开始就预设了激情、目标、意义、快乐和成就感才是驱动人们前进的动力。

sentences.en: But as I've said, of all of the high performers that I've spoken to, the vast, vast, vast majority of them are driven by insufficiency and resentment and terrible parents or terrible upbringings or a chip on their shoulder about bullies in school.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，在我交谈过的所有高成就者中，绝大多数人都是被匮乏感、怨恨、糟糕的父母、不幸的成长经历，或者因为在学校被霸凌而产生的某种心结所驱动的。

sentences.en: Pick your poison. they have decided to use that to create the activation energy right you can lower your action threshold and increase how many points you have to prove.
sentences.zh: 随你选吧，他们决定利用这些来产生启动能量，你可以降低行动门槛，并增加你需要证明自己的点。

sentences.en: It's like, oh, I want to live a better life.
sentences.zh: 就像是：哦，我想过上更好的生活。

sentences.en: Yeah, that sounds good. It's like, I want to prove the bullies that said I was a worthless piece of shit in school wrong.
sentences.zh: 是的，听起来不错。就像是：我想向学校里那些说我是个废物的人证明他们错了。

sentences.en: It's like, that's some fucking potent fuel.
sentences.zh: 这真是强有力的燃料。

sentences.en: I do believe that scaled over a long enough time, it's toxic.
sentences.zh: 我确实相信，如果长期来看，这是有毒的。

sentences.en: And I don't think that it's necessarily- How long?
sentences.zh: 而且我不认为这一定是——多久？

sentences.en: Well, that's the question. Like a lifetime, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这就是问题所在。比如一辈子，对吧？

sentences.en: But I mean, it'll fuel you for a decade pretty well.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，它能很好地支撑你十年。

sentences.en: And I think that, I look at me, I look at, you know, I was bullied pretty badly in school and was an only child and had expectations from parents.
sentences.zh: 我想，看看我，看看我，你知道，我在学校被霸凌得很惨，又是独生子，还背负着父母的期望。

sentences.en: And, you know, I combined all of those things together and I did have a chip on my shoulder and I did want to prove to the world that I was worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我把所有这些事情结合在一起，我确实产生了一个心结，我确实想向世界证明我是有价值的。

sentences.en: And I did want people to realize that they had doubted the wrong person.
sentences.zh: 我确实想让人们意识到他们看错人了。

sentences.en: Fuck yeah. Yeah, damn right I do.
sentences.zh: 去他的，没错，我确实这么想。

sentences.en: I think being really specific about your pain is helpful. so like even being specific about the cheese really specificity in general is helpful but like even more so like what is the twisting the pain what is twisting the knife like what is how do you operationalize twisting the knife right instead of being like i hate my life right it's i hate the way andrew makes me feel when he says that i'm a piece of shit and i'm not going to amount to anything comma because he's right like why does it hurt me like if someone says alex you're a piece of shit you're not going to amount to anything if someone accuses you of being poor or fat right i i would have i'd be like i have evidence to the contrary so this will probably not bother me but the things that bother us are the ones that you know have an element of truth or sometimes not an element are comprised almost entirely of truth and we just don't want to look at it and so i think it's it's the the twisting the knife is looking in the mirror and saying what if they're right success is the only revenge as you expand they shrink into irrelevance as you get louder no one can hear them you don't beat them you cast a shadow so big no one can see them to begin with when people copy they copy the wrong stuff because they don't know why it worked to begin with and when it breaks they don't know how to fix it because they didn't build it so don't sweat it copycats will always be behind good shit but success is the only revenge is such a lovely does that um want to tell you the story behind it i'm right yeah so i was 15 years old so this was really early in my life still jacked still jacked always jacked perma jacked and i uh this sounds so lame so i had this teacher so i'm freshman in high school and i might have been 14 whatever the age is and i'm walking through the hallway and this this teacher is like an admin of some kind walks out of his office.
sentences.zh: 我认为对你的痛苦保持具体是非常有帮助的。就像对那块“奶酪”保持具体，总的来说，具体化很有帮助，但更重要的是，什么是“扭转痛苦”，什么是“刺向自己那一刀”，你该如何操作这种“刺向自己”？而不是仅仅说“我讨厌我的生活”，而是说“我讨厌Andrew说我是个废物、我一事无成时带给我的那种感觉，因为他说得对”。为什么这会让我受伤？如果有人说“Alex，你是个废物，你一事无成”，如果有人指责你贫穷或肥胖，我会说我有证据反驳，所以这可能不会困扰我。但那些困扰我们的事情，往往是因为它们包含了一部分事实，有时甚至完全是事实，而我们只是不想面对。所以我认为，“刺向自己”就是照镜子，然后问自己：如果他们说的是对的呢？成功是唯一的复仇。当你扩张时，他们会萎缩到无关紧要；当你声音变大时，没人能听到他们；你不需要打败他们，你投下的阴影如此巨大，以至于一开始就没人能看到他们。当人们模仿时，他们模仿的是错误的东西，因为他们根本不知道为什么它会成功，当它崩溃时，他们也不知道如何修复，因为那不是他们建立的。所以别担心，模仿者永远会落在后面。好东西，但“成功是唯一的复仇”这句话真是太棒了。你想听听背后的故事吗？我当然想。好的，当时我15岁，那是我生命中非常早期的阶段，依然很壮，一直都很壮，永远都很壮。我当时……这听起来太逊了，我有个老师，我是高一新生，可能14岁，不管几岁吧，我走在走廊里，这个老师，某种行政人员，从办公室走出来。

sentences.en: And he's like, son. And I was like, I'm like, you're just in trouble.
sentences.zh: 他说：孩子。我当时想：你肯定有麻烦了。

sentences.en: What am I going to do? And he's like, you work out?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么办？他说：你健身吗？

sentences.en: He's like, I'll show you. He's like, you got the genes.
sentences.zh: 他说：我教你。他说：你有这方面的基因。

sentences.zh: 于是那个老师，Mr. Gibbons，最终在高中每天陪我健身，教我怎么练。

sentences.en: And he probably saw on some level that I was some angsty teenager that felt angry about whatever.
sentences.zh: 他可能在某种程度上看出我是一个对任何事情都感到愤怒的焦虑青少年。

sentences.en: And I, during our workout sessions would be like, this guy said this to me, like, you know, or like keep this, whatever.
sentences.zh: 在我们的训练课上，我会说：那个人对我说了这个，或者说，记住这个，不管是什么。

sentences.en: And I was like, man, I'm going to come back at our 10 year reunion.
sentences.zh: 我说：伙计，我要在十年同学会上回来找他。

sentences.en: And I was like, I'm going to show him. I was like, he's going to be working for me, like blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 我说：我要让他看看。我说：他以后会为我打工，等等等等。

sentences.en: Right. And he's like, no, he's not. And I was like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 他说：不，他不会。我说：你什么意思？

sentences.en: I was like, let me just have my moment. He's like, no, he's not.
sentences.zh: 我说：让我享受一下我的时刻吧。他说：不，他不会。

sentences.en: He's like, and you're not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 他说：而且你不会那样做。

sentences.en: Not if I have anything to say about it. When you come back for the 10 year reunion, I was like, what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 只要我还在，你就不会。当你十年后回来时，我说：你什么意思？

sentences.en: He's like, because if you come back at a 10 year reunion and say, Hey, John, everything I have, look at me now.
sentences.zh: 他说：因为如果你十年后回来，说“嘿，John，看看我拥有的一切，看看现在的我”。

sentences.en: He's like, the guy's going to laugh and be like, you did all of this to try and prove me wrong?
sentences.zh: 他说：那个人会笑话你，说“你做这一切就是为了向我证明我错了？”

sentences.en: Man, I feel sorry for you. And when he said that, when he actually played out what my revenge fantasy was in real life, I realized it looked stupid.
sentences.zh: 伙计，我真为你感到难过。当他说出这句话，当他真正演绎出我的复仇幻想在现实中是什么样子时，我意识到这看起来太蠢了。

sentences.en: Yeah. I looked like the beta in the fucking situation, right?
sentences.zh: 是的。我在那种情况下看起来像个失败者，对吧？

sentences.en: And so he was like, the only thing that you can do is win so big that all of them constantly compare themselves to you and then you'll forget they exist.
sentences.zh: 所以他说：你唯一能做的就是取得巨大的成功，让他们不断地拿自己和你比较，然后你就会忘记他们的存在。

sentences.en: And that's when he said, he said, success is the only revenge.
sentences.zh: 那就是他说“成功是唯一的复仇”的时候。

sentences.en: He's like, it's not the best revenge. He's like, it's the only one.
sentences.zh: 他说：这不是最好的复仇，这是唯一的复仇。

sentences.en: There's no other revenge because everything else is petty.

sentences.en: I really do think I've gotten a lot better at it.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为我在这方面进步了很多。

sentences.en: At least recognizing because the more times I've had Ws and then realized that right afterwards, I felt nothing.
sentences.zh: 至少在识别这一点上，因为我获得胜利的次数越多，就越意识到在那之后，我什么感觉都没有。

sentences.en: I had to think back of like, what are the things that I enjoyed most in my life?
sentences.zh: 我不得不回想，我生命中最享受的事情是什么？

sentences.en: And it's always in pursuit. And I'm like, well, then why don't I set something really big, really far so I can be in pursuit for the longest period of time possible.
sentences.zh: 总是处于追求的过程中。所以我心想，好吧，那为什么我不设定一个非常宏大、非常遥远的目标，这样我就可以在尽可能长的时间里处于追求的状态中呢？

sentences.en: And that's where I think a lot of people from the outside, you know, they cast their expectations of life onto me and say, I wouldn't live my life that way.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为很多局外人，你知道，他们把对生活的期望投射到我身上，说，我才不会那样过日子。

sentences.en: You're always, you're always working. You're always doing these things, but it's like, I'm actually always spending my time in pursuit because in pursuit is my button for enjoyment.
sentences.zh: 你总是，你总是忙个不停。你总是做这些事情，但实际上，我总是把时间花在追求上，因为“追求”就是我享受生活的按钮。

sentences.en: Well, what about if it wasn't achieving the thing at the end?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果不是为了实现最终的目标呢？

sentences.en: If the reason that you set yourself goals is exclusively to motivate yourself to enjoy the route toward those goals.
sentences.zh: 如果你设定目标的原因仅仅是为了激励自己去享受通往这些目标的路径呢？

sentences.en: And I I know that it's not the destination, it's the journey is kind of cliche.
sentences.zh: 我知道“不在乎目的地，只在乎旅程”是一种陈词滥调。

sentences.en: And I think this is slightly subtly different, which is that it's actually about setting the destination.
sentences.zh: 但我认为这有细微的不同，那就是这实际上是关于设定目的地。

sentences.en: Without the destination, you wouldn't do the journey.
sentences.zh: 没有目的地，你就不会去经历旅程。

sentences.en: Like the way that you set goals and then achieve them and the dopamine and the trigger that you get.
sentences.zh: 就像你设定目标然后实现它们，以及你从中获得的多巴胺和触发点一样。

sentences.en: I often think about the balance between like serotonin, Chris, and dopamine, Chris.
sentences.zh: 我经常思考血清素和多巴胺之间的平衡。

sentences.en: And I don't even know the difference between them.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不知道它们之间的区别。

sentences.en: It's like, am I feeling sort of lovey and present and wanting to connect with people?
sentences.zh: 就像，我是感到那种充满爱意、活在当下并想要与人建立联系的感觉？

sentences.en: Or am I driving toward a thing because I have a goal that's in front of me?
sentences.zh: 还是因为我面前有一个目标，所以我在朝着那个目标前进？

sentences.en: And I'm very sort of dopamine, Chris, a lot of the time.
sentences.zh: 我很多时候都是那种多巴胺驱动型的人。

sentences.en: But I genuinely think that if you remind yourself, these are the golden years.
sentences.zh: 但我真心认为，如果你提醒自己，这就是黄金岁月。

sentences.en: Like this right now, when you look back, these will be the golden years, right?
sentences.zh: 就像现在，当你回首往事时，这些就是黄金岁月，对吧？

sentences.en: When I had my health, I had my full mental capacity.
sentences.zh: 当我拥有健康，拥有完整的智力能力时。

sentences.en: I had control of my bladder. I had all of the money that I needed to do the things that I wanted to crush it with my friends, to fly around America and film these podcasts or to launch this book that I spend all of this time on.
sentences.zh: 我拥有控制自己膀胱的能力。我拥有做我想做的事情所需的所有金钱，和朋友们一起大干一场，飞遍美国拍摄这些播客，或者发布我投入了所有时间的这本书。

sentences.en: And you can even see it in the micro. You can even see it when you look back on stuff that you've done in your day-to-day business or what you did at university.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在微观层面看到这一点。当你回顾你在日常业务中所做的事情，或者你在大学时所做的事情时，你也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: What were the times that you enjoyed? Was it when success came to you easily?
sentences.zh: 你享受的时光是什么时候？是成功轻易到来的时候吗？

sentences.en: Or was it when you stayed up and ordered Domino's because you had that project that needed to be in at six in the morning and you ran an all-nighter and John slept under the table and everybody ordered monsters.
sentences.zh: 还是你熬夜点着达美乐披萨，因为那个项目必须在早上六点前完成，你通宵达旦，John睡在桌子底下，每个人都喝着魔爪饮料的时候？

sentences.en: And then the next morning we got it done.
sentences.zh: 然后第二天早上我们完成了它。

sentences.en: What was good about that? Was it when you submitted it or was it the dominoes and the 3am sleep under the table?
sentences.zh: 那段时光好在哪里？是提交项目的时候，还是吃披萨和凌晨三点睡在桌子底下的时候？

sentences.en: Because I'm pretty sure it's that.
sentences.zh: 因为我很确定是后者。

sentences.en: I love this as a side note.
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，我很喜欢这个观点。

sentences.en: But one of the things that really motivates me, or one of my most powerful motivational frames is thinking about the person that I want to become as the destination.
sentences.zh: 但真正激励我的一件事，或者我最强大的激励框架之一，就是把我想成为的那个人当作目的地。

sentences.en: And thinking like, I want to be bulletproof.
sentences.zh: 我在想，我想成为一个刀枪不入的人。

sentences.en: I want to be bulletproof in these ways. I want to be bulletproof in my marriage.
sentences.zh: 我想在这些方面都做到刀枪不入。我想在婚姻中刀枪不入。

sentences.en: I want to be bulletproof in my business, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 我想在事业上刀枪不入，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And I think about that man, whoever I want him to be.
sentences.zh: 我一直在思考那个男人，无论我想成为什么样的男人。

sentences.en: Like we said, hell is when you look at who you could have been and realize that you're not that person.
sentences.zh: 就像我们说过的，地狱就是当你看着自己本可以成为的样子，却意识到你并不是那个人。

sentences.en: And then I think if I were to make that man, what would I put that man through to make him who he is?
sentences.zh: 然后我在想，如果我要塑造那个男人，我会让他经历什么来成就现在的他？

sentences.en: Like it wouldn't be easy times. it wouldn't be quick wins.
sentences.zh: 那肯定不会是轻松的时光，也不会是唾手可得的成功。

sentences.en: It wouldn't even be easy wins. It would be the, the toil and the struggle of achieving and reaching for things that are right out of grasp that are right above my threshold and continuing to do that, to like lift the weight, to build the muscle, to break it down and do it over and over again, because like, that's what creates the character traits that are the man that I want to be.
sentences.zh: 甚至连简单的胜利都不会有。那将是辛勤的耕耘和挣扎，去追求那些触手可及却又刚好超出我阈值的东西，并持续这样做，就像举重一样，为了练就肌肉，不断地破坏它、重建它，一遍又一遍，因为这正是塑造我想要成为的那种人的性格特质。

sentences.en: And so when I'm going through those like really harder times, I like to think of Like looking in my mental mirror of like, I'm making you, I'm not there yet, but I'm making you.
sentences.zh: 所以，当我经历那些非常艰难的时刻时，我喜欢在脑海中的镜子里看着自己，对自己说：我正在塑造你，虽然还没到那一步，但我正在塑造你。

sentences.en: And that has helped me get through some of the harder times.
sentences.zh: 这帮助我度过了一些最艰难的时刻。

sentences.en: And from a gratitude perspective, my most powerful frame for gratitude has been thinking about my 85 year old self, waking up as my 30 year old self.
sentences.zh: 从感恩的角度来看，我最强大的感恩框架是想象我85岁时的自己，醒来时变成了30岁的我。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden looking at Layla and be like, man, I remember when we were this young and then looking out the window and be like, man, And Vegas wasn't even developed.
sentences.zh: 突然间看着Layla，心想：天哪，我记得我们年轻的时候。然后看向窗外，心想：天哪，那时候Vegas还没开发呢。

sentences.en: There's no flying cars yet. Man, they still used gas.
sentences.zh: 还没有飞行汽车。天哪，他们那时候还在用汽油。

sentences.en: This is so cool. And I get out of bed and I'm like, man, my elbows don't hurt.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。我从床上起来，心想：天哪，我的手肘不疼。

sentences.en: My knees don't hurt, right? Because I'm thinking about what my 85-year-old self would think.
sentences.zh: 我的膝盖也不疼，对吧？因为我在想我85岁时会怎么想。

sentences.en: And we're talking about whatever. But it allows me to enjoy the mundane in a way that I know that I would give everything that I had when I was 85 to enjoy again.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论什么都无所谓。但这让我能以一种我知道自己85岁时会付出一切来重温的方式，去享受当下的平凡。

sentences.en: And it's a trippy frame. But if you can think, what would 85-year-old me would be like, my body doesn't hurt. know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 这是一种很奇妙的思维框架。但如果你能去想，85岁的我会是什么样，我的身体不疼了，你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like I actually have energy. Like I can think clearly.
sentences.zh: 就像我真的有精力，我可以清晰地思考。

sentences.en: I don't have brain fog because I'm 85. Right.
sentences.zh: 我没有脑雾，因为我才85岁，对吧。

sentences.en: And that has been probably my single most powerful frame on feeling grateful and allowed me to feel more present at times when I start, like when I start to feel like I'm going through the motions and just like clicking in the routine and just like day after day after day, and they feel the same.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我感受感恩最强大的单一框架，它让我在开始觉得自己在走过场、陷入例行公事、日复一日感觉都一样的时候，能让我感到更加活在当下。

sentences.en: That's been my biggest slowdown where I can pull the reins and be like, just, and mind you, it lasts a few minutes.
sentences.zh: 这是我最大的减速带，我可以拉住缰绳，心想：等等。请注意，这只持续几分钟。

sentences.en: But when I think back on the days where I, when I use that frame, the part of the day that I remember is just the few minutes that I use it.
sentences.zh: 但当我回想那些日子，当我使用那个框架时，我记得的那部分时间，就是我使用它的那几分钟。

sentences.en: So I did this episode with Sam Harris. A lot of people have problems with Sam Harris.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了这期和Sam Harris的节目。很多人对Sam Harris有意见。

sentences.en: I found the time that I spent with him unbelievably enjoyable.
sentences.zh: 但我发现我和他在一起的时间非常愉快。

sentences.en: I sat opposite him and a couple of times caught myself thinking, I am having so much fun doing this.
sentences.zh: 我坐在他对面，好几次发现自己在想：做这件事我真的太开心了。

sentences.en: And he said this thing, and I really wish that I'd asked him another question.
sentences.zh: 他说了那件事，我真希望当时能再问他一个问题。

sentences.en: I should email him about it.
sentences.zh: 我应该给他发邮件问问。

sentences.en: I was talking about presence and the importance of presence, and you could use it as a proxy for gratitude and he said that really what you're aiming to do is find small moments in the day when you just open up and realize what's happening right conor mcgregor won the featherweight title twice because he won the interim because aldo was injured right and then he won against aldo and somebody asked him what are you going to do differently this time again before the Aldo fight that you didn't do in the Mendez fight.
sentences.zh: 当时我们在谈论临在感以及临在感的重要性，你可以把它当作感恩的代名词，他说你真正想要做的是在一天中找到一些小瞬间，当你只是敞开心扉，意识到正在发生什么。Conor McGregor两次赢得羽量级冠军，因为他先赢了临时冠军，因为Aldo受伤了，对吧？然后他赢了Aldo。有人问他：这次在Aldo的比赛前，你有什么不同于Mendez那场比赛的做法？

sentences.en: He says, this time I'm going to be present.
sentences.zh: 他说：这次我要活在当下。

sentences.en: And there's this photo of him, and he stood like this at the weigh-in, and you've got this entire stadium in front of him, and he stood like that.
sentences.zh: 有一张他的照片，他在称重时就这样站着，面前是整个体育场，他就那样站着。

sentences.en: He said the first time he did it, he couldn't remember it because he was just drowning in what was next.
sentences.zh: 他说第一次他这样做的时候，他记不住了，因为他当时完全沉浸在接下来要发生的事情中。

sentences.en: And what I really loved that Sam said, and I think that you look at somebody that's a master meditator or you set yourself high bars for what it means to be mindful and you realize that you can be present with a sip of a coffee.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢Sam说的这一点，我想当你看到一个冥想大师，或者你为自己设定了很高的正念标准时，你会意识到你可以在喝一口咖啡时保持临在。

sentences.en: Okay, I can be present with this one sip of a coffee and then it like sand in your hands or like trying to remember a dream, it just evaporates, right?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我可以在喝这一口咖啡时保持临在，然后它就像手里的沙子，或者像试图记住一个梦，它就蒸发了，对吧？

sentences.en: Okay, well, what if your goal was just to try and get five of those a day?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你的目标只是每天尝试获得五个这样的瞬间呢？

sentences.en: What if that was it? What if being mindful was just five moments when you allow yourself to be where your feet are, where your feet are underneath you.
sentences.zh: 如果这就是目标呢？如果正念只是五个让你允许自己双脚着地的瞬间，双脚就在你身下。

sentences.en: And then what if you tried to just string like two of those together five times a day, like just this first sip.
sentences.zh: 然后如果你尝试每天五次把其中的两个瞬间串联起来呢，比如这第一口咖啡。

sentences.en: And then as I put it down the view out of the window, oh my God, like that's two things in one.
sentences.zh: 然后当我放下它时，看着窗外的风景，天哪，这一下子就是两件事。

sentences.en: And then I can do that five times. And if I'd asked him, I would have said, really is the path to just increase the frequency of the times that you are where your feet are underneath you.
sentences.zh: 然后我可以做五次。如果我当时问他，我会说，真正的道路是不是就是增加你双脚着地的频率？

sentences.en: And one of the cue that I love that I got from an embodiment coach is the times when you see in your peripheral vision, you're looking and the way that our vision actually works, you're focused so heavily on what's directly in front of you.
sentences.zh: 我从一位具身教练那里学到一个我很喜欢的提示，就是当你用余光看到东西的时候，你正在看，而我们的视觉实际上是这样工作的：你太专注于正前方的东西了。

sentences.en: If there's ever a time... when you see what's out here, you realize that it's impossible to see all of that and not be in the present moment because you've naturally just opened yourself up.
sentences.zh: 如果有什么时候……当你看到周围的东西时，你会意识到，如果不活在当下，是不可能看到所有这些的，因为你自然而然地敞开了自己。

sentences.en: And I love that cue. So during the times when I'm doing things, like that Sam episode, I'm like, the next question and there's millions of people watching it and all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢这个提示。所以当我在做事情的时候，比如那期Sam的节目，我在想：下一个问题，有数百万人看着，所有这些东西。

sentences.en: And there's this guy in front of me and he's super smart or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我面前有这个家伙，他超级聪明之类的。

sentences.en: This is fucking cool. Just that one moment.
sentences.zh: 这太酷了。就那一瞬间。

sentences.en: And that, when I look back on that episode, that's what I enjoyed.
sentences.zh: 当我回看那期节目时，我享受的就是那一刻。

sentences.en: That's what I enjoyed about it. So I think that being where your feet are underneath you and allowing yourself to open up and stringing those together largely allows you to enjoy being whilst you're in the process of becoming.
sentences.zh: 这就是我享受它的原因。所以我认为，双脚着地，允许自己敞开心扉并把这些瞬间串联起来，很大程度上能让你在追求目标的过程中享受当下的存在。

sentences.en: It's also interesting, those moments, you can capture a moment independent from your surroundings.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那些瞬间，你可以捕捉到一个独立于你周围环境的时刻。

sentences.en: Because a lot of times those moments, you're not thinking about the goal that you have, the meeting that you have, the prep that you have to do for some talk or some podcast or whatever it is. and I can't remember where I heard this, but they were talking about Gladiator, the movie, and the film opens with this like little bird on a bow, right?
sentences.zh: 因为很多时候在那些瞬间，你并没有在想你的目标、你的会议、你为某个演讲或播客所做的准备，或者其他任何事情。我不记得是在哪里听到的，但他们谈论了电影《角斗士》，电影开头是树枝上的一只小鸟，对吧？

sentences.en: With like the leaves and whatnot. And then they zoom out from that little bird on the, on the, on the bow.
sentences.zh: 带着叶子之类的。然后他们从小鸟身上拉远镜头。

sentences.en: And it's this disgusting war scene, right?
sentences.zh: 那是一个令人作呕的战争场景，对吧？

sentences.en: And so it's kind of like micro, macro, micro, um, of how, no matter how tough whatever the moment that you're going through is, if you can just take a picture of the corner of the room and look at the beauty in that, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这有点像微观、宏观、微观，无论你正在经历的时刻有多艰难，如果你能拍下房间的一个角落，看看其中的美，对吧？

sentences.en: Of being present in that moment, even if it's the suffering, right?
sentences.zh: 在那个时刻保持临在，即使是在痛苦中，对吧？

sentences.en: Like you get punched and you're spitting blood out, but it's like this moment that you capture, then all of a sudden like everything fades away and you are present.
sentences.zh: 就像你被打了一拳，吐着血，但如果你能捕捉到那一刻，突然间一切都消失了，你就在当下。

sentences.en: And so it can take this, what would be a brutal war scene of death and dismemberment.
sentences.zh: 所以它可以把这本来是一个残酷的死亡和肢解的战争场景。

sentences.en: And the thing that makes it memorable is the zooming in on a detail.
sentences.zh: 让它变得令人难忘的是对细节的放大。

sentences.en: And so it's like, if you feel like you're going through life too fast, it's like, just look for a detail.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你觉得生活节奏太快，那就去寻找一个细节。

sentences.en: Whenever I wanted to try and get myself back into the present, I used to have brain fog a lot in my twenties.
sentences.zh: 每当我想让自己回到当下时，我二十多岁时经常有脑雾。

sentences.en: And maybe not brain fog, maybe just the clarity of my thoughts now is so much better than it used to be.
sentences.zh: 也许不是脑雾，也许只是我现在思维的清晰度比过去好多了。

sentences.en: I don't fucking know. Maybe it was just the drugs.
sentences.zh: 我他妈不知道。也许只是因为药物。

sentences.en: I don't know. But But one of the things I used to have this, I still have this BMW sat on my drive with a perforated steering wheel.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。但我曾经有这个，我那辆宝马现在还停在车道上，方向盘是打孔的。

sentences.en: And I remember that if I ran my thumbs across the steering wheel and I really felt the perforation, really felt it, or I'd do it with a leaf.
sentences.zh: 我记得如果我用拇指划过方向盘，真的去感受那些孔洞，真的去感受它，或者我用一片叶子这样做。

sentences.en: I'd pick a leaf up and I'd really feel the sensation of the leaf.
sentences.zh: 我捡起一片叶子，真的去感受叶子的触感。

sentences.en: I couldn't think about anything else. You can only have one thought at one time.
sentences.zh: 我就没法想别的事情了。你一次只能有一个念头。

sentences.en: You cannot think two things, right? You have a supercomputer inside of your head and it's got one megabyte of RAM.
sentences.zh: 你不能同时想两件事，对吧？你的大脑里有一个超级计算机，但它只有1MB的内存。

sentences.en: So just think the one thought. This next one, me and you text each other pretty frequently about, we've seen this cool thing and someone's repurposed one of the things that we've done, which is cool.
sentences.zh: 所以只去想那一个念头。接下来这个，我和你经常互发短信讨论，我们看到了这个很酷的东西，有人重新利用了我们做过的事情，这很酷。

sentences.en: And it makes me feel good that things that we've said, or that you've said largely, get repurposed.
sentences.zh: 这让我感觉很好，我们说过的话，或者你主要说过的话，被重新利用了。

sentences.en: This is something that hadn't happened before, which is you misquoted me, but improved the quote.
sentences.zh: 这是以前没发生过的事情，就是你引用错了我的话，但改进了那句引语。

sentences.en: So this was like the human centipede of content creation.
sentences.zh: 这就像内容创作界的《人体蜈蚣》。

sentences.en: And then I named it. So this is fame's seesaw. when you're on your way up everyone roots for you because you remind them of their dreams when you're at the top everyone tears you down because you remind them that they gave up on them and you have one which is for anyone who needs a reminder no one is going to hate on you for doing worse than them and this is interesting because kind of like the challenges you face in the beginning you don't have anything to say no to therefore the woman in the red dress is easy to say no to or there are fewer women this is a challenge that nobody is going to give you any sympathy for.
sentences.zh: 然后我给它命名了。这就是名声的跷跷板：当你处于上升期时，每个人都为你加油，因为你让他们想起了自己的梦想；当你处于巅峰时，每个人都把你拉下来，因为你提醒了他们，他们已经放弃了自己的梦想。你有一个观点，就是给任何需要提醒的人：没有人会因为你做得比他们差而讨厌你。这很有趣，因为就像你刚开始面临的挑战一样，你没有什么需要拒绝的，因此红裙女郎很容易拒绝，或者说女人更少了，这是一个没人会同情你的挑战。

sentences.en: It's a very unique category of challenge because the total addressable market for sympathy is basically zero.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常独特的挑战类别，因为同情的潜在市场几乎为零。

sentences.en: Because almost everybody is on their way up and very few people are at the top.
sentences.zh: 因为几乎每个人都在上升的路上，很少有人在巅峰。

sentences.en: And the people that are at the top are seen as having a degree of privilege that almost legitimates you twisting the knife or you poking the finger.
sentences.zh: 而那些在巅峰的人被视为拥有某种特权，这几乎让你捅刀子或指指点点变得合理化了。

sentences.en: This is how public figures can have normal everyday people on Twitter say unspeakable, like heinous things to them, dehumanizing things because they do not see them as human. they don't see them as a person there is no person on the other side of this there is it's they're a representation they're a menagerie of of of ideas therefore i can say whatever i want to them because they're not they're not really a person but they are and the fact that before there is any status associated with tearing you down no one is incentivized to tear you down and you haven't changed fuck dude the lewis capaldi documentary i've watched this twice now no lewis capaldi is the singer scottish singer amazing dude really fascinating story suffering a lot with mental health makes this first album and billions billions of streams world tour phenomenal and he's playing songs that he wrote in 2017 and played in working men's pubs around scotland the same songs go to number one so not just that he's become better he's the same guy.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么公众人物在Twitter上会被普通人说出难以启齿的、令人发指的话，非人化的东西，因为他们不把他们看作人。他们不把他们看作一个人，对面没有一个人，他们只是一个代表，一个思想的集合体，所以我可以对他们说任何我想说的话，因为他们不是真正的人。但他们确实是人。事实上，在撕下你的标签带来任何地位之前，没有人有动力去撕下你，而你并没有改变。该死，Lewis Capaldi的纪录片，我已经看了两遍了。Lewis Capaldi是那位歌手，苏格兰歌手，很棒的家伙，非常迷人的故事，深受心理健康困扰，制作了第一张专辑，数十亿次的播放量，世界巡演，现象级。他唱的歌是他2017年写的，在苏格兰的工人酒吧里唱的。同样的歌变成了冠军单曲。所以不仅仅是他变得更好了，他还是同一个人。

sentences.en: The same guy. Maybe his production's improved.
sentences.zh: 同一个人。也许他的制作水平提高了。

sentences.en: Maybe his recording quality's improved. He's got better mastering and his voice coaching's got a bit better, but he's largely the same person.
sentences.zh: 也许他的录音质量提高了。他有了更好的母带处理，声乐指导也稍微好了一点，但他基本上还是同一个人。

sentences.en: He hasn't changed. And he has this quote halfway through and it really spoke to me and he said, fame doesn't change you.
sentences.zh: 他没有变。他在片中有一句引语，深深触动了我，他说：名声不会改变你。

sentences.en: It just changes everybody around you.
sentences.zh: 它只会改变你周围的所有人。

sentences.en: And that when you're on your way up, everyone roots for you because you remind them of their dreams.
sentences.zh: 当你处于上升期时，每个人都为你加油，因为你让他们想起了自己的梦想。

sentences.en: When you're at the top, everyone tears you down because you remind them that they gave up on them.
sentences.zh: 当你处于巅峰时，每个人都把你拉下来，因为你提醒了他们，他们已经放弃了自己的梦想。

sentences.en: That really, yeah, that spoke to me. I wrote an essay on this because I'm a...
sentences.zh: 那真的，是的，那触动了我。我为此写了一篇文章，因为我是一个……

sentences.en: Psychopath? Yeah. When I was a gym owner.
sentences.zh: 精神病患者？是的。当我还是健身房老板的时候。

sentences.en: So a lot of people don't know this, but I got a writing scholarship in college.
sentences.zh: 很多人不知道这一点，但我大学时拿到了写作奖学金。

sentences.en: I was a vice president of the newspaper.
sentences.zh: 我是校报的副主编。

sentences.en: I was editor of the creative writing magazine.
sentences.zh: 我是创意写作杂志的编辑。

sentences.en: So I've been writing for a long time. I enjoy writing.
sentences.zh: 所以我写作已经很久了。我喜欢写作。

sentences.en: And I wrote this essay. I said, I think the title of it was, um, everyone believes in the American dream until it comes true.
sentences.zh: 我写了那篇文章。我想标题大概是，《每个人都相信美国梦，直到它成真》。

sentences.en: And I remember because what had happened was everybody, when I, when I was sleeping on the gym floor, right?
sentences.zh: 我记得是因为当时发生的事情是，每个人，当我睡在健身房地板上的时候，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, you know, I was the, I was the underdog and everyone, you know, my clients were all like, oh, good for you.
sentences.zh: 我是个失败者，每个人，我的客户都说：哦，为你高兴。

sentences.en: You know, you're going after your dream.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在追求你的梦想。

sentences.en: They'd see my blanket and my pillow in the corner of the gym and they knew I was sleeping there.
sentences.zh: 他们看到我在健身房角落里的毯子和枕头，他们知道我睡在那里。

sentences.en: And it was evident, you know, I, I, I lived there.
sentences.zh: 这很明显，我住在那里。

sentences.en: Um, I didn't have a shower. I didn't have a shower to go to the YMCA to go shower.
sentences.zh: 我没有淋浴间。我没有淋浴间，得去YMCA洗澡。

sentences.en: And everybody was like pro me. And then people come in, they sign up like, I'm going to support you.
sentences.zh: 每个人都支持我。然后人们进来，注册说：我要支持你。

sentences.en: And then within nine months, I had hired people and I had a manager and I pulled up and I remember I walked in the lobby and all the same people were like, ah, boss man's here.
sentences.zh: 然后在九个月内，我雇了人，我有了经理，我开车过来，我记得我走进大厅，所有同样的人都说：啊，老板来了。

sentences.en: Oh, you're not too good for us now. And I remember being so jarred by the experience.
sentences.zh: 哦，你现在觉得我们配不上你了。我记得那次经历让我非常震惊。

sentences.en: And I was like, you guys rooted for me. And I was like, and now I did what you said you were rooting for me to do.
sentences.zh: 我说：你们以前为我加油。现在我做了你们说你们支持我去做的事情。

sentences.en: And that was when I realized that people want you to do well, but not better than them.
sentences.zh: 那时我意识到，人们希望你过得好，但不能比他们好。

sentences.en: And I was like, I had gone from underdog to the man.
sentences.zh: 我从失败者变成了大人物。

sentences.en: And I was like, when does that happen? And the litmus test of when it happens is it depends on who the person is.
sentences.zh: 我心想：这是什么时候发生的？而判断它何时发生的试金石取决于那个人是谁。

sentences.en: Because for the person who was working at my gym, who was a janitor or a cleaner, it happened really quick, right?
sentences.zh: 因为对于那个在我健身房工作的清洁工来说，这发生得很快，对吧？

sentences.en: For the people who were more successful, it took longer.
sentences.zh: 对于那些更成功的人来说，这花的时间更长。

sentences.en: And then the only people at the end who would still root for me were the business owners who were doing way better than me, right?
sentences.zh: 最后唯一还会为我加油的人，是那些比我做得好得多的企业主，对吧？

sentences.en: Who were still members of my gym. And so that was a really interesting experience that happened when I was 23.
sentences.zh: 他们还是我健身房的会员。所以那是我23岁时发生的一次非常有趣的经历。

sentences.en: And that was the first time I went from underdog to the person that someone would want to attack.
sentences.zh: 那是我第一次从失败者变成了别人想要攻击的对象。

sentences.en: But I had a performance coach tell me this.
sentences.zh: 但我有一位表现教练告诉我这个。

sentences.en: He said, hatred isn't something you avoid.
sentences.zh: 他说：仇恨不是你需要避免的东西。

sentences.en: He said, it is a requisite for success. He said, if you get no hate, you are not successful.
sentences.zh: 他说：它是成功的必要条件。他说：如果你没有得到任何仇恨，你就没有成功。

sentences.en: And for some reason, that just really stuck with me because rather than it being this thing that I was trying to avoid, it actually became a leading indicator or an indicator that I was on the right path in achieving things.
sentences.zh: 出于某种原因，这真的深深印在了我的脑海里，因为与其把它当作我试图避免的东西，它实际上变成了一个领先指标，或者说是一个我正在实现目标的正确道路上的指标。

sentences.en: And so I think that's why, I mean, I don't want to toot horns or anything.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这就是为什么，我的意思是，我不想自吹自擂。

sentences.en: But in terms of like my ability to deal with the naysayers and things like that, I feel like I'm pretty good at it.
sentences.zh: 但在处理反对者之类的事情上，我觉得我做得还不错。

sentences.en: Like it doesn't really bug me very much.
sentences.zh: 这真的不会太困扰我。

sentences.en: And I think in large part, it was because of how it's framed, at least how, you know, in this discussion, how it was framed for me early on, which is that no one hates you from above.
sentences.zh: 我认为在很大程度上，是因为它的框架，至少在这次讨论中，它是如何在我早期被构建的，那就是没有人会从高处恨你。

sentences.en: And even, you know, even when I think back about like the bullies and whatnot that you had earlier, like even in middle school, like there were things that I had that were going for me that I couldn't recognize.
sentences.zh: 即使当我回想起你之前提到的那些欺凌者之类的，即使在初中，我身上也有一些我无法识别的优势。

sentences.en: Cause of course, everything that comes easy to you are things that they're easy to you.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，所有对你来说容易的事情，你都觉得它们很容易。

sentences.en: So you don't think that they're, you know, new or interesting or cool.
sentences.zh: 所以你不会认为它们是新的、有趣的或酷的。

sentences.en: And, but like, at the same time, I was like, I'd advanced a grade in multiple, in multiple subjects.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我当时在多个科目上跳级。

sentences.en: I had straight A's. I worked really hard.
sentences.zh: 我成绩全A。我工作非常努力。

sentences.en: I was in shape, right? But I had these people who would hate.
sentences.zh: 我身材很好，对吧？但我有那些会恨我的人。

sentences.en: But you internalize it, but now I can look back and be like, it's kind of like the parents were like, it's because she's into you, right?
sentences.zh: 你把它内化了，但现在我可以回过头来看，就像父母说的那样：那是因为她喜欢你，对吧？

sentences.en: No, it might not be the same that way. But just thinking about it as an indicator that the hate is actually the light that you're on the right path. we spoke about this last time that nothing is going to be worthwhile that doesn't come with an associated amount of discomfort therefore when you start to feel friends around you and the people that you used to be able to speak a common language with start to push back and start to make the quips of oh not drinking tonight yeah oh you must be too cool for us now i know it hurts I know it hurts that is the lead indicator not even the lagging indicator that is the lead indicator that you are doing the right thing and lots of people listen to this podcast I get messages from people like hey man I'm a 22 year old rugby player from the northwest of the UK I live in Cumbria none of my friends understand me I want to do personal growth I don't want to live in the UK and when I listen to modern wisdom I feel less alone and it makes me tear up because I'm like fuck I see me in that person I see me in that.
sentences.zh: 不，可能不完全是那样。但只要把它看作一个指标，说明仇恨实际上是你走在正确道路上的光。我们上次谈到过，没有任何值得做的事情是不伴随着一定程度的不适的。因此，当你开始感觉到周围的朋友，那些你曾经能用共同语言交流的人开始反击，开始说些俏皮话，比如：哦，今晚不喝酒了？哦，你现在一定觉得我们配不上你了。我知道这很痛，我知道这很痛，但那是领先指标，甚至不是滞后指标，那是你正在做正确事情的领先指标。很多人听这个播客，我收到人们的消息说：嘿，伙计，我是来自英国西北部的一名22岁橄榄球运动员，我住在坎布里亚，我的朋友们都不理解我。我想进行个人成长，我不想住在英国。当我听《Modern Wisdom》时，我感到不那么孤独了。这让我热泪盈眶，因为我心想：该死，我在那个人身上看到了我自己。

sentences.en: And it's so hard to reframe it. The pushback you are getting is the indicator that you are doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 重新构建它太难了。你得到的反击是你正在做正确事情的指标。

sentences.en: It is. And if you can reframe the distaste that you get from other people as the same as that.
sentences.zh: 确实是。如果你能把从别人那里得到的厌恶重新构建成同样的东西。

sentences.en: Because they're projecting the things that they know they should be doing that you are doing that they're not doing.
sentences.zh: 因为他们是在投射那些他们知道自己应该做而你正在做、他们却没做的事情。

sentences.en: And you remind them of that. And so it's that it's even, so even though the mountain that you're climbing is actually a smaller one than the one that you ultimately want to climb, you're actually at the top of their mountain.
sentences.zh: 你提醒了他们这一点。所以，即使你正在攀登的山峰实际上比你最终想要攀登的山峰要小，你实际上已经站在了他们的山顶上。

sentences.en: And so they start tearing you down. So like, that's where the underdog story that we said, the very beginning of this with the quote, which is like on the way up, they root for you.
sentences.zh: 所以他们开始把你拉下来。所以，这就是我们开头引用的那个失败者故事，也就是：在上升的路上，他们为你加油。

sentences.en: And then when you're at the top, they try and tear you down because you remind them of the dreams that they couldn't accomplish.
sentences.zh: 然后当你处于巅峰时，他们试图把你拉下来，因为你提醒了他们那些他们无法实现的梦想。

sentences.en: Right. And so you quitting drinking, or you staying in to work on your side hustle or your project or the business that you want to launch the podcast, that might be, you might be at the top of their mountain.
sentences.zh: 对。所以你戒酒，或者你留下来为你的副业、你的项目、你想推出的业务或播客工作，你可能已经站在了他们的山顶上。

sentences.en: And so they are tearing you down because now you remind them that they haven't done it.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把你拉下来，因为现在你提醒了他们，他们还没有做到。

sentences.en: And it's purely a projection of them onto you and has nothing to do with you.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是他们对你的投射，与你无关。

sentences.en: And that, I hope that that comforts someone.
sentences.zh: 我希望这能安慰到某个人。

sentences.en: Because what you said, I think is like, if you're going through that right now, and like, and I promise you, every single person who wants to do something with their life and has done something with their life has gone through the exact chapter that you're going through.
sentences.zh: 因为你所说的，我认为是：如果你现在正在经历这些，我向你保证，每一个想在生活中做点什么并已经做成点什么的人，都经历过你现在正在经历的这一章。

sentences.en: And it's the lonely chapter. It's the chapter where you don't fit in with your own friends, but you don't have the outcomes yet to fit into a new group of friends.
sentences.zh: 这是孤独的一章。这是你与自己的朋友不再合拍，但还没有取得成果去融入新朋友圈的一章。

sentences.en: And you're doing this thing. You're consuming content on the internet.
sentences.zh: 你正在做这件事。你在互联网上消费内容。

sentences.en: You're doing these free tutorials online to try and figure out how to set up a podcast and where do I host this thing?
sentences.zh: 你在网上做这些免费教程，试图弄清楚如何建立一个播客，我在哪里托管这个东西？

sentences.en: And you're going through this and you're like, is this even worth it?
sentences.zh: 你正在经历这些，心想：这真的值得吗？

sentences.en: Because you have no signs of success, right?
sentences.zh: 因为你没有任何成功的迹象，对吧？

sentences.en: But if there's anything that you can take away from what we're saying right now is that the sign of success is the hate that you get along the way.
sentences.zh: 但如果说你能从我们现在所说的话中得到什么，那就是成功的标志就是你一路上得到的仇恨。

sentences.en: And what you can't do is bend the knee to their hate and fit back into the conformity because it's comfortable and it's warm.
sentences.zh: 你不能做的是向他们的仇恨屈膝，回到那种从众中去，因为那样很舒服，很温暖。

sentences.en: Because like in the matrix, when Trinity opens the door, when, when Neo is about to go take the red pill and he wants to get out of the car, she says, Neo, you've been down that road and you know exactly where it leads.
sentences.zh: 就像在《黑客帝国》里，当Trinity打开门时，当Neo准备去吃红色药丸，他想下车时，她说：Neo，你走过那条路，你知道它通向哪里。

sentences.en: And I know that's not where you want to be.
sentences.zh: 我知道那不是你想去的地方。

sentences.en: And then he closes the door. Like right now, this moment that you're going through is Trinity opening the door and being like, you could go back, but then you'd have to remember exactly what the reason was that you decided not to go out to begin with, just because you listen to this podcast and you consume this content.
sentences.zh: 然后他关上了门。就像现在，你正在经历的这一刻就是Trinity打开门，好像在说：你可以回去，但那样你就必须记住你当初决定不走出去的真正原因。仅仅因为你听了这个播客，你消费了这个内容。

sentences.en: You're like, I can fucking do more than this.
sentences.zh: 你心想：我他妈能做的比这更多。

sentences.en: Like, because you are starting to live in some of that, how are you look in the mirror and you're like, I can do more.
sentences.zh: 因为你开始活在其中的一部分里，你看着镜子，心想：我能做得更多。

sentences.en: And you start to see the person that you could be.
sentences.zh: 你开始看到你可以成为的那个人。

sentences.en: And you're like, this does start to feel like hell.
sentences.zh: 你心想：这真的开始感觉像地狱了。

sentences.en: The reason that it's uncomfortable. And the reason that I do have sympathy for the people that see this is ignorance in some regards is bliss.
sentences.zh: 它不舒服的原因，以及我确实同情那些看到这一点的人的原因，在某种程度上是无知是福。

sentences.en: As soon as you begin to posit an ideal, you then begin to compare yourself to that ideal.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始提出一个理想，你就会开始拿自己与那个理想进行比较。

sentences.en: And the gap in potential between you and the person that you could have been begins to get more stark.
sentences.zh: 你与你本可以成为的人之间的潜力差距开始变得更加鲜明。

sentences.en: And even the slightest glimmer of, wow, I can read a book or follow a course or listen to a podcast and then work really, really hard on one thing and change the thermodynamics of my mind, change the texture of my own existence day to day because I worked at a thing.
sentences.zh: 甚至是一丝微光，哇，我可以读一本书，或者参加一个课程，或者听一个播客，然后在一件事上非常非常努力，改变我思维的热力学，改变我日常存在的质感，因为我致力于一件事。

sentences.en: And now I understand nutrition. I know Kung Fu.
sentences.zh: 现在我了解营养学了。我知道功夫了。

sentences.en: I understand nutrition or I understand how to sleep well.
sentences.zh: 我了解营养学，或者我了解如何睡个好觉。

sentences.en: Okay. As soon as you know that sleep is important and what you need to do to do it, every single night of bad sleep that you have is on you.
sentences.zh: 好吧。一旦你知道睡眠很重要，以及你需要做什么来做到这一点，你每一个糟糕的睡眠夜晚都是你自己的责任。

sentences.en: Because before you had the excuse that you're ignorant.
sentences.zh: 因为之前你有无知的借口。

sentences.en: And guess what? Now you don't.
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？现在你没有了。

sentences.en: Every worthwhile goal is worthwhile because it has a cost associated with it.
sentences.zh: 每一个有价值的目标之所以有价值，是因为它伴随着代价。

sentences.en: And so the cost that you're going through is what makes the goal worthwhile to begin with.
sentences.zh: 所以你正在经历的代价，正是让这个目标从一开始就值得的原因。

sentences.en: Because if what you were setting out to do were immediately available to you, then it would mean it would be immediately available to everyone, which means it wouldn't be worthwhile.

sentences.en: You're a genetic dead end and eat shit. Is that a bad thing?
sentences.zh: 你就是基因的死胡同，活该倒霉。这是件坏事吗？

sentences.en: According to them.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来是。

sentences.en: So, okay. I'm going to zoom out real quick.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我快速跳出来谈谈。

sentences.en: I know we're going to go on this. Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们要聊这个。是的是的。

sentences.en: So if we're looking at a species, right?
sentences.zh: 如果我们观察一个物种，对吧？

sentences.en: Let's look at deer. A lot of people have deer in their backyard, right?
sentences.zh: 来看看鹿。很多人后院都有鹿，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, what is natural is that one buck inseminates 50 doe and he competes with all the other deer.
sentences.zh: 自然界的情况是，一只雄鹿会让50只雌鹿受孕，它会与其他所有雄鹿竞争。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is because then it actually allows the quote best genes to proliferate.
sentences.zh: 这样做的原因，是为了让所谓的“最优基因”得以繁衍。

sentences.en: Now, best is determined by what actually continues on.
sentences.zh: 而“最优”是由什么能延续下去来决定的。

sentences.en: Getting perilously close to eugenics here, Alex.
sentences.zh: Alex，你这快要谈到优生学了。

sentences.en: Well, I'm just talking about deer. I'm just talking about deer.
sentences.zh: 我只是在谈论鹿。我只是在谈论鹿而已。

sentences.en: I'm just talking about deer. I'm not saying this is what it should be, but the point that I wanted to make was not, I think, where everyone thinks I'm going with this, which is that a lot of the black, whatever you just said, right, black pill, I would imagine are casting an expectation on the universe that it shouldn't be this way.
sentences.zh: 我只是在谈论鹿。我并不是说这就是人类应该有的样子，但我想表达的重点，我想并不是大家以为的那样，而是说很多信奉“黑药丸”之类观点的人，他们对宇宙抱有一种不该有的期待。

sentences.en: Why not? And this is exactly like the hater who says, you're not going to amount to anything.
sentences.zh: 为什么不该有？这就像那些喷子说“你一事无成”一样。

sentences.en: And the reason that it hurts is because you're like, what if they're right?
sentences.zh: 之所以会感到受伤，是因为你在想：万一他们说对了呢？

sentences.en: And then like staring at the mirror with that question of like, what if they're right?
sentences.zh: 然后对着镜子问自己：万一他们说对了呢？

sentences.en: What if I am out of shape? because the thing is that in order to be the top quote 1% or even the top 10% or even just above average you just need to not be overweight you need to not be overweight you need to be gainfully employed the bar is so low the bar is so unbelievably low I got this idea I got to teach you about the alpha history fantasy modern men who are angry at a world they feel has rejected them mistakenly believe that they would have somehow done better in medieval times.
sentences.zh: 万一我真的身材走样了呢？因为事实是，想要进入所谓的前1%，甚至前10%，或者仅仅是高于平均水平，你只需要不超重，你需要有份正经工作，门槛真的太低了，低到令人难以置信。我有个想法，我得教教你关于“阿尔法历史幻想”的事，那些对世界感到愤怒的现代男性，错误地认为如果生在古代，他们会过得更好。

sentences.en: They are adamant that the chance of them being Genghis Khan is greater than the chance of them being cannon fodder peasant number 1,373,000 whose favela was sacked and destroyed.
sentences.zh: 他们坚信自己成为成吉思汗的几率，要大于成为第137万3000个被洗劫并摧毁家园的炮灰农民的几率。

sentences.en: And it's this wistfulness for the past. And dude, I get it.
sentences.zh: 这是一种对过去的怀旧。伙计，我懂。

sentences.en: If you feel lost and alone and nobody understands you and you've been forgotten and things shouldn't be this way, guess what?
sentences.zh: 如果你感到迷茫、孤独，没人理解你，觉得自己被遗忘了，觉得事情不该是这样，猜猜怎么着？

sentences.en: They've always been this way. And right now, the bar has never been set lower.
sentences.zh: 事情一直都是这样。而现在，门槛从未像现在这样低。

sentences.en: If you have the opportunity to sit down and listen to me and Alex waffle on for three and a half hours, you have the capacity, the conscientiousness, the wherewithal to be able to go out tomorrow and take one thing. that you've hit from today this is this is something that i want you to get onto which which i think is important which is oh sorry go avoiding the mental masturbation you know we can do this thing and and like speed fuck quotes into the ether and like a like an uzi right just unloading all of these different things and i think that a lot of people feel uh a general overwhelm of indexing of information and oh my god i'm learning all of this stuff and i don't feel like I'm making any progress.
sentences.zh: 如果你有机会坐下来听我和Alex胡扯三个半小时，你就具备了能力、责任感和资源，明天就可以去采取行动，哪怕只是从今天的内容里挑出一件事。这是我想让你去做的，我认为这很重要，抱歉，我是说要避免那种“精神自慰”。你知道，我们可以做这种事，像乌兹冲锋枪一样把各种语录喷向虚空，而我认为很多人感到被信息淹没了，觉得“天哪，我学了这么多东西，却感觉不到任何进步”。

sentences.en: And I really wanted to try and cut through this at some point in the conversation today as well, which is Tim Ferriss has an idea called the good shit sticks.
sentences.zh: 我今天在谈话中也确实想找个机会打破这种状态，那就是Tim Ferriss的一个观点：真正的好东西会留下。

sentences.en: All right. I, when I first started out on this journey of personal growth, felt guilty because I didn't have a perfectly curated Evernote external brain with nested folders and all of my book summaries.
sentences.zh: 好吧。我刚开始个人成长之旅时，曾感到内疚，因为我没有一个完美整理的Evernote外部大脑，没有嵌套文件夹，也没有所有的书籍摘要。

sentences.en: And I was supposed to keep all of this thing and how am I going to remember it and blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 我本以为我得记住所有这些东西，我该怎么记住它等等。

sentences.en: Five and a bit years later, people come up to me and ask, one of the most common questions I get asked is how the fuck do you remember all of the things that you remember?
sentences.zh: 五年多过去了，人们走过来问我，我被问到最多的问题之一就是：你到底是怎么记住所有这些东西的？

sentences.en: Two things. First off, I don't remember anything that I don't care about.
sentences.zh: 两点。首先，我不关心的东西，我什么都不会记。

sentences.en: And the second thing, massive amounts of exposure.
sentences.zh: 第二点，海量的接触。

sentences.en: Those are the only two things that are going on.
sentences.zh: 只有这两点在起作用。

sentences.en: I've done 670 podcasts in five years for hours.
sentences.zh: 五年里我做了670期播客，每期几个小时。

sentences.en: And all of the reading I had to do beforehand and all of the listening i had to do beforehand as well and i didn't stress myself about what i had to remember so if you listen to this three and a bit hour podcast and you go they talked they said a lot of words there alex said a lot of words chris said a lot of words what's the one thing that you couldn't stop thinking about and there may be nothing fair play we failed if there's one thing that you can't stop thinking about that story about the kid from cumbria that time when Alex had to drive across the country.
sentences.zh: 还有我之前必须做的所有阅读和听力，我并没有因为必须记住什么而给自己压力。所以如果你听了这三个多小时的播客，觉得他们说了好多话，Alex说了好多，Chris说了好多，那么有什么是你无法停止思考的呢？可能什么都没有，那也公平。如果我们失败了，但如果有一件事是你无法停止思考的，比如那个坎布里亚孩子的故事，或者Alex开车横穿全国的那次经历。

sentences.en: That's the thing. That is the thing. And allowing yourself to naturally select whatever the most important learning is from the content that you consume is the best way to work out what is going to resonate.
sentences.zh: 那就是重点。就是那个东西。允许自己从消费的内容中自然筛选出最重要的学习内容，是找出什么能引起共鸣的最好方法。

sentences.en: And it's the best way to act on it as well.
sentences.zh: 这也是付诸行动的最好方法。

sentences.en: If you can't stop thinking about it when you go to bed tonight and you can't stop telling your friends about it in the morning and you've clipped it from this podcast or any other podcast, any other book or whatever, whatever the thing is that you keep sending photos of and you keep on reciting to people and you try and tell your mom about it and she doesn't care.
sentences.zh: 如果你今晚睡觉时无法停止思考它，明天早上无法停止告诉你的朋友，并且你把它从这期播客或其他任何播客、书籍中剪辑下来，无论是什么，只要是你不断发送照片、不断向人复述、试图告诉妈妈但她并不关心的事情。

sentences.en: That is the thing that you need to work on.
sentences.zh: 那才是你需要去钻研的东西。

sentences.en: And you don't need to do, if you take half a thing from this podcast or any other podcast that, and you work on it for a month, you have made so much progress.
sentences.zh: 你不需要做太多，如果你能从这期或其他播客里学到半个点，并为此努力一个月，你就已经取得了巨大的进步。

sentences.en: And do you understand how blessed you are to have this opportunity?
sentences.zh: 你明白你拥有这个机会是多么幸运吗？

sentences.en: You could have been born in the middle ages before the Gutenberg printing press when they wouldn't even give you the Bible in the common language so that you had to go through the priest to be able to have a relationship with God.
sentences.zh: 你本可能出生在中世纪，在古腾堡印刷机发明之前，那时他们甚至不给你提供母语版的圣经，你必须通过牧师才能与上帝建立联系。

sentences.en: Right now, you can search for whatever it is that you're dealing with, find the greatest minds on the planet, listen to them, and then the next day implement it and you move not only yourself, but you move the world around you.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可以搜索任何你正在处理的问题，找到地球上最伟大的头脑，听取他们的建议，然后在第二天付诸实践，你不仅改变了自己，还改变了你周围的世界。

sentences.en: You get to nudge yourself and the rest of the world in a direction that you want to go and you get to feel proud about it and it's within your control.
sentences.zh: 你可以推动自己和周围的世界朝着你想要的方向前进，你可以为此感到自豪，而且这一切都在你的掌控之中。

sentences.en: You have never been more blessed.
sentences.zh: 你从未如此幸运过。

sentences.en: There's a quote that I want to hit here that I think would be relevant to what we were just talking about with the people who were sad and alone.
sentences.zh: 我想引用一句话，我认为这与我们刚才谈论的那些悲伤和孤独的人有关。

sentences.en: And one of the biggest breakthroughs that I had from a mental perspective was actually defining emotions for what they are operationally.
sentences.zh: 我从心理层面获得的最大突破之一，实际上是定义了情绪的运作方式。

sentences.en: So sadness comes from a lack of options, or rather a lack of perceived options.
sentences.zh: 悲伤源于缺乏选择，或者说缺乏感知到的选择。

sentences.en: And that's why it feels like hopelessness, because you don't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么它感觉像绝望，因为你不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: But when I realized that sadness meant that I didn't know what to do, it meant that another way that I could define sadness was ignorance.
sentences.zh: 但当我意识到悲伤意味着我不知道该怎么办时，意味着我可以把悲伤定义为“无知”。

sentences.en: And that is solvable. And so whenever I feel sad now, it's been my trigger to immediately think, What do I not know?
sentences.zh: 而这是可以解决的。所以每当我感到悲伤时，它就成了我的触发点，让我立刻去想：我不知道什么？

sentences.en: What option do I not see? Because the opposite of that is anxiety, which is you have many options and you have few priorities.
sentences.zh: 我没看到什么选择？因为它的反面是焦虑，即你有很多选择，但优先级很少。

sentences.en: You have many paths that you could pursue and you just don't know which one.
sentences.zh: 你有很多可以追求的道路，但你只是不知道选哪一条。

sentences.en: And so being able to operationalize what these emotions felt like.
sentences.zh: 所以能够将这些情绪运作化（operationalize）是很重要的。

sentences.en: So if you feel sad, it just means that you need to go learn more and that you can do.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你感到悲伤，那只是意味着你需要去学习更多，而这是你能做到的。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden the learning more becomes the option and then you don't need to feel sad anymore.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，学习更多就成了那个选择，你就不再需要感到悲伤了。

sentences.en: And that was like one of the biggest breakthroughs from my like mental health or whatever you want to call it, mindset, that set me free.
sentences.zh: 这就像是我在心理健康或无论你怎么称呼它——心态方面最大的突破之一，它让我获得了自由。

sentences.en: And I've taken a lot of effort to try and operationalize emotions so that I can either get out of them or lean into them.
sentences.zh: 我花了很多精力去尝试将情绪运作化，这样我就可以摆脱它们或利用它们。

sentences.en: So like patience, for example, right? I'm only bringing this up because I think it might be relevant to some people, is that most goals are attainable if you expand the time horizon, even enormous ones.
sentences.zh: 比如耐心，对吧？我提这个只是因为我认为它对某些人可能有意义，大多数目标只要你拉长时间跨度都是可以实现的，即使是巨大的目标。

sentences.en: Like you can do anything in 10 years. You could walk to the moon.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以在10年内做任何事。你可以走到月球。

sentences.en: You could do, there you go. You can do anything.
sentences.zh: 你可以做到，就是这样。你可以做任何事。

sentences.en: And so for me, I am, I would say a naturally impatient person.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，我是一个天生缺乏耐心的人。

sentences.en: I tend to want things immediately now. And you know what?
sentences.zh: 我倾向于想要立刻得到结果。你知道吗？

sentences.en: You probably are too. But once I defined patience as figuring out what to do in the meantime, it allowed me to control what I did.
sentences.zh: 你可能也是。但一旦我把耐心定义为“弄清楚在此期间该做什么”，它就让我能够控制自己的行为。

sentences.en: Because now, you and I are being patient for your stock investments.
sentences.zh: 因为现在，你和我正在为你的股票投资保持耐心。

sentences.en: Right now, as we're on this podcast, we're being patient for that because we're doing things in the meantime.
sentences.zh: 现在，当我们录制这期播客时，我们正在为此保持耐心，因为我们在此期间正在做其他事情。

sentences.en: And so whenever I felt impatient and wanted to change course, I had to just redefine what do I need to do today.
sentences.zh: 所以每当我感到不耐烦并想改变方向时，我只需要重新定义我今天需要做什么。

sentences.en: And if you are sad and impatient, then it means that right now you need to learn what the option is that you need to go pursue.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到悲伤和不耐烦，那就意味着你现在需要去学习你需要去追求的选择是什么。

sentences.en: And then that makes it very much under your control.
sentences.zh: 然后这就会让你感到一切尽在掌握。

sentences.en: And so step by step, each of these emotions over time, I spent a lot of time trying to define them out so that they no longer control me and I know how to solve them. and then now it just becomes a faster and faster muscle.
sentences.zh: 所以一步一步地，随着时间的推移，我花了很多时间去定义这些情绪，这样它们就不再控制我，我也知道如何去解决它们。现在，这已经变成了一种越来越熟练的肌肉记忆。

sentences.en: Like, oh, I feel anxiety. That means that I have many options that I don't have priorities.
sentences.zh: 比如，哦，我感到焦虑。这意味着我有太多的选择，却没有分清优先级。

sentences.en: Okay, what's my priority? And then all of a sudden, what used to take days of anxiety and feeling this frog in my throat was just, oh, I need to make a list of all the things that I'm looking at.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我的优先级是什么？突然之间，那些曾经需要几天时间来焦虑、让我如鲠在喉的事情，变成了：哦，我只需要把我关注的所有事情列个清单。

sentences.en: Which one's the most important? Ignore the rest.
sentences.zh: 哪一个最重要？忽略其余的。

sentences.en: And then I'm good. And what you just take days takes minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后我就搞定了。原本需要几天的事情，现在只需要几分钟。

sentences.en: One of yours is choosing the plan isn't hard.
sentences.zh: 你的一条原则是：选择计划并不难。

sentences.en: Doing the plan isn't hard. sticking to the plan is hard.
sentences.zh: 执行计划并不难。坚持计划才难。

sentences.en: Charlie Munger said, the money isn't made in the buy and it's not made in the sell.
sentences.zh: Charlie Munger 说过，赚钱不在于买入，也不在于卖出。

sentences.en: It's made in the wait.
sentences.zh: 而在于等待。

sentences.en: And that, like, I just feel like that's such an elegant way of thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这是一种非常优雅的思考方式。

sentences.en: It's like the hard part about the plan is sticking to the plan.
sentences.zh: 就像计划中最难的部分是坚持执行计划。

sentences.en: Like the plan wasn't bad. Your first plan was good because it's easy to go say, I'm going to work out three days a week for the next year.
sentences.zh: 计划本身并不坏。你的第一个计划是好的，因为说“我明年每周锻炼三次”很容易。

sentences.en: And it's a good plan. Pretty good plan. It's a pretty good plan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好计划。相当不错的计划。确实是个不错的计划。

sentences.en: And the interesting thing is that, like, a mediocre plan that's stuck to always outperforms an amazing and perfect plan that you never stick with to begin with.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，一个平庸但能坚持下去的计划，总是优于一个你从一开始就无法坚持的完美计划。

sentences.en: And I know this obviously from the fitness world, but it applies to everything.
sentences.zh: 我从健身领域显然明白这一点，但这适用于所有事情。

sentences.en: And so like the stick to it muscle is the one that you have to flex.
sentences.zh: 所以，“坚持下去”这种肌肉是你必须去锻炼的。

sentences.en: And that's why like, if you're going through things, especially in the earlier days, like I remember I used to start and stop and start and stop.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么如果你正在经历一些事情，特别是在早期，我记得我以前总是开始又停止，开始又停止。

sentences.en: And I tried this thing. I tried that thing.
sentences.zh: 我试过这个，试过那个。

sentences.en: It's normal because you haven't been reinforced enough of sticking with something, right?
sentences.zh: 这很正常，因为你还没有得到足够的反馈来坚持做某事，对吧？

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that you have to stick get out long enough that you get that first carrot, you get that first cookie.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，你必须坚持足够长的时间，直到你得到第一根胡萝卜，得到第一块饼干。

sentences.en: And then all of a sudden, everything that you did to get there, you're like, oh, more of that will get me more cookies.
sentences.zh: 然后突然之间，你为了达到目标所做的一切，你会觉得：哦，多做一点就能得到更多饼干。

sentences.en: And then it just becomes this self-perpetuating cycle and then you get addicted to work.
sentences.zh: 然后这就变成了一个自我强化的循环，你就对工作上瘾了。

sentences.en: Yes. And then you do a launch to 500,000 people and you lock yourself in a closet six hours a day for two years.
sentences.zh: 是的。然后你向50万人发布产品，每天把自己关在衣柜里工作六个小时，持续两年。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly that. Because I've been rewarded in the past because the first time I actually spent a lot of time on a presentation and I felt good when I walked on stage and didn't feel anxiety, I was like, oh, I want this every time.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是那样。因为我过去得到过奖励，第一次我确实花了很多时间准备演示，当我走上舞台时感觉很好，没有感到焦虑，我就想：哦，我每次都想要这种感觉。

sentences.en: And then I had the second thought, which is the much scarier thought, which is now I have to do this every time.
sentences.zh: 然后我有了第二个想法，这是一个更可怕的想法：现在我每次都必须做到这样。

sentences.en: This is the new bar. This is the new bar.
sentences.zh: 这是新的标准。这是新的标准。

sentences.en: I want to round out something on that sort of black pill side, which is...
sentences.zh: 我想在那种“黑色药丸”的一面补充一点，那就是……

sentences.en: If you listen to this and you think, must be nice or easy for you to say, I get it.
sentences.zh: 如果你听了这些，觉得“这对你来说肯定很好”或者“说起来容易”，我明白。

sentences.en: Like, I get it. And if you feel like there is something that you can't get over, some genetic, societal, cultural defect that means that you do not have the same ceiling that you think that you should or that other people appear to have, I get it.
sentences.zh: 我明白。如果你觉得有什么东西是你无法克服的，某种基因、社会或文化上的缺陷，意味着你没有你认为自己应该有的，或者别人看起来有的那种上限，我明白。

sentences.en: And the question I would ask is, what do you want?
sentences.zh: 而我会问的问题是：你想要什么？

sentences.en: Like, do you want sympathy? Because I will happily give you sympathy.
sentences.zh: 你是想要同情吗？因为我很乐意给你同情。

sentences.en: I know what it feels like to be someone that has no belief in themselves and that believes that you are fundamentally a loser and that nothing is going to come to you and that you deserve for nothing to come to you.
sentences.zh: 我知道那种对自己毫无信心、认为自己本质上是个失败者、认为什么都不会降临到自己身上、认为自己不配得到任何东西的感觉是什么样的。

sentences.en: I understand what that feels like. But what does that mindset get you?
sentences.zh: 我理解那种感觉。但那种心态能给你带来什么？

sentences.en: Like fundamentally, what does that mindset give you?
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，那种心态能给你什么？

sentences.en: Okay, so let's say that you have been dealt as difficult of a hand as possible.
sentences.zh: 好吧，假设你拿到了一手尽可能烂的牌。

sentences.en: And? Yeah. And to quote you to you, i can promise you that there is someone who has had it worse and has done it better i put this clip out a while ago this like just random talking about a morning routine thing and it was pretty basic but it went fucking interstellar and the real internet got a hold of it you know like not your fans but like the real internet like it got the general public internet got a hold of it the most common comment was something along the lines of tell me you don't have kids without telling me that you don't have kids which is must be easy for you to say i have a daughter to get up in the morning.
sentences.zh: 然后呢？是的。引用你自己的话，我可以向你保证，有人处境比你更糟，但做得更好。我前段时间发布了这个片段，只是关于晨间例行公事的一些随口谈话，内容很基础，但它在网上火得一塌糊涂，真正的互联网用户注意到了它，你知道，不是你的粉丝，而是真正的互联网用户，大众互联网注意到了它。最常见的评论大概是：“不用告诉我你没有孩子，我就知道你没有孩子”，意思是“说起来容易，我有女儿要照顾，没法早起”。

sentences.en: I'm like, okay, tell me what that mindset gets you.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，告诉我那种心态能给你带来什么。

sentences.en: Genuinely tell me what that mindset gets you.
sentences.zh: 真诚地告诉我，那种心态能给你带来什么。

sentences.en: It says, I'm in a situation which I cannot get over.
sentences.zh: 它说：我处于一种我无法克服的境地。

sentences.en: And there are things in reality imposed on me, which stopped me from doing something.
sentences.zh: 现实中强加给我的事情阻止了我做某事。

sentences.en: There is somebody out there who has three times as many kids as you, and they still do it.
sentences.zh: 外面有人比你多三倍的孩子，但他们依然做到了。

sentences.en: So what is it that they've got? Like, what is it that they're doing?
sentences.zh: 那么他们拥有什么？他们到底在做什么？

sentences.en: Have they got an unfair advantage? What is it?
sentences.zh: 他们有不公平的优势吗？到底是什么？

sentences.en: Tell me. It's also, if you take down, if you walk down the natural logic of that statement.
sentences.zh: 告诉我。而且，如果你顺着这种说法的逻辑走下去。

sentences.en: Who do you blame? If you're saying must be nice or tell me, tell me that you don't have kids without telling me that you don't have kids, then does that mean that you blame your child for all the things that you don't have in life?
sentences.zh: 你怪谁？如果你说“那肯定很好”或者“不用告诉我你没有孩子，我就知道你没有孩子”，那是不是意味着你把你生活中所有没得到的东西都怪罪于你的孩子？

sentences.en: It's tough, tough weight to put on a kid because I mean, I would hope that they don't see that comment because then they'd be like, wait, mom, dad, like you didn't live out your dreams because I exist?
sentences.zh: 这很沉重，给孩子施加了沉重的负担，因为我希望他们没看到那条评论，否则他们会想：等等，妈妈，爸爸，是因为我的存在，你们才没能实现梦想吗？

sentences.en: Tough. Another one here, a sequence actually that I love.
sentences.zh: 很沉重。这里还有一点，实际上是一个我非常喜欢的逻辑序列。

sentences.en: You don't have to feel good about it. You just have to keep going.
sentences.zh: 你不必对它感觉良好。你只需要继续前进。

sentences.en: The feeling will pass, but you will remain.
sentences.zh: 感觉会过去，但你会留下来。

sentences.en: You are greater than your feelings. Going to bed late and waking up early to work for a few days won't kill you.
sentences.zh: 你比你的情绪更伟大。晚睡早起工作几天不会杀了你。

sentences.en: You're not going to burn out. You're doing what it takes.
sentences.zh: 你不会精疲力竭的。你是在做必要的事情。

sentences.en: If you're one of those people that push work-life balance, just remember the people who like working a lot, don't care.
sentences.zh: 如果你是那些推崇工作与生活平衡的人之一，请记住，那些喜欢努力工作的人，根本不在乎。

sentences.en: I've never regretted trying harder at anything ever.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有后悔过在任何事情上付出更多努力。

sentences.en: Hard times last long, but an epic story feels like a lifetime.
sentences.zh: 艰难的时光持续很久，但一段史诗般的故事感觉就像一生。

sentences.en: Nailed it. Fuck yeah. I just think when I look at you in particular, and I realized this during our second conversation at the start of this year, the reason that people get confused about your motivation and your workload is that they don't realize that the thing you do for work is the thing that you do for fun.
sentences.zh: 说得太对了。去他的。我只是觉得，当我特别看着你时，我在今年年初我们的第二次谈话中意识到，人们对你的动力和工作量感到困惑的原因是，他们没有意识到你为了工作所做的事情，正是你为了乐趣所做的事情。

sentences.en: That's the fundamental misunderstanding that people have.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们产生的根本误解。

sentences.en: And because of that, you're prepared to work hard.
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，你才准备好努力工作。

sentences.en: And working hard doesn't feel like wasted time.
sentences.zh: 而努力工作并不感觉像是浪费时间。

sentences.en: Lots of people associate working hard with not making progress.
sentences.zh: 很多人把努力工作与没有取得进展联系在一起。

sentences.en: Therefore, working feels like wasting.
sentences.zh: 因此，工作感觉就像是在浪费。

sentences.en: So the idea that working hard doesn't make progress is one of the biggest farces that exists in humanity.
sentences.zh: 所以，“努力工作不能取得进展”这种想法是人类社会中最大的谎言之一。

sentences.en: Because at the end of the day, whatever you amount to isn't going to matter anyways. right?
sentences.zh: 因为归根结底，你最终成就了什么并不重要，对吧？

sentences.en: And so if there is anything that's eternal for us, at least as individuals, it's going to be who we become in the process.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果有什么东西对我们个人来说是永恒的，那就是我们在过程中成为了什么样的人。

sentences.en: And so one of my favorite quotes is, the work works on you more than you work on it.
sentences.zh: 所以我最喜欢的名言之一是：工作对你的塑造，远胜于你对工作的投入。

sentences.en: And so if you want to be the best in the world at something, you do the work to become the best in the world and the work works on you.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想成为世界上某件事的佼佼者，你就要努力成为世界上最好的，而工作会塑造你。

sentences.en: And so, I mean, there's a biblical proverb, I think it says like, there is profit in all labor.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想有一句圣经箴言，我想它是说：所有的劳苦都有益处。

sentences.en: And that means that even if the thing that you're working on right now doesn't amount to the outcome that you expected that it would, it doesn't mean that you don't become better through doing it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着即使你现在所做的事情没有达到你预期的结果，也不代表你在做这件事的过程中没有变得更好。

sentences.en: And so I'll give you a very real example.
sentences.zh: 所以我给你举一个非常真实的例子。

sentences.en: So I spent five years building a chain of gyms.
sentences.zh: 我花了五年时间建立了一家健身房连锁店。

sentences.en: So I had six locations. And after that, I sold five of them.
sentences.zh: 我有六个分店。在那之后，我卖掉了其中五个。

sentences.en: I shut one down. And then I transitioned to doing turnarounds.
sentences.zh: 我关掉了一个。然后我转型做企业扭亏为盈。

sentences.en: In the transition between shutting my gyms down, I got a big payday because I sold my five gyms, big for me, relative.
sentences.zh: 在关闭健身房的过渡期，我赚了一大笔钱，因为我卖掉了五个健身房，对我来说相对很大。

sentences.en: I took all that money and I put it into the next thing.
sentences.zh: 我把所有的钱都投入到了下一件事中。

sentences.en: The partner that I had in that next thing ended up taking the money and disappearing, filing bankruptcy and sending it to his girlfriend in Sweden.
sentences.zh: 我在那件事中的合伙人最终拿了钱消失了，申请破产，并把钱寄给了他在瑞典的女朋友。

sentences.en: I couldn't make this up. So there was no way I could get the money back and he had filed bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 我编不出这种故事。所以我没法把钱要回来，而且他已经申请了破产。

sentences.en: There's no course of action for a lawsuit.
sentences.zh: 没有诉讼的途径。

sentences.en: And so a lot of people would probably go through that mental situation and think, and I went through this, was thinking, I just wasted the last five years.
sentences.zh: 所以很多人可能会经历那种心理状态，认为——我也经历过——认为我刚刚浪费了过去五年。

sentences.en: I literally started to change, put everything into the second location, put everything in the third location, the fourth location, it kept going, right?
sentences.zh: 我真的开始改变，把一切投入到第二个分店，投入到第三个、第四个分店，一直持续下去，对吧？
