sentences.en: I kept doubling down. And then I get my big payday and I put it all on black and then it disappears with one spin of the roulette.
sentences.zh: 我不断加码。然后我赚了大钱，把一切都押在黑色上，结果轮盘赌一转，钱就消失了。

sentences.en: And so here I am and I'm like, I have nothing to show for the last five years of work.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在在这里，我想：过去五年的工作我一无所获。

sentences.en: But then in the next 12 months, I made more money than I'd ever made in my entire life up to that point.
sentences.zh: 但在接下来的12个月里，我赚的钱比我一生中任何时候都要多。

sentences.en: The five years, I made more profit the next 12 months than I made in the last five years times like five.
sentences.zh: 那五年，我在接下来的12个月里赚的利润比过去五年加起来还要多五倍。

sentences.en: And it was because, and this is only, I was only able to realize this in retrospect, which is why I'm sharing it, which is that the thing that was the outcome of those five years was me and the skills and the experiences that I possessed through going through it.
sentences.zh: 这是因为——我只能在事后回顾时才意识到这一点，这就是我分享它的原因——那五年产生的结果是我自己，以及我在经历过程中所拥有的技能和经验。

sentences.en: And so whatever the next mountain that you're trying to climb is, of course, it's going to be higher, but it's going to require you to go through the smaller mountains to get to that point.
sentences.zh: 所以无论你试图攀登的下一座山是什么，当然它会更高，但它需要你先翻越较小的山才能到达那个点。

sentences.en: Because the more able you are, the more able you realize you can become.
sentences.zh: 因为你越有能力，你就越意识到自己能变得更有能力。

sentences.en: And you will get way bigger outcomes from the things that you have, like the path that led you here, then you think you can.
sentences.zh: 你会从你所拥有的事物中获得比你想象中大得多的成果，就像引领你走到这里的道路一样。

sentences.en: And so that's why since that moment where I lost everything, And then I was able to make more in the next 12 months.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么从我失去一切的那一刻起，我就能在接下来的12个月里赚得更多。

sentences.en: I realized that no work is wasted because I am the output of the work, not the outcome.
sentences.zh: 我意识到没有工作是浪费的，因为我是工作的产出，而不是结果。

sentences.en: And that was one of the biggest frame shifts for me in never thinking that work is wasted because the more I work, the bigger my work ethic, the more my work capacity increases.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说是最大的框架转变之一，让我再也不认为工作是浪费，因为我工作得越多，我的职业道德就越强，我的工作能力就越强。

sentences.en: And to give an exercise example, because I think it's cool and interesting, is that a lot of people talk about this concept of overtraining.
sentences.zh: 为了举一个运动的例子，因为我觉得这很酷很有趣，很多人谈论“过度训练”这个概念。

sentences.en: Don't worry, I'll bring it back. All right.
sentences.zh: 别担心，我会绕回来的。好的。

sentences.en: They talk about this concept of overtraining.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论过度训练这个概念。

sentences.en: I remember I was talking, I had this woman that, Leila and I are friends with, very successful business owner, had a boy toy with her.
sentences.zh: 我记得我当时在谈话，我和Leila有位朋友，是一位非常成功的企业主，带了一个小白脸。

sentences.en: And he was like, aren't you concerned about overtraining?
sentences.zh: 他问：你不担心过度训练吗？

sentences.en: And I was feeling a little pissy that day.
sentences.zh: 那天我心情有点烦躁。

sentences.en: And I said, bro, once you start looking like you work out, you can worry about overtraining.
sentences.zh: 我说：兄弟，等你练得看起来像是在健身的时候，你再担心过度训练吧。

sentences.en: I was like, until that point, you don't need to worry about overtraining.
sentences.zh: 我说：在那之前，你不需要担心过度训练。

sentences.en: I was being a little bit mean, but I think he did remember it and he did change the way he trained and he did gain muscle afterwards.
sentences.zh: 我当时有点刻薄，但我认为他确实记住了，他确实改变了训练方式，之后也确实长了肌肉。

sentences.en: So I felt okay about it. Now, the point of that little quip, right?
sentences.zh: 所以我感觉还好。现在，那个俏皮话的重点是什么？

sentences.en: Was that what I explained to him is that your ability to recover from working out itself is trainable.
sentences.zh: 我向他解释的是，你从锻炼中恢复的能力本身就是可以训练的。

sentences.en: So when you do more volume, your ability to withstand volume, your work capacity increases.
sentences.zh: 所以当你增加训练量时，你承受训练量的能力，即你的工作能力就会增加。

sentences.en: And so to the same degree, people are like, I feel burnt out.
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，人们说：我感到精疲力竭。

sentences.en: The thing is, is that you either die or you adapt.
sentences.zh: 问题是，你要么死，要么适应。

sentences.en: That's it. right? And in the fitness world, you either die, get injured or adapt, right?
sentences.zh: 就是这样。对吧？在健身界，你要么死，要么受伤，要么适应，对吧？

sentences.en: And since you're probably not going to die, you really just need to make sure that you don't get injured.
sentences.zh: 既然你可能不会死，你只需要确保自己不受伤。

sentences.en: And if you don't get injured and you don't die, you get better.
sentences.zh: 如果你不受伤也不死，你就会变得更好。

sentences.en: And so that mental process in terms of how I see work has been like the most self-fulfilling prophecy that I've had, because the more I work, the better I get at working, the more productive I am per unit of time.
sentences.zh: 所以这种心理过程，就我如何看待工作而言，一直是我所拥有的最自我实现的预言，因为我工作得越多，我工作得就越好，我在单位时间内就越高效。

sentences.en: And so, and then I get the outcomes that happen eventually.
sentences.zh: 所以，然后我最终得到了结果。

sentences.en: But the point is, and you probably, I mean, I already know, you know this, but the outcomes become so irrelevant compared to the reward that you get in the meantime.
sentences.zh: 但重点是，你可能——我的意思是，我已经知道你知道这一点——但结果与你在此期间获得的奖励相比变得如此无关紧要。

sentences.en: Because the people who are experts, and this is from my good friend, Dr.
sentences.zh: 因为那些专家——这是我好朋友Dr. Cashy说的——任何技能的专家之所以成为专家，是因为他们学会了如何从工作本身获得奖励。

sentences.en: Cashy, people who are experts at any skill become experts because they learn how to become rewarded from the work itself.
sentences.zh: 所以他们并没有什么你没有的东西。

sentences.en: And so they don't actually have something that you don't.
sentences.zh: 只是他们衡量成功的方式不同。

sentences.en: It's just that they measure success differently.
sentences.zh: 用你的行动来评判自己，而不是用你的想法。

sentences.en: Judge yourself by your actions, not by your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 当我开始只根据我采取的行动而不是我产生的想法来评判自己时，我对自己的失望感显著降低了。

sentences.en: I became significantly less disappointed in myself when I started judging myself only on the actions I took, not the thoughts I had.
sentences.zh: 所以耐心是一种我觉得我没有的美德。

sentences.en: So patience is a virtue that I feel like I haven't had.
sentences.zh: 多年来我一直对自己说这句话。

sentences.en: And it's been something that I've spoken over myself for many years.
sentences.zh: 我说：我是一个没耐心的人。我想要快点得到结果，等等。

sentences.en: I was like, I'm an impatient person. I want things fast, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 但当我意识到我应该用评判别人的眼光来评判自己时，比如有人可能会说：我是一个非常诚实的人。

sentences.en: But when I realized that I should use the same lens that I judge other people on when I judge myself, which is someone might say, I'm a really honest guy.
sentences.zh: 但如果我没有任何证据表明你是一个诚实的人，或者当我把你放在一个可以诚实但你却没有诚实的境地时，我会说：不，你不是。

sentences.en: But if I have no evidence that you're an honest person, or when I put you in a situation where you could be honest and you're not, I would say, no, you're not.
sentences.zh: 现在那个人可能认为自己很诚实，或者同样地：我是一个非常忠诚的人。

sentences.en: Now that person probably thinks of themselves as honest or to the same degree, I'm a really loyal guy.
sentences.zh: 但一旦我把一个10分的美女放在你面前，而你家里有女朋友，你就动摇了。

sentences.en: But as soon as I put a 10 in front of you and you've got your girl at home, you jump.
sentences.zh: 你并不那么忠诚。你只是没有机会表现出你的忠诚。

sentences.en: You're not that loyal. You just haven't had the opportunity to show that you're loyal.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说，关于我以为我是什么样的人的想法实际上非常负面。

sentences.en: And so for me, my thoughts about what I thought I was were actually really negative.
sentences.zh: 但当我试着想：好吧，我可以表现得有耐心，即使我感觉不到耐心。

sentences.en: But when I tried to think, okay, well, I can be patient if I act patient, even if I don't feel patient.
sentences.zh: 这让我开始给自己积累一堆不可否认的证据，证明我就是我想成为的那个人。

sentences.en: And then that allowed me to start giving myself a stack of undeniable proof that I am who I wanted to be.
sentences.zh: 我不相信二元特征，意思是说：他要么有耐心，要么没耐心，要么忠诚，要么不忠诚。

sentences.en: And I don't believe in binary traits, meaning like he's patient or he's impatient or he's loyal or he's disloyal.
sentences.zh: 问题是：你有多忠诚？你有多诚实？

sentences.en: The question is, how loyal are you? How honest are you?
sentences.zh: 你有多耐心？通过将我想要拥有的性格特征转化为进展或连续体，让我能够通过给自己更多的证据，或者在天平上多放一分钱，证明我比以前更有耐心一点，从而在这些特征上取得进展。

sentences.en: How patient are you? And by switching the character traits that I wanted to have into progressions or continuums allowed me to make progress on them simply by giving myself more proof or one more penny on the scale that says I'm a little bit more patient than I was.
sentences.zh: 我更有耐心一点。我更有耐心一点。直到我在天平上放了这么多钱，以至于我可以对自己说：我想我很有耐心。

sentences.en: I'm a little bit more patient. I'm a little bit more patient to the point where I have so many pennies on the scale that I can say, I think I am pretty patient.
sentences.zh: 尽管每次我在天平上放钱时，我都不想放钱。

sentences.en: Even though every time I put a penny on the scale, I don't want to put a penny on the scale.
sentences.zh: 我想让事情今天就发生。

sentences.en: I want to get the thing to happen today.
sentences.zh: 我想让它昨天就发生，因为为什么花了这么长时间？

sentences.en: I want it to happen yesterday because why is it taking so long?
sentences.zh: 这对那个人来说没花那么长时间。

sentences.en: It didn't take that long for this person.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我比他们努力，我觉得我比他们强。

sentences.en: I feel like I work harder than them and I feel like I'm better than them.
sentences.zh: 为什么我没做到？但我还是把钱放在了天平上。

sentences.en: Why am I not doing that? But I put the penny on the scale.
sentences.zh: 好吧，归根结底，什么是耐心？耐心是感觉有耐心，还是做耐心该做的事？

sentences.en: Well, ultimately, what is patience? Is patience feeling patient or is patient doing the thing that is patience?
sentences.zh: 所以Sam Harrison，他与Jocko Willink的第一次谈话大约在10年前，他们谈到勇气是一种无法伪造的情绪。

sentences.en: So Sam Harrison, his first conversation with Jocko Willink about 10 years ago, they talk about how courage is an unfakeable emotion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的框架。你会喜欢这个的。

sentences.en: And it's such a good frame. You're going to love this.
sentences.zh: 所以他说：如果你在害怕做某事的情况下依然做了那件事，那就是勇气。

sentences.en: So he said, if you do the thing, in spite of being fearful of doing the thing, that is courage.
sentences.zh: 如果你在想做某事的情况下却没有做，那就是懦弱。

sentences.en: And if you don't do the thing, even though you felt like doing the thing, that is cowardice.
sentences.zh: 我认为动力和耐心也是一样的。

sentences.en: And I think that motivation and patience are exactly the same.
sentences.zh: 如果你在感觉不到耐心的情况下依然保持耐心，那就是耐心。

sentences.en: If you're patient, despite not feeling patient, that is patience.
sentences.zh: 这就是它的运作方式。而那个你刚才说的领悟，就是那句名言的原因，因为那是我意识到我实际上可以拥有这些特质，即使我不觉得我活出了这些特质。

sentences.en: That is how it works. And that was that realization that you just said was the reason for that quote, because it was me realizing that I can actually have these traits, even if I don't feel like I live those traits.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么可能，至少对我来说，当人们说：无论是什么特质，比如“他太谦虚了”，“他太怎么样了”，你可能永远不会觉得你拥有这个特质。

sentences.en: And so that's why probably, at least for me, when people are like, whatever the trait is, like, he's so humble, he's so whatever, like, you probably will never feel like you have the trait.
sentences.zh: 但你仍然可以基于证据而不是情绪来拥有这个特质。

sentences.en: But you can still have the trait based on evidence rather than emotion.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种证据框架一直以来——我的意思是，如果我有一个个人发展的北极星，那就是给自己证据。

sentences.en: And I think that frame of evidence has been, I mean, if I had a North Star of personal development for myself, it's been just give myself proof.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在很多方面。比如我没有——我的意思是，我要跑题了，但同样，我会绕回来。

sentences.en: And I mean, in so many ways. Like the reason that I didn't, I mean, I'm going to go on a tangent, but again, I'll bring it back.
sentences.zh: 我直到有六家健身房才谈论如何经营健身房，因为我觉得自己没有足够的资格谈论它。

sentences.en: I didn't talk about how to run gyms until I had six gyms because I didn't feel like I was qualified enough to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 我只有在很多人问我“伙计，你是怎么经营健身房的？”时才开始谈论健身房。

sentences.en: And I only started talking about gyms when so many people were like, dude, how do you run your gyms?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么经营健身房的？如果我在此之前倒带，我觉得自己没有资格谈论健身，但我已经有十年腹肌了。

sentences.en: How do you run your gyms? And if I rewind even before that, I didn't feel qualified to talk about fitness, but I'd had a six pack for a decade.
sentences.zh: 你知道我的意思吗？我有多个州纪录，但我仍然觉得没资格谈论健身，直到每个人都问我：伙计，你是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: You know what I mean? And I had multiple state records, but I still didn't feel qualified to talk about fitness until everyone was like, dude, how do you, how do you do this?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么做到的？你是怎么进行力量训练的？你是怎么这样吃的？

sentences.en: How do you strength train? How do you eat this way?
sentences.zh: 无论是什么。所以如果你能给自己证据，你周围的世界，比如名声，你的证据会改变人们对待你的方式，而不管你对此感觉如何。

sentences.en: Whatever it is. And so if you can give yourself evidence, the world around you, like fame, your evidence will change how people treat you independent of how you feel about it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这就是为什么“那肯定很好”、“那肯定容易”这种说法如此有缺陷，因为你所说的是：我看到了结果，但我对投入的难度一无所知。

sentences.en: Well, this is why the must be easy, must be nice is so flawed because what you're saying is I see the outcomes and I have no idea of the difficulty of the inputs.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道你需要克服什么障碍。你可能觉得保持耐心有99%的难度，然而别人却说“那肯定容易，你有耐心基因”。去吃屎吧。你根本不知道人们做他们所做的事情有多难，而在某些方面让事情看起来容易的人，加剧了这个问题。这就是为什么我真的很喜欢，我是你很多作品的忠实粉丝。

sentences.en: I have absolutely no idea what barriers you need to get over. you could be you could find it 99 out of 100 difficult to be patient and yet you are must be nice for you you've got that patience gene you go eat shit eat shit you have no idea how hard it is for people to do the things that they do and the people that make it look easy in some regards contribute to this problem like i and this is why i really love i am a massive fan of a lot of your work.
sentences.zh: 我认为原因之一是它对挑战和必须经历的步骤非常诚实和谦逊。

sentences.en: And I think that one of the reasons is that it's so honest and self-effacing about the challenges and about the steps that you have to get through.
sentences.zh: 因为旅程叙述得相对清晰，你可以一步步追踪它，你创造了一个关于这一切如何运作的连贯时间线，在你的旅程中，具体来说，但希望也是我的和其他人的，有一个点人们可以代入自己说：哦，我正处于那个阶段。

sentences.en: And because the journey is relatively well narratized and you can track it step by step and you've created a kind of a cohesive timeline of how all of this stuff worked, there is a point along specifically your journey, but hopefully mine and other people's too, where people can inject themselves and say, oh, I'm at that bit.
sentences.zh: 我是那个15岁的孩子，我正处于那个阶段，我怨恨我的父母，我刚刚失去了所有的钱，我觉得我需要……你知道，你生活中可能遇到的每一个不同的问题都存在于Alex的时间线中，我认为这非常重要。我认为这是我对一些个人发展、自我成长和很多商业建议的批评，即使是糟糕的时光也被浪漫化了，它们一点也不浪漫，感觉就像地狱，做那件事、失败、感觉没有人关心你、甚至不知道回顾时是否会有荣耀，感觉就像狗屎一样。

sentences.en: I'm the 15 year old that I'm at that bit I resent my parents I've just lost all my money I feel like I need to you know like you have every different problem that you can encounter in life is present in Alex's timeline and I think that that's really important I think this this is one of the I would say this is a criticism that I have about some of the personal development self-growth and a lot of the business advice as well even the bad times are romanticized and they're not fucking romantic like it feels like hell it feels like shit to do the thing to fail to not feel like anybody cares about you to not even know that there's going to be glory in retrospect yeah it feels despondent and destitute and sad and alone and i get it and i think that the more visceral that we can make these stories the better it is because i know that that's what would have resonated with me because i would have gone that's an undeniable stack of proof that you were where you said you were i'll tell you one that maybe will resonate with somebody in the audience.
sentences.zh: 是的，感觉绝望、贫困、悲伤和孤独，我明白。我认为我们能让这些故事越生动越好，因为我知道那会引起我的共鸣，因为我会说：那是一堆不可否认的证据，证明你确实在你所说的地方。我会告诉你一个可能引起观众共鸣的故事。

sentences.en: So I remember when I decided to move, so I moved to California to start a gym or get into fitness.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得当我决定搬家时，我搬到加州去开健身房或进入健身行业。

sentences.en: And I got there and the guy who I said I was going to mentor under was like, where are you staying?
sentences.zh: 我到了那里，我打算跟随导师的那个人问：你住哪儿？

sentences.en: And I was like, I don't know. I just got here.
sentences.zh: 我说：我不知道。我刚到。

sentences.en: And he was like, what do you mean you don't know?
sentences.zh: 他说：你什么意思你不知道？

sentences.en: I was like, I don't know. I just, I just showed up.
sentences.zh: 我说：我不知道。我只是……我只是出现了。

sentences.en: And so he went, he said I could sleep at his place that night.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了，他说那天晚上我可以睡在他那里。

sentences.en: The next morning went to the gym and he got on a chair and said, Hey, who here is going to house this kid?
sentences.zh: 第二天早上去了健身房，他坐在一张椅子上说：嘿，这里有谁能收留这个孩子？

sentences.en: And one guy came up to me, he was like, I'll give you a room.
sentences.zh: 一个人走过来对我说：我会给你一个房间。

sentences.en: So I rented one room in a house for 400 bucks a month.
sentences.zh: 所以我以每月400美元的价格租了一个房子里的一个房间。

sentences.en: And then when I left that room to start sleeping at the gym, which was an hour away because I couldn't make the commute.
sentences.zh: 然后当我离开那个房间开始睡在健身房时，那离我住的地方有一个小时的路程，因为我负担不起通勤费用。

sentences.en: So I saved 400 bucks a month. I remember being actually kind of excited about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我每月省下了400美元。我记得当时其实还挺兴奋的。

sentences.en: I remember being like, man, this is going to be a sick story.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想：伙计，这会是一个很酷的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah. This is my Rocky cut scene, right?
sentences.zh: 是的。这是我的《洛奇》剪辑片段，对吧？

sentences.en: But the thing is that the Rocky cut scene lasts 30 seconds in the movie, but it can last five years in your life.
sentences.zh: 但问题是《洛奇》的剪辑片段在电影里只持续30秒，但在你的生活中却可能持续五年。

sentences.en: And when I was sleeping on the gym floor, I'll give you a detail that. that'll tell you that the stack of a denial proof, was that my first gym was underneath of a parking garage.
sentences.zh: 当我睡在健身房地板上时，我给你一个细节，那会告诉你那堆不可否认的证据，就是我的第一个健身房是在一个停车场下面。

sentences.en: And so there's these metal dividers in the ceiling.
sentences.zh: 天花板上有金属隔板。

sentences.en: And so cars would drive over this and it's a concrete box.
sentences.zh: 所以汽车会开过这里，这是一个混凝土盒子。

sentences.en: And so it sounded like a gunshot, like, and it would happen at all hours of the night.
sentences.zh: 所以听起来像枪声，而且它会在深夜的任何时候发生。

sentences.en: And probably the most painful from an emotional perspective experience that I would have on a regular basis was that it was also abandoned enough parking a lot that college kids, kids my age would go up and party on the roof.
sentences.zh: 可能从情感角度来看，我经常经历的最痛苦的经历是，那也是一个足够荒废的停车场，大学生，和我同龄的孩子会上去在屋顶聚会。

sentences.en: And so like while they were partying literally above my head and making noise that would prevent me from sleeping, I would be down below in a dark warehouse in a city that I knew no one.
sentences.zh: 所以当他们在我的头顶上方聚会并制造噪音让我无法入睡时，我却在下面，在一个我谁也不认识的城市的黑暗仓库里。

sentences.en: Like I was from Baltimore. I drove across the country.
sentences.zh: 就像我来自巴尔的摩。我开车横跨全国。

sentences.en: I went to Huntington Beach. I literally knew no one and no one knew me.
sentences.zh: 我去了亨廷顿海滩。我真的谁也不认识，也没人认识我。

sentences.en: And so I'm sleeping there. And then I realized that I can't really sleep at night.
sentences.zh: 所以我睡在那里。然后我意识到我晚上真的睡不着。

sentences.en: And so I'm taking basically, I'm living on naps for the first six months of the gym.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上是在靠打盹生活，在健身房的前六个月。

sentences.en: And like homeless people are sleeping in my parking lot and I have to like go out and tell them to like go away.
sentences.zh: 无家可归的人睡在我的停车场，我不得不出去告诉他们离开。

sentences.en: And then I get back, lock the door and I go back on the AstroTurf, which is where I slept with a blanket and a pillow.
sentences.zh: 然后我回来，锁上门，回到人造草坪上，那是我带着毯子和枕头睡觉的地方。

sentences.en: And I bring this up because like the visceral feeling that you go through when you're going through the mound of shit period or the shit eating, what feels like a marathon. is that it becomes a 30-second soundbite in my story.
sentences.zh: 我提到这一点是因为，当你经历那段“吃屎”时期或“吃屎”过程时，那种生动的感觉，感觉就像一场马拉松。它在我的故事里变成了一个30秒的片段。

sentences.en: But it was years. And so even to the same degree, people are like, man, you're such a natural salesman.
sentences.zh: 但它持续了几年。所以同样地，人们说：伙计，你真是个天生的推销员。

sentences.en: The first job I ever got offered out of college was a sales job.
sentences.zh: 我大学毕业后得到的第一份工作是销售工作。

sentences.en: And I said, I'm not a salesman. I'm an academic.
sentences.zh: 我说：我不是推销员。我是个学者。

sentences.en: And then as soon as I opened my gym, I was like, oh shit, how do I pay rent?
sentences.zh: 然后我一开健身房，我就想：哦，该死，我怎么付房租？

sentences.en: And someone walked in the door and I was like, please give me money.
sentences.zh: 有人走进门，我就说：请给我钱。

sentences.en: I promise. And I had no equipment in my gym because I couldn't afford any.
sentences.zh: 我保证。我的健身房里没有任何设备，因为我买不起任何设备。

sentences.en: So it's an empty gym with just turf. And I was like, I promise you, I will get you amazing results.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个只有草坪的空健身房。我说：我向你保证，我会让你得到惊人的结果。

sentences.en: And they were like, are you going to be here tomorrow?
sentences.zh: 他们问：你明天还会在这里吗？

sentences.en: And I was like, I sleep here. I have to be here.
sentences.zh: 我说：我睡在这里。我必须在这里。

sentences.en: I promise I'll be here. It's impossible for me to not be here.
sentences.zh: 我保证我会在这里。我不在这里是不可能的。

sentences.en: I can't leave. I can't leave. And so the early people took pity on me when they literally paid the first 29 members I signed up in the first two weeks before the gym opened was from pity.
sentences.zh: 我不能离开。我不能离开。所以早期的人们对我产生了怜悯，当他们真的付钱时，我在健身房开业前两周签下的前29名会员是出于怜悯。

sentences.en: It wasn't from charisma. It was pure pity.
sentences.zh: 不是因为魅力。纯粹是怜悯。

sentences.en: I'll be real with you. And it was the exact amount that I needed to pay rent.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说实话。这正好是我付房租所需的金额。

sentences.en: And I remember the first month of rent that I paid, this is actually wild.
sentences.zh: 我记得我付的第一个月房租，这其实很疯狂。

sentences.en: I only looked at this in retrospect. I made exactly $4,972 my first month of my gym.
sentences.zh: 我只是在回顾时才看到这一点。我健身房第一个月正好赚了4972美元。

sentences.en: My rent was $4,972. And I remember working like a dog to get that.
sentences.zh: 我的房租是4972美元。我记得为了得到那个数字，我像狗一样工作。

sentences.en: I'd never made money in my life. I'd never really asked anyone for money.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没赚过钱。我从来没有真正向任何人要过钱。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden I had to come up with $5,000 in a month.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我一个月内必须拿出5000美元。

sentences.en: And then at the end of the month, I watched it go to zero.
sentences.zh: 然后在月底，我看着它归零。

sentences.en: And then I was like, I have to do it again.
sentences.zh: 然后我想：我必须再做一次。

sentences.en: And that was when like the reality of the situation of like, there was no escape.
sentences.zh: 那就是当现实情况——没有逃脱的可能——出现的时候。

sentences.en: There was no one who was going to come to save me.
sentences.zh: 没有人会来救我。

sentences.en: And there was, I couldn't blame my dad. I couldn't blame my mom.
sentences.zh: 我不能怪我爸爸。我不能怪我妈妈。

sentences.en: I was the one who had chosen this life. But the alternative was that I had to go back to my father of failure and have him look me in the eyes and say, I told you, come here, don't worry about it.
sentences.zh: 是我选择了这种生活。但另一种选择是，我必须回到我父亲那里承认失败，让他看着我的眼睛说：我告诉过你，过来吧，别担心。

sentences.en: I told you this gym stuff, this fitness stuff, this starting room, it's for later.
sentences.zh: 我告诉过你这些健身房的事，这些健身的事，这些创业的事，那是以后的事。

sentences.en: It's fine. I just go back, hey, you've got this great degree.
sentences.zh: 没关系。我只是回去，嘿，你有个很棒的学位。

sentences.en: You've got, just go to the business school to do the thing.
sentences.zh: 你拥有，去商学院做那件事吧。

sentences.en: And I knew exactly what would have happened.
sentences.zh: 我知道会发生什么。

sentences.en: But what would have happened after that is that for the rest of my life, he would have had absolute authority over everything that I did.
sentences.zh: 但那之后会发生的是，在我的余生中，他将对我所做的一切拥有绝对的权威。

sentences.en: And that felt like death. And so that was what I ran away from when I was in that moment.
sentences.zh: 那感觉就像死亡。所以这就是我在那一刻逃避的东西。

sentences.en: Like whenever I felt like my back was against the wall and I didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 每当我觉得自己被逼到墙角，不知道该怎么办时。

sentences.en: And it felt like the Instagram reels of like the motivation weren't going to get me through what I was going through because no one cared that I was sleeping alone.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像Instagram上那些励志短片无法帮我度过我正在经历的事情，因为没人关心我独自睡觉。

sentences.en: I'd let them know I'm sleeping on the floor.
sentences.zh: 我让他们知道我睡在地板上。

sentences.en: And a month later, when you're still sleeping on the floor, everyone's like, don't care.
sentences.zh: 一个月后，当你还在睡地板时，每个人都说：不关心。

sentences.en: Like, great. You're pursuing your dream, right?
sentences.zh: 太棒了。你在追求你的梦想，对吧？

sentences.en: Early days.
sentences.zh: 早期阶段。

sentences.en: But despite that, the must be easy mantra is the easiest indicator that you have a victim mindset. because what it means is I can't achieve this thing because on some level of use, it must be easy.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，“那肯定容易”的口头禅是你拥有受害者心态的最简单指标。因为这意味着我无法实现这件事，因为在某种程度上，它肯定很容易。

sentences.en: There's some level of desire that's there.
sentences.zh: 有一种渴望存在。

sentences.en: You're like, I'd like to achieve some aspect of this.
sentences.zh: 你觉得：我想实现这个的某个方面。

sentences.en: And then rather than feel the pain of saying that I'm inadequate or I'm not taking action, we cast our inadequacy on some outside object or some outside circumstance.
sentences.zh: 然后与其感受说自己无能或没有采取行动的痛苦，我们把我们的无能投射到某个外部对象或外部环境上。

sentences.en: And by doing that, we remove all agency and all power that we have over our lives.
sentences.zh: 通过这样做，我们消除了我们对生活的所有代理权和所有力量。

sentences.en: And for me, I would rather be somebody who has absolute power and have nothing to show for it than somebody who has all the things to show for it, but know that I'm life's bitch.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我宁愿成为一个拥有绝对力量却一无所获的人，也不愿成为一个拥有一切却知道自己是生活奴隶的人。

sentences.en: Life being one protracted training montage is a really important lesson to learn.
sentences.zh: 把生活看作一个漫长的训练蒙太奇是一个非常重要的教训。

sentences.en: The fact that in the Rocky movie, it is 90 seconds and then everything is fixed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在《洛奇》电影中，它只有90秒，然后一切都解决了。

sentences.en: And that can last for decades. That can last for years.
sentences.zh: 而这可能持续几十年。这可能持续几年。

sentences.en: And I think that the lack of glory, the lack of certainty, it makes it it turns it from worthwhile majesty into it's it's not even sufficiently triumphant to be called sad like it's just like weak and pissy and you have no idea if anything's going to work but what's the alternative entropy is going to come and fucking get you so what's the alternative.
sentences.zh: 我认为缺乏荣耀，缺乏确定性，它使它从值得的威严变成了——它甚至不足以被称为悲伤，就像它只是软弱和烦躁，你根本不知道任何事情是否会奏效，但另一种选择是什么？熵会来找你，去他的，所以另一种选择是什么？

sentences.en: Like my Twitter bio says, locally reversing entropy.
sentences.zh: 就像我的Twitter简介所说：局部逆转熵。

sentences.en: And I think that that really is what you should try and do because it's going to fucking come for you.
sentences.zh: 我认为这确实是你应该尝试做的事情，因为它会来找你的。

sentences.en: The lack of certainty is what actually makes it worth it.
sentences.zh: 缺乏确定性才是让它值得的原因。

sentences.en: And so here's my point. Let's consider the alternative, which is that you are on the path and you are guaranteed to know that you're going to get the outcome.
sentences.zh: 所以这是我的观点。让我们考虑另一种选择，那就是你在路上，并且你保证知道你会得到结果。

sentences.en: All of the mystery is gone. There is no excitement, which is why they said in the ancient Romans, or sorry, the ancient Greeks would say that the gods always envied the mortals because their life was so ephemeral, they had so much chance that could happen to them, right?
sentences.zh: 所有的神秘感都消失了。没有兴奋感，这就是为什么古罗马人——抱歉，古希腊人会说众神总是嫉妒凡人，因为他们的生命如此短暂，他们有这么多可能发生的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Where the gods always knew that they weren't going to die and it was completely guaranteed.
sentences.zh: 而众神总是知道他们不会死，而且一切都是完全保证的。

sentences.en: And so what we do is we basically have this wish that if it actually came true, we would hate it even more than our current circumstance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们所做的是，我们基本上有一个愿望，如果它真的实现了，我们会比我们目前的情况更讨厌它。

sentences.en: If you knew that you were going to succeed, it wouldn't be worth doing to begin with.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道你会成功，那从一开始就不值得做。

sentences.en: The fact that you are uncertain when you start is what makes it worthwhile.
sentences.zh: 你开始时是不确定的，这才是让它值得的原因。

sentences.en: And the fallacy of being in the pursuit is the worry or the concern that it won't amount to anything because who you are becoming is the thing that you are amounting to in real time every day.
sentences.zh: 而处于追求中的谬论是担心或忧虑它不会有任何结果，因为你正在成为的人就是你每天实时成就的东西。

sentences.en: This was something that Mark Manson tweeted.
sentences.zh: 这是Mark Manson发推文的内容。

sentences.en: He put it in his newsletter actually and it made me think of a lesson that I learned a long time ago.
sentences.zh: 他实际上把它放在了他的通讯中，这让我想起了一个我很久以前学到的教训。

sentences.en: Stop complaining about the results you didn't get from the work you didn't put in.
sentences.zh: 停止抱怨你没有投入工作而没有得到的结果。

sentences.en: The only way to become more successful than most people is to be willing to do something most people aren't willing to do. and this is that lean in mentality again it's like look it sucks it's shitty you're tired everybody says that you're leaving your friends behind leaving your family behind betraying your culture betraying whatever expectation it is that they have on you you need to do something that most people aren't willing to do because as we've said the average american is obese in debt and divorced like is that really oh brilliant fantastic i'm in the fucking center of the bell curve distribution here.
sentences.zh: 成为比大多数人更成功的人的唯一方法是愿意做大多数人不愿意做的事情。这又是那种“倾斜”心态，就像：看，这很烂，这很糟糕，你很累，每个人都说你抛弃了朋友，抛弃了家人，背叛了你的文化，背叛了他们对你的任何期望，你需要做一些大多数人不愿意做的事情，因为正如我们所说，普通美国人肥胖、负债、离婚，这真的……哦，太棒了，太棒了，我正处于钟形曲线分布的中心。

sentences.en: That's really, congratulations. And then the other side, stop complaining about the results you didn't get from the work you didn't put in.
sentences.zh: 那真的，恭喜。然后另一方面，停止抱怨你没有投入工作而没有得到的结果。

sentences.en: Okay. So you didn't lose weight this month.
sentences.zh: 好吧。所以你这个月没有减肥。

sentences.en: Did you follow your diet? Well, I did for half the month.
sentences.zh: 你遵循你的饮食计划了吗？嗯，我遵循了一半。

sentences.en: Okay. So is it any surprise that you didn't lose any weight?
sentences.zh: 好吧。所以你没有减肥有什么好惊讶的吗？

sentences.en: How's your content creation game going? Well, I spent a lot of time planning for the podcast that I'm going to release or for the Instagram that I'm going to start or from the sub stack that I'm going to begin writing on.
sentences.zh: 你的内容创作进展如何？嗯，我花了很多时间为我要发布的播客或我要开始的Instagram或我要开始写的Substack做计划。

sentences.en: Okay. And what did you actually do? It comes back to like the work.
sentences.zh: 好吧。那你实际上做了什么？这又回到了工作上。

sentences.en: Doesn't care. Yeah.
sentences.zh: 不在乎。是的。

sentences.en: Charlie Munger in one of his seminal speeches, he talks about how to guarantee failure, how to make sure that you are a failure.
sentences.zh: Charlie Munger在他的一篇开创性演讲中，谈到了如何保证失败，如何确保你是一个失败者。

sentences.en: And he inverts the concept of success. It's like, what could you do to make sure that you were a failure?
sentences.zh: 他颠倒了成功的概念。就像，你能做些什么来确保你是一个失败者？

sentences.en: It's like, well, you would definitely get involved in drugs, drinking.
sentences.zh: 就像，嗯，你肯定会卷入毒品、酗酒。

sentences.en: He says, was it leverage liquor in women?
sentences.zh: 他说，是杠杆、酒和女人吗？

sentences.en: That's the Charlie's big one, right? But one of the ones that he has, I think he has seven in his speech, is consistency.
sentences.zh: 那是Charlie的大原则，对吧？但他提到的其中之一，我想他在演讲中有七个，是坚持。

sentences.en: He's like, you have to make sure that you're inconsistent.
sentences.zh: 他说：你必须确保你不坚持。

sentences.en: He's like, because if you are consistent and you have none of the other attributes, he's like, you still might be successful.
sentences.zh: 他说：因为如果你坚持，即使你没有任何其他属性，他说：你仍然可能成功。

sentences.en: He's like, it's very tough for people who are consistent to not be successful.
sentences.zh: 他说：对于坚持的人来说，不成功是非常困难的。

sentences.en: And he makes an especially pointed point about consistency because in my opinion, it's one of the most difficult of the virtues for humans to do because we're so attracted to novelty.
sentences.zh: 他特别强调了坚持，因为在我看来，这是人类最难做到的美德之一，因为我们太被新奇事物所吸引了。

sentences.en: And so like, I mean, I used to do this with people on their diets all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我过去经常和人们谈论他们的饮食。

sentences.en: I remember I ran gyms. And so someone would come in and I would always ask the question, so have you been following the meal plan?
sentences.zh: 我记得我经营健身房。所以有人会进来，我总是问这个问题：那么你一直在遵循饮食计划吗？

sentences.en: And then they would say, yes. And so then I started changing the way I asked the question.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会说：是的。所以我开始改变我问问题的方式。

sentences.en: So I'd say, out of the 21 meals that you were supposed to eat, how many of the 21 did you have exactly the way it was on the meal plan?
sentences.zh: 所以我会说：在你应该吃的21顿饭中，有多少顿是你完全按照饮食计划吃的？

sentences.en: And then they would be like, oh, I mean, at least half.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会说：哦，我的意思是，至少一半。

sentences.en: And they would say it as though that was a mark of success.
sentences.zh: 他们说得好像那是一个成功的标志。

sentences.en: And right now the meal plan could be your content plan.
sentences.zh: 现在饮食计划可以是你的内容计划。

sentences.en: It could be your showing up to work on time plan.
sentences.zh: 它可以是你的准时上班计划。

sentences.en: It could be the time that you want to put towards your side hustle doesn't really matter.
sentences.zh: 它可以是你想要投入到副业的时间计划，这并不重要。

sentences.en: But if there's one muscle that you can flex, it's learning to do the same thing over and over again.
sentences.zh: 但如果有一块肌肉你可以锻炼，那就是学习一遍又一遍地做同样的事情。

sentences.en: Like one of the, one of the values that we had at gym launch is do the boring work because boring is what makes you rich, right?
sentences.zh: 就像我们在Gym Launch拥有的价值观之一是：做无聊的工作，因为无聊让你富有，对吧？

sentences.en: It's, it's, it's, it's writing the follow-up sequence to your, to the purchase page that you don't feel like doing, but you know, you should do it's running the split test for the 10th time.
sentences.zh: 它是编写购买页面的后续序列，你不想做，但你知道你应该做；它是第10次运行拆分测试。

sentences.en: It's, it's actually going through and prepping for 20 minutes before you have the meeting, because it's amazing how much smarter you can appear with 20 minutes of preparation.
sentences.zh: 它实际上是在开会前花20分钟进行准备，因为只要20分钟的准备，你看起来能聪明多少，这很神奇。

sentences.en: Like you can appear 50 IQ points smarter if you just prepare for meetings for 20 minutes.
sentences.zh: 就像只要你为会议准备20分钟，你看起来就能聪明50个IQ点。

sentences.en: I remember I did a consulting day, which I've only done three in my entire life.
sentences.zh: 我记得我做过一次咨询日，我一生中只做过三次。

sentences.en: And when I showed up to the day, because I always want to make sure that everyone always gets more from me than they give me, I had taken, I don't know, four hours, not a long time, but a long time for, I think some people, but for me, four hours is nothing.
sentences.zh: 当我出现在那一天时，因为我总是想确保每个人从我这里得到的总是比他们给我的多，我花了，我不知道，四个小时，时间不长，但对一些人来说很长，但对我来说，四个小时不算什么。

sentences.en: I count in hundreds. So this was irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 我按百计算。所以这无关紧要。

sentences.en: And so I put like four hours and actually took the time and put it in to do research on the individual.
sentences.zh: 所以我投入了四个小时，确实花时间对个人进行了研究。

sentences.en: So I looked at every single page to head, every landing page, every offer, every everything.
sentences.zh: 所以我看了每一个页面，每一个登陆页面，每一个报价，每一个东西。

sentences.en: And I had seven pages of things that I thought would make them more money.
sentences.zh: 我有七页我认为能让他们赚更多钱的东西。

sentences.en: And so when I started, I was like, this is what we're going to go through today.
sentences.zh: 所以当我开始时，我说：这就是我们今天要过的内容。

sentences.en: And I'll walk you through line by line. And you'll have this as a take behind so you can execute it with your team.
sentences.zh: 我会逐行带你过一遍。你会把它作为带走的东西，这样你就可以和你的团队执行它。

sentences.en: It was a bigger company. And the guy was shocked.
sentences.zh: 那是一家更大的公司。那个人很震惊。

sentences.en: He was like, never in my entire life has anyone had this much preparation.
sentences.zh: 他说：我一生中从来没有人做过这么多的准备。

sentences.en: And that's when it goes back to, like, you need 20 podcasts to be in the top 1%.
sentences.zh: 这就是回到：你需要20个播客才能进入前1%。

sentences.en: The bar for excellence, like, I have this timer that I have on my desk, which it's the easiest purchase you can make.
sentences.zh: 卓越的标准，就像，我桌上有一个计时器，这是你能做的最简单的购买。

sentences.en: I think it was like seven bucks on Amazon.
sentences.zh: 我想在亚马逊上大概七块钱。

sentences.en: It's a little twist kitchen timer. It's very easy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个小扭转厨房计时器。非常简单。

sentences.en: And it's been probably my biggest focus hack to date, which is I turn it when I want to start working.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我迄今为止最大的专注黑客，就是我开始工作时就转动它。

sentences.en: And part of it allows me to think how long...
sentences.zh: 它的一部分让我思考需要多长时间……

sentences.en: I get better at predicting how long it's going to take me to do something.
sentences.zh: 我更擅长预测做某事需要多长时间。

sentences.en: So I think this will take me 35 minutes.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为这需要我35分钟。

sentences.en: So I turn the clock to 35 and I click on.
sentences.zh: 所以我把时钟转到35，然后点击开始。

sentences.en: And then I start working on the thing. And the moment my phone rings or I look at Slack or whatever, I stop the timer.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始做那件事。当我手机响了或者我看Slack或者其他什么的时候，我停止计时器。

sentences.en: And so you actually see that your time on task is usually significantly less than you think it is.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上看到你的任务时间通常比你想象的要少得多。

sentences.en: And I think that in my early days, I would spend a very long time in front of a computer telling myself that I was working with very few minutes actually on task.
sentences.zh: 我认为在我的早期，我会花很长时间在电脑前告诉自己我在工作，而实际上任务时间很少。

sentences.en: And that's why I think that most things are actually significantly easier than people think they are.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我认为大多数事情实际上比人们想象的要容易得多。

sentences.en: They just don't know how to try hard because the harder that you try, the easier it gets.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不知道如何努力尝试，因为你尝试得越努力，它就变得越容易。

sentences.en: And so it's like, if you can just learn to love what trying hard feels like, then all of a sudden it becomes unreasonable that you can't win.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你能学会爱上努力尝试的感觉，那么突然之间，你无法获胜就变得不合理了。

sentences.en: So like for the presentation that I'm giving, I explained a little bit earlier about what my process looks like.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像我正在做的演示，我刚才解释了一点我的过程是什么样的。

sentences.en: If you were to say, what would it take for somebody to be unreasonably good, that it would be impossible for them to not be a top 1% salesman or a top 1% content creator.
sentences.zh: 如果你要说：一个人要达到不合理的好，以至于他们不可能不是前1%的推销员或前1%的内容创作者，需要什么？

sentences.en: And you said, what would that person need to do?
sentences.zh: 你说：那个人需要做什么？

sentences.en: Irrelevant from outcome, what would be the actions or evidence that they would have to do prior to that thing that would make it unreasonable that they couldn't succeed? and then you do those things what happens is you realize that it's actually not that hard because you put so much work into it and the bar from other people working is so embarrassingly low that they then ask you how you did it and it must be easy consistency doesn't guarantee that you'll be successful but not being consistent will guarantee that you won't reach success.
sentences.zh: 与结果无关，在做那件事之前，他们必须采取的行动或证据是什么，这会使他们无法成功变得不合理？然后你做这些事情，发生的事情是你意识到它实际上并不那么难，因为你投入了这么多工作，而其他人工作的标准低得令人尴尬，他们然后问你是怎么做到的，那肯定很容易。坚持不能保证你会成功，但不坚持肯定保证你不会达到成功。

sentences.en: You have a productivity hack, an easy productivity hack.
sentences.zh: 你有一个生产力黑客，一个简单的生产力黑客。

sentences.en: Instead of spending time getting in the mood to work, just start working, confront the work.
sentences.zh: 与其花时间进入工作状态，不如直接开始工作，面对工作。

sentences.en: People think they need perfect conditions to start when in reality, starting is the perfect condition.
sentences.zh: 人们认为他们需要完美的条件才能开始，而实际上，开始就是完美的条件。

sentences.en: I'm married to that. I love that. Because if you think, like I, you know, I obviously am somebody who always wants to optimize how much work I do per unit of time.
sentences.zh: 我对此深信不疑。我喜欢这个。因为如果你想，就像我，你知道，我显然是一个总是想优化我在单位时间内做多少工作的人。

sentences.en: And so there was definitely times earlier in my life I was really romanticized by these very extensive morning routines and supplement rituals and all this stuff of mental masturbation around the work that needed to be done.
sentences.zh: 所以在我生命早期肯定有几次，我真的被这些非常广泛的晨间例行公事、补充剂仪式以及所有围绕需要完成的工作的心理自慰所浪漫化了。

sentences.en: But when I looked at two hours later and nothing had actually gotten done, the moment you begin working is when your output per unit of time goes up. and so that makes beginning the single greatest hack that you can have for everything else that you do and work because the thing is when you start working you start getting in the mood to work right like everything else is procrastinating around the work that you think you should do but like i have noticed for me at least i have these i have some big mental tasks you know what i mean like big content piece or big thing that you need like you know it's going to take real mental effort it takes me like five minutes of actually being in it to then get a little bit of a lay of the land to then get into it.
sentences.zh: 但当我两个小时后看时，什么都没做成，你开始工作的时刻就是你单位时间产出上升的时刻。所以这使得开始成为你可以为你在工作中所做的一切拥有的最伟大的黑客，因为关键是当你开始工作时，你开始进入工作状态，对吧？就像其他一切都是在拖延你认为你应该做的工作，但我已经注意到，至少对我来说，我有这些——我有一些大的心理任务，你知道我的意思吗？比如大的内容片段或你需要的大事，你知道它需要真正的心理努力，我需要大约五分钟真正进入它，然后才能对它有一个大致的了解，然后进入它。

sentences.en: But I used to take hours to delay to start the first five minutes.
sentences.zh: 但我过去需要几个小时来推迟开始前五分钟。

sentences.en: And so my time compression of when I thought I should start doing something and when I started doing it over time, it's just compressed to the point where it's like the moment I think that I need to start doing it.
sentences.zh: 所以我的时间压缩，从我以为我应该开始做某事到我开始做它，随着时间的推移，它已经压缩到就像我想到我需要开始做它的那一刻。

sentences.en: Sometimes I just start it because then what happens, I get this open loop.
sentences.zh: 有时我只是开始它，因为然后发生的事情是，我得到了这个开放循环。

sentences.en: And so rather than complete work at like, because a lot of people are like, I want to complete it at this really nice, clean point.
sentences.zh: 所以与其在——因为很多人说：我想在一个非常漂亮、干净的点完成它。

sentences.en: Stop halfway through the sentence because it'll drive you mad.
sentences.zh: 在句子中间停下来，因为它会让你发疯。

sentences.en: That's the Zygonic effect in full work. Do you know this story?
sentences.zh: 这就是蔡加尼克效应在工作中充分体现。你知道这个故事吗？

sentences.en: Zygonic? oh wow this is way more than i do that's what you shut up that's what you're leveraging here so um the zygonic effect was a study originally done on servers in restaurants okay and they realized you've ever been at a restaurant and a server comes up and stands with the hands behind the back and go what would you like tonight sir and you say i'll have the lobster roll and a glass of red wine and a blah blah and you're like this motherfucker's not he hasn't got a pen or a pad of paper.
sentences.zh: 蔡加尼克？哦，哇，这比我知道的要多得多，这就是你在这里利用的东西。所以，嗯，蔡加尼克效应最初是对餐馆服务员的一项研究，好的。他们意识到你有没有去过餐馆，服务员走过来，双手背在身后，说：先生，今晚你想点什么？你说：我要龙虾卷和一杯红酒，还有巴拉巴拉，你就像：这个混蛋，他没有笔或纸垫。

sentences.en: He's crazy. And then they go off. And what they realized was servers in restaurants were unbelievably good at being able to recall exactly what a table's order was while that table's order was still open.
sentences.zh: 他疯了。然后他们走了。他们意识到的是，餐馆里的服务员在桌子订单仍然开放时，能够准确回忆起桌子订单的能力好得令人难以置信。

sentences.en: So guys in table 16, they want to swap the peas out for a little bit of extra rice.
sentences.zh: 所以16号桌的伙计们，他们想把豌豆换成一点额外的米饭。

sentences.en: And they're doing this thing. As soon as the table was closed, they couldn't remember anything.
sentences.zh: 他们正在做这件事。一旦桌子结账了，他们就什么都不记得了。

sentences.en: So this is an open loop, closed loop system.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个开放循环和封闭循环系统。

sentences.en: And it's built into the brain. the brain abhors an open loop it's the same reason why netflix cliffhangers at the end of every episode guaranteed you'll watch the next one because you can't bear the fact there's even novels in the dark romance genre that make guarantees that there won't be cliffhangers they make they put it on the front or the back of the book and they say no cliffhangers guaranteed which is Let's go.
sentences.zh: 这是大脑与生俱来的机制。大脑厌恶开放循环，这就是为什么Netflix在每集结尾设置悬念，保证你会看下一集，因为你无法忍受那种未完成感。甚至在暗黑浪漫小说领域，有些书会明确保证没有悬念，他们会把这个写在书的封面或封底，承诺绝无悬念，这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: People have so much distaste for it that it's a selling point that you get the closure at the end of it.
sentences.zh: 人们对悬念如此反感，以至于“结局圆满”反而成了一个卖点。

sentences.en: And finishing halfway through a sentence reduces the activation energy required to begin that sentence the next day.
sentences.zh: 而在句子写到一半时停下来，可以降低第二天继续写这个句子的启动能量。

sentences.en: And it keeps it in your mind too overnight.
sentences.zh: 而且这也能让它在你的脑海里留存过夜。

sentences.en: So I think, yeah, whether you've stumbled on it or whether you knew about it, you've managed to leverage a pretty powerful piece of psychology there.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，无论你是偶然发现的，还是早就知道，你确实成功地利用了一个非常强大的心理学原理。

sentences.en: Sick. Going back to the work thing, another one from you that I absolutely adore. it just takes work shit loads and shit loads of work every time i try and dress it up or cut a corner i get brutally reminded the work just needs doing the work doesn't care who you are it just cares that it gets done i'm actually going to reverse quote david goggins on this one but uh i love this quote that he has which he says there's no shortcuts for you david or there's no shortcuts for you, Goggins.
sentences.zh: 太强了。回到工作的话题，你说的另一句话我非常喜欢。它就是需要工作，大量大量的工作。每次我试图粉饰它或走捷径时，我都会被残酷地提醒：工作就是必须完成。工作不在乎你是谁，它只在乎是否被完成。我其实要反向引用一下David Goggins的这句话，但我很喜欢他说的：没有捷径，Goggins。

sentences.en: I heard him say that. And I just love that as a refrain, which is that a lot of people look for a shortcut.
sentences.zh: 我听他说过。我非常喜欢这句话作为座右铭，因为很多人都在寻找捷径。

sentences.en: But the idea that you say like, they're not for you, you don't get to use them.
sentences.zh: 但你说的那种“捷径不属于你”，你没法利用它们。

sentences.en: You are immune to shortcuts. I just love it because then it just further shortcuts the path to the work that needs to get done.
sentences.zh: 你对捷径免疫。我太喜欢这句话了，因为它进一步缩短了通往必须完成的工作的路径。

sentences.en: And I wrote that tweet on my, I don't know, 11th run of this presentation that I'm because that's a recent one.
sentences.zh: 我写那条推文时，大概是我这篇演讲稿的第11次修改了，因为那是最近的事。

sentences.en: And so it was like 11 o'clock at night. And so right now I'm working triple shifts, which is not common for me.
sentences.zh: 当时是晚上11点。所以现在我正在进行“三倍轮班”，这对我来说并不常见。

sentences.en: I usually do two, not three. So for me, a normal workday is like I wake up, I start working at six or seven, and then I go until about six-ish.
sentences.zh: 我通常做两轮，而不是三轮。所以对我来说，正常的工作日是我醒来，六七点开始工作，然后一直干到六点左右。

sentences.en: So it's like 10 to 12, really concentrated hours work.
sentences.zh: 所以大概是10到12个小时的高度集中工作。

sentences.en: And that I can do six and a half days a week.
sentences.zh: 我可以每周这样干六天半。

sentences.en: I usually take Saturday afternoons off. And it's really just because at that point, I can't work anymore and my brain's due.
sentences.zh: 我通常周六下午休息。这真的只是因为到了那个时候，我实在干不动了，大脑已经宕机了。

sentences.en: And then I get my one half day and then I'm good to go. and I'm rearing to work on Sundays.
sentences.zh: 然后我休息半天，我就恢复了，周日又干劲十足。

sentences.en: My triple shift is I go to dinner and I come back at 7.30 and then I work from 7.30 until 11.30 or 1 or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我的“三倍轮班”是指我吃完晚饭，7点半回来，然后从7点半一直工作到11点半或1点，或者随便什么时候。

sentences.en: And when I'm putting in triple shifts is when I know I'm really gassing it.
sentences.zh: 当我开启三倍轮班时，我就知道我真的在全力以赴了。

sentences.en: And that's when I'm repeatedly doing 16, 17 a day of actual productive work.
sentences.zh: 那时我是在反复进行每天16、17个小时的实际生产性工作。

sentences.en: And I hear the same thoughts that everyone does, which is like, it's not going to matter.
sentences.zh: 我也会听到每个人都会有的那种想法，比如“这没关系”。

sentences.en: Like, it's fine. You've like, it's good enough.
sentences.zh: 比如“没事的，这就够好了”。

sentences.en: Like, I hate that. Like it, it makes me sick to even say that.
sentences.zh: 我讨厌那种想法。光是说出来都让我感到恶心。

sentences.en: Right. Because the thing that I like David Goggins, right.
sentences.zh: 没错。因为我喜欢David Goggins的那种态度。

sentences.en: He's got like, there's no shortcuts for you.
sentences.zh: 他有那种“没有捷径”的信条。

sentences.en: I would say the one that I have two that are like my internal ones.
sentences.zh: 我有两个自己的内心准则。

sentences.en: One that is probably the most common is I will do what is required.
sentences.zh: 最常见的一个是：我会做被要求做的事。

sentences.en: And this work needs doing. And there's just no way around it.
sentences.zh: 这项工作需要完成，没有别的办法。

sentences.en: And it's just, it's just looking at the face of the work and it's like smiling back at me, like no one else is going to do it.
sentences.zh: 这就像是直面工作，它也在对我微笑，仿佛在说“没别人会做了”。

sentences.en: Um, and like, I love that one. Like when we're recording content in the early days, we're doing like a hundred shorts every time we did it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个准则。比如我们早期录制内容时，每次都要做一百个短视频。

sentences.en: And it was direct to camera. And it was the only time I could fit it in with all the portfolio stuff they were doing.
sentences.zh: 而且是直接对着镜头。那是唯一能把它塞进我们所有投资组合工作中的时间。

sentences.en: And so I was, it was always like, I will do what's required.
sentences.zh: 所以当时总是这样：我会做被要求做的事。

sentences.en: And that's been a really helpful refrain for me when I'm confronted with, especially when you know what needs to get done.
sentences.zh: 当我面对困难时，这个准则对我非常有帮助，尤其是当你清楚知道什么需要完成的时候。

sentences.en: And the second one is, but I'll know.
sentences.zh: 第二个准则是：但我自己会知道。

sentences.en: And so like, even if it does go well, and even if everyone else says it's great, but I'll know.
sentences.zh: 所以，即使事情进展顺利，即使所有人都说它很棒，但我自己会知道。

sentences.en: And it'll then rob me of all of the joy of all of those moments in that experience, because I'll know that I could have done better.
sentences.zh: 那会剥夺我在那种体验中所有的快乐，因为我知道我本可以做得更好。

sentences.en: And the thing is, is like to quote myself from earlier, Like I've never regretted working harder ever, not once.
sentences.zh: 问题是，引用我之前的话，我从来没有后悔过更努力地工作，一次都没有。

sentences.en: And some people are like, on your deathbed, you're like, no, because I lived every moment of my day doing what I wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说，在你临终时，你会后悔吗？不，因为我每天的每一刻都在做我想做的事。

sentences.en: And I remember I had a boss when I, my first boss after college, she said this thing, I had had a particularly good weekend and she said, I'm pretty sure happiness is stringing as many of those days in a row as you possibly can.
sentences.zh: 我记得我大学毕业后的第一位老板，她说过一件事。当时我刚过了一个特别好的周末，她说：“我相信幸福就是尽可能多地把这些日子串联在一起。”

sentences.en: And although I hated the job, that piece of advice has actually been probably what I, has been my blueprint for how to live, which is like my birthday, it looks the same as my Tuesdays, which looks the same as my Sundays.
sentences.zh: 虽然我讨厌那份工作，但那条建议实际上成了我生活的蓝图，即我的生日看起来和周二一样，也和周日一样。

sentences.en: You know what the original name pool for this podcast was?
sentences.zh: 你知道这个播客最初的名字候选吗？

sentences.en: It's the only time in history, I've done branding my entire adult life and with club nights, all you're doing is coming up with brands.
sentences.zh: 这是历史上唯一一次，我整个成年生活都在做品牌策划，做夜店活动时，你所做的就是想品牌名。

sentences.en: Paradiso, oh, it's tropical. There'll be a flamingo.
sentences.zh: Paradiso，哦，那是热带风情，会有火烈鸟。

sentences.en: Skint, oh, it's a cheap night. It's for people to get fingered in the corner.
sentences.zh: Skint，哦，那是廉价之夜，是给人在角落里亲热用的。

sentences.en: All I did was branding. I was the branding guy.
sentences.zh: 我做的全是品牌策划。我是那个品牌策划人。

sentences.en: I'm pretty good at copywriting. All I did was branding.
sentences.zh: 我文案写得还不错。我做的全是品牌策划。

sentences.en: The one time I've had divine inspiration, three in the morning, wake up with the name was Modern Wisdom.
sentences.zh: 只有那一次，我有过神来之笔，凌晨三点醒来想到的名字是Modern Wisdom。

sentences.en: The one time out of every business, every night, every brand I've ever come up with, that was the one time.
sentences.zh: 在我做过的每一个生意、每一个夜晚、每一个品牌中，那是唯一的一次。

sentences.en: But on the list of the others, Mind and Matter was one of them.
sentences.zh: 但在其他候选名单里，Mind and Matter是其中之一。

sentences.en: The other one was a quote from Tim Ferriss.
sentences.zh: 另一个是Tim Ferriss的一句名言。

sentences.en: It was called Crushing a Tuesday. And he said that what you should aim for in life is for your average Tuesday.
sentences.zh: 它叫“Crushing a Tuesday”（过好一个周二）。他说，你在生活中应该追求的是你的平均周二。

sentences.en: Not the spectacular one-time private jet with the friends to go for the whatever, whatever.
sentences.zh: 不是那种和朋友坐私人飞机去某地参加什么活动的壮观时刻。

sentences.en: Not the UFC power slap launch party staring at the back of Dan Bilzerian's dirty mullet.
sentences.zh: 不是盯着Dan Bilzerian那油腻的鲻鱼头参加UFC Power Slap发布会。

sentences.en: Like, not that. You want your average Tuesday to look the way that you want most of your life to do.
sentences.zh: 不是那种。你想要你的平均周二看起来就是你希望生活中大部分时间的样子。

sentences.en: And when I think about the days that I look back on at the end of my day and think like today was a good day, invariably, it's the same few things.
sentences.zh: 当我回想一天结束时，觉得“今天真是美好的一天”的日子，总是那几件事。

sentences.en: It's I worked very hard on something that I felt was worth doing.
sentences.zh: 我为一件我觉得值得做的事情努力工作了。

sentences.en: I worked out and I spent time with people that I enjoy being around. if I do those three things, I had a good day.
sentences.zh: 我锻炼了身体，并且和我喜欢的人在一起度过了时光。如果我做了这三件事，我今天就过得很好。

sentences.en: And so that's been my, you know, Alex's simple blueprint for doing things.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是我的，你知道的，Alex的简单做事蓝图。

sentences.en: And I think the point that you were making earlier, I think it's worth hitting on again, which is just that like most people's definition of work is a negative one, which is why they abhor it, which is also why they misunderstand so many people who quote, I'll say quote here are successful ahead of them or whatever, is that both people, one person says the word work and the other person hears the word pain.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你刚才提到的那一点，值得再强调一下，那就是大多数人对“工作”的定义是负面的，这就是为什么他们厌恶它，这也是为什么他们误解了许多他们口中所谓的“成功人士”，因为当一个人说“工作”这个词时，另一个人听到的是“痛苦”。

sentences.en: And so the first step to like becoming more successful is understanding the language that the people who are successful are using.
sentences.zh: 所以迈向成功的第一步，是理解成功人士所使用的语言。

sentences.en: They're actually defining the word differently.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上对这个词的定义不同。

sentences.en: And so whatever that thing is that you actually enjoy doing, where you lose track of time when you're in it, even if it's challenging, but usually it is challenging, right?
sentences.zh: 所以无论你真正喜欢做的事情是什么，即使在挑战中你也会忘记时间，通常它确实充满挑战，对吧？

sentences.en: Like it's not easy because then it's boring, right?
sentences.zh: 它不容易，因为如果容易的话就无聊了，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is also why the uncertainty thing is so key, right?
sentences.zh: 这也是为什么不确定性如此关键，对吧？

sentences.en: To not knowing if it's going to work or not.
sentences.zh: 不知道它是否会成功。

sentences.en: You are going to work though either way.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何你都会去做的。

sentences.en: Is that the people who are quote addicted to work make it easy to be addicted to work because they do things worth doing.
sentences.zh: 那些“沉迷于工作”的人，之所以容易沉迷，是因为他们在做值得做的事情。

sentences.en: And I think a lot of it is coming down to making sure that you take the few precious seconds that we have to do the few things that are worth doing for the rest of your life.
sentences.zh: 我认为很大程度上归结于确保你利用我们仅有的宝贵时间，去做余生中那些值得做的事情。

sentences.en: The more I listen to this, the better my life gets.
sentences.zh: 我听得越多，我的生活就越好。

sentences.en: If they don't have what you want, don't listen to what they say.
sentences.zh: 如果他们没有你想要的东西，就别听他们说什么。

sentences.en: There's no greater waste of time than justifying your actions to people who have a life you don't want.
sentences.zh: 没有什么比向那些过着你不想要的生活的人证明你的行为更浪费时间的了。

sentences.en: That was a message to my younger self. But I remember I got in and, well, I won't call it out.
sentences.zh: 那是给我年轻时的自己的一条信息。但我记得我当时，嗯，我不会点名。

sentences.en: Let me see how I can say this the right way.
sentences.zh: 让我看看怎么说才合适。

sentences.en: You know what? I'll just say it. I'll whitewash the names.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？我就直说吧。我把名字隐去。

sentences.en: So I was with a family member and we're all around the kitchen table and it's during the holidays because I don't go home very much.
sentences.zh: 当时我和一位家庭成员在一起，我们围坐在厨房桌旁，那是假期期间，因为我很少回家。

sentences.en: And they kind of started attacking me. And they were like, I would never live your life.
sentences.zh: 他们开始攻击我。他们说：“我永远不会过你的生活。”

sentences.en: You're so unbalanced, like attacking. And I was like, what are you saying?
sentences.zh: “你太不平衡了”，就像是在攻击。我说：“你在说什么？”

sentences.en: And she said, I just would never do that.
sentences.zh: 她说：“我只是永远不会那样做。”

sentences.en: And I was like, all right, well, what part of my life is unbalanced?
sentences.zh: 我说：“好吧，我生活的哪一部分不平衡了？”

sentences.en: I was like, do you feel like my health is unbalanced?
sentences.zh: 我说：“你觉得我的健康不平衡吗？”

sentences.en: I was like, do you feel like my marriage is unbalanced?
sentences.zh: 我说：“你觉得我的婚姻不平衡吗？”

sentences.en: I was like, do you feel like my finances are unbalanced?
sentences.zh: 我说：“你觉得我的财务不平衡吗？”

sentences.en: I was like, what part of my life do you feel like is out of whack?
sentences.zh: 我说：“你觉得我生活的哪一部分出了问题？”

sentences.en: She was like, you know, I'm not as good with words as you are.
sentences.zh: 她说：“你知道，我没你那么会说话。”

sentences.en: And that was the, and I was like, okay, so the fact that you can't make a logical argument, I'm not going to continue how that conversation went.
sentences.zh: 那就是，我说：“好吧，既然你无法提出逻辑论据，我就不继续这场对话了。”

sentences.en: But the TLDR of that was, I really thought a lot about it.
sentences.zh: 但那件事的总结是，我真的思考了很多。

sentences.en: And it came down to, I wouldn't live your life.
sentences.zh: 归根结底就是“我不会过你的生活”。

sentences.en: And my response to that is, good, don't.
sentences.zh: 我的回应是：很好，别过。

sentences.en: It's not your life. It's mine. Live yours the way you want.
sentences.zh: 这不是你的生活，是我的。按你想要的方式过你自己的生活。

sentences.en: And I wouldn't live your life either. And so what ends up happening is they become these statements, these projections that are not actually real.
sentences.zh: 我也不会过你的生活。所以最后发生的事情是，这些话变成了投射，而不是真实的东西。

sentences.en: Now, on some level, maybe they were saying that because there was envy in that aspect of wishing that they were living that life.
sentences.zh: 现在，在某种程度上，也许他们那样说是因为嫉妒，希望自己也能过那种生活。

sentences.en: But in this particular instance, I don't think it was.
sentences.zh: 但在这种特定情况下，我不认为是这样。

sentences.en: I think they genuinely were trying to help.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们是真心想帮忙。

sentences.en: It was a family member. And they thought that I was being misguided.
sentences.zh: 那是我的家人。他们认为我被误导了。

sentences.en: This is an intervention. Let me hold the talking pillow.
sentences.zh: 这就像是一场干预。让我拿着谈话枕头。

sentences.en: Alex, we've all come together because we care about you.
sentences.zh: “Alex，我们聚在一起是因为我们关心你。”

sentences.en: We really feel like we need to have a conversation here. it's exactly what it was.
sentences.zh: “我们真的觉得我们需要在这里进行一次谈话。”这正是当时的情况。

sentences.en: And I got so angry. You? So angry. And you can hear Layla patting my back.
sentences.zh: 我当时非常生气。你？是的，非常生气。你可以听到Layla在拍我的背。

sentences.en: I'm like, see, you can feel the heat coming off of me as I go upstairs.
sentences.zh: 我说，你看，当我上楼时，你能感觉到我身上散发出的热气。

sentences.en: I'm like, how dare she? But it really just came down to her just saying, I don't want to live your life.
sentences.zh: 我说，她怎么敢？但归根结底，她只是说“我不想过你的生活”。

sentences.en: And I think the answer to that question is good.
sentences.zh: 我认为那个问题的答案是：很好。

sentences.en: Don't. And I think that has been one of the things that has diffused so many of these like hateful comments where people dehumanize you or whatever and make you into this ideal that they reject.
sentences.zh: 别过。我认为这已经成为化解许多这种仇恨评论的事情之一，人们将你非人化，或者把你变成他们所拒绝的某种理想。

sentences.en: It's like, you're right. One of the things that I had a mentor tell me to say is like, when you're in an art, if somebody is like, it's like, you're, you're a terrible person, blah, blah, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 就像是：你说得对。我的一位导师告诉我的一件事是，当你在争论时，如果有人说“你是个糟糕的人，巴拉巴拉”，

sentences.en: You just say, you're right.
sentences.zh: 你只需要说：你说得对。

sentences.en: And, and then they have nothing, they have, they have nothing to say.
sentences.zh: 然后他们就没话说了，他们什么都说不出来。

sentences.en: And then you just move on with your life.
sentences.zh: 然后你就继续你的生活。

sentences.en: And so like, in that way, it's acceptance, but of like your, your idea of who I am that you hate so much i accept it i can live with that even though like we don't want to think what if i am it i don't believe that but i can do that and i can end the conversation so i'm taking improv classes at the moment because i'm doing my first live shows in the uk and island oh so this live talk uh thank you yeah uh everything's uh no solo stood on stage for 90 minutes comedy no just oh okay lessons yeah insights and stuff probably some shit that i've learned today uh anyway we released it and every show sold out and then got venue upgraded and then sold out again in less than 45 minutes across all of the dates which was great but then scary because i now had to speak to like three times as many people per night for additional nights on top of what i thought anyway i'm doing improv in improv there is one rule and the rule is don't punk the game so uh we're doing some exercise where we need to make silly noises as we pass this imaginary energy around and i need to go like boing and send it back and you need to go whoosh and pass it on and all this sort of shit the one thing that you're not allowed to do is not make one of the noises that's allowed yeah and i really think about punking the game an awful lot and you see it happen in podcasts you see it happen on tv you see it happen and it can be both destructive and constructive, but it's always destructive to the people that are trying to play the game.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种意义上说，这是一种接受，接受你对我那种充满恨意的看法。我接受它，我可以忍受，尽管我们不想去想“万一我是呢”，我不相信那是真的，但我可以那样做，我可以结束对话。

sentences.en: And it can sometimes be constructive to the person who is punking it.
sentences.zh: 所以我现在正在上即兴表演课，因为我正在英国和爱尔兰进行我的第一次现场演出。哦，是现场演讲，谢谢。嗯，一切都是……没有，在舞台上站90分钟，是喜剧吗？不，只是……哦，好的，课程，见解之类的，可能还有我今天学到的一些东西。总之，我们发布了门票，每场演出都售罄，然后升级了场地，然后在不到45分钟内再次售罄，所有日期都卖光了，这很棒，但也很可怕，因为我现在每晚要面对的人数是原来的三倍，而且还要增加场次。总之，我在做即兴表演，即兴表演中有一条规则，规则是“不要破坏游戏”。所以，我们正在做一些练习，我们需要在传递这种想象中的能量时发出愚蠢的声音，我需要发出“Boing”的声音并传回去，你需要发出“Whoosh”的声音并传下去，诸如此类。唯一不允许做的事情就是不发出允许的声音。我真的经常思考“破坏游戏”这件事，你在播客中看到过，在电视上看到过，它既可以是破坏性的，也可以是建设性的，但对于那些试图玩游戏的人来说，它总是破坏性的。

sentences.en: So what you did is you punked the game. that we are playing a game of tennis.
sentences.zh: 对于那个破坏游戏的人来说，有时它可能是建设性的。

sentences.en: We are hitting the ball back and forth. Here I go.
sentences.zh: 所以你所做的是你破坏了游戏。我们正在玩一场网球游戏。

sentences.en: I hit the ball across the net. And where is it?
sentences.zh: 我们来回击球。轮到我了。

sentences.en: Hit it back. Hit it back to me. Like this is the game that we're playing.
sentences.zh: 我把球打过网。它在哪？

sentences.en: And you didn't move reciprocally back and forth.
sentences.zh: 把它打回来。打回给我。这就是我们正在玩的游戏。

sentences.en: You went orthogonally. You went across on a different axis.
sentences.zh: 而你没有进行往复的互动。

sentences.en: And you're like, I'm not playing this anymore.
sentences.zh: 你走了一条正交的路径。你在不同的轴线上穿过。

sentences.en: This is a different game. I'm not bothered.
sentences.zh: 你就像是说：我不玩这个了。

sentences.en: There's not even words to describe what that means.
sentences.zh: 这是另一个游戏。我不介意。

sentences.en: Now, the way that it can be destructive is especially if you're having, let's say, a meaningful conversation, sometimes people who are uncomfortable with getting into their emotions can use a variety of different things.
sentences.zh: 甚至没有词语来描述这意味着什么。

sentences.en: They can be scathing. They can be mocking.
sentences.zh: 现在，它可能具有破坏性的方式是，特别是如果你正在进行一场有意义的对话时，有时那些对陷入情绪感到不舒服的人可以使用各种不同的东西。

sentences.en: They can laugh, you know, because they don't want to sit with the discomfort of this particular part of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 他们可以尖刻，可以嘲讽。

sentences.en: That's punking the game in a way that I think is destructive both externally and internally.
sentences.zh: 他们可以大笑，你知道，因为他们不想面对对话中这部分的不适感。

sentences.en: That was one that was destructive externally.
sentences.zh: 这是一种我认为在外部和内部都具有破坏性的破坏游戏的方式。

sentences.en: It broke the game, but it was constructive internally. and it is a way refusing to play by the rules that somebody else has set in a game that you didn't agree to is the best prophylactic against stepping into a situation that you do not want and it's one of the things that wealth affords and it's one of the things that freedom affords and freedom is often downstream from wealth remember george one of my really good friends been on the show like five times george mack you'll follow him on twitter he's fucking phenomenal He was on Fox and Friends yesterday talking about his cocaine phone and his kale phone.
sentences.zh: 那是一种在外部具有破坏性的方式。

sentences.en: Like, what the fuck? What world is this?
sentences.zh: 它打破了游戏，但在内部是建设性的。这是一种拒绝按照别人设定的规则玩你没有同意参加的游戏的方式，这是防止陷入你不想要的境地的最佳预防措施。这是财富带来的好处之一，也是自由带来的好处之一，而自由往往是财富的下游。记得George吗？我非常好的朋友之一，上过节目五次了，George Mack，你会在Twitter上关注他，他简直太棒了。他昨天在Fox and Friends上谈论他的可卡因手机和羽衣甘蓝手机。

sentences.en: I remember before the first time that I moved away to work, I've traveled a lot, but it was always in between work.
sentences.zh: 就像，这他妈是什么？这是什么世界？

sentences.en: I never traveled to work. COVID happens.
sentences.zh: 我记得在我第一次搬走工作之前，我旅行过很多次，但总是在工作间隙。我从未为了工作而旅行。COVID发生了。

sentences.en: World gets shut down. Just after Halloween, Boris tells all of the UK, we're going back into lockdown in three days' time and all flights are canceled. so I messaged George and I was like I'm not doing this let's go somewhere he wanted to go to I can't even remember some island that has 300,000 people on it and I was like why don't we do Dubai it's a five hour flight the weather's great I know people it'll be fun it's not got 300,000 people on it it'll be there's Uber and I'll never fucking forget what he replied to me with I got up and I paid 350 pounds for my COVID fit to fly test before he was awake, but he'd sent me a message the night before.
sentences.zh: 世界被封锁了。万圣节刚过，Boris告诉整个英国，我们三天后要重新进入封锁状态，所有航班都被取消了。所以我给George发了信息，我说我不想这样，我们去个地方吧。他想去一个我甚至记不住名字的岛，上面有30万人。我说为什么我们不去迪拜？飞行五个小时，天气很好，我认识人，会很有趣，那里没有30万人，有Uber。我永远不会忘记他回复我的话。我起床并支付了350英镑进行COVID飞行前测试，在他醒来之前，但他前一天晚上给我发了信息。

sentences.en: And this is what compelled me to do it. He said, what's the point in having fuck you freedom if you never say fuck you?
sentences.zh: 这就是促使我去做这件事的原因。他说：“如果你从不说‘去你的’，那么拥有‘去你的’自由有什么意义？”

sentences.en: And I was like, I was so fired up reading that message.
sentences.zh: 我当时读到那条信息时非常激动。

sentences.en: And I was like, yeah, why have I put all of this work in?
sentences.zh: 我说，是的，我为什么要付出所有这些努力？

sentences.en: Why have I done all of these things if I don't ever punk a game that I didn't agree to be a part of?
sentences.zh: 如果我从不破坏我不同意参加的游戏，我做所有这些事情是为了什么？

sentences.en: I think this is really big if we go all the way back to the earlier part of this podcast, when you have the friends who are telling you, oh, must be nice, or you think you're better than us, or, oh, so we can't drink anymore.
sentences.zh: 我认为如果我们回到这个播客的早期部分，这非常重要。当你那些朋友告诉你“那一定很不错”或者“你以为你比我们强”或者“哦，所以我们不能再喝酒了”。

sentences.en: That's when you can be like, yeah.
sentences.zh: 那时候你就可以说：是的。

sentences.en: Then what? Well, then we wouldn't be friends.
sentences.zh: 然后呢？“好吧，那我们就做不成朋友了。”

sentences.en: You're not going to be friends with them eventually anyways, I promise you.
sentences.zh: 反正你最终也不会和他们做朋友了，我向你保证。

sentences.en: Anyone who says that, so you're not going to be friends with.
sentences.zh: 任何说那种话的人，你都不会和他们成为朋友。

sentences.en: If you want to ultimately become the person you want to become, they're only going to reject you harder and harder until eventually you have nothing to share about.
sentences.zh: 如果你最终想成为你想成为的人，他们只会越来越强烈地拒绝你，直到最后你们无话可说。

sentences.en: And the only thing that you'll talk about is the past, which by the way, one of the great leading indicators of, at least in my opinion, of a great way to know when to cut a friend is when they only talk about your past.
sentences.zh: 而你唯一会谈论的就是过去，顺便说一句，在我看来，判断何时切断朋友关系的一个重要指标，就是当他们只谈论你的过去时。

sentences.en: And so punking the game, and it's one of those really uncomfortable things the first time you do it, but then you get more and more comfortable with it because they're like, I would never live your life.
sentences.zh: 所以破坏游戏，这是你第一次做时非常不舒服的事情之一，但随后你会越来越习惯它，因为他们会说“我永远不会过你的生活”。

sentences.en: And you're like, I know.
sentences.zh: 而你会说：我知道。

sentences.en: This relates to another one of yours. Don't trade your self respect for someone else's it's easy to lose theirs and hard to get yours back yeah but i would know But you would know.
sentences.zh: 这与你的另一个准则有关：不要为了别人的尊重而牺牲自己的自尊。失去别人的尊重很容易，找回自己的尊重很难。是的，但我会知道。但你会知道。

sentences.en: Yeah. Related to the sort of cynicism thing that we were talking about earlier, and I call it the cynicism safety blanket, that sour grapes at an existential level.
sentences.zh: 是的。这与我们之前谈论的那种愤世嫉俗有关，我称之为“愤世嫉俗的安全毯”，那是存在主义层面的“酸葡萄”。

sentences.en: I had Sean Puri on the show. You know, Sean, you've been on my first million.
sentences.zh: 我让Sean Puri上了节目。你知道Sean，你上过我的《My First Million》。

sentences.en: He casually dropped this. I don't think his episode's going to be out before this goes, but it's money.
sentences.zh: 他随口说了这个。我不认为他的那一集会在这一集之前播出，但那是金玉良言。

sentences.en: And he said, the cynics get to be right and the optimists get to be rich.
sentences.zh: 他说：愤世嫉俗者总是对的，而乐观主义者总是富有的。

sentences.en: And from you, I think the winner's mindset sits in the uncomfortable place between two surface level contradictions, extreme paranoia in the present and unshakable faith in the future.
sentences.zh: 从你那里，我认为赢家的心态存在于两个表面矛盾之间的不舒服位置：对当下的极端偏执和对未来的坚定信念。

sentences.en: The tension between the two makes someone hard to beat today and hard to outlast tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 两者之间的张力使一个人今天难以被击败，明天难以被超越。

sentences.en: The cynics get to be right and the optimists get to be rich.
sentences.zh: 愤世嫉俗者总是对的，而乐观主义者总是富有的。

sentences.en: One of the biggest fallacies of the advice from people who are in your current situation is that they are right most of the time.
sentences.zh: 处于你当前处境的人给出的建议中，最大的谬论之一就是他们大多数时候都是对的。

sentences.en: When you bring a girl home 99 times out of 100, when your parents say, she's not the girl, I don't like her, she won't last.
sentences.zh: 当你带女孩回家时，100次里有99次，当你的父母说“她不是那个女孩，我不喜欢她，她不会长久”。

sentences.en: They're right every single time, except for the one time it matters and you end up marrying the person.
sentences.zh: 他们每次都对，除了那一次至关重要的时刻，你最终和那个人结婚了。

sentences.en: When they say you're not going to succeed, this idea of yours, it's not going to last.
sentences.zh: 当他们说你不会成功，你的这个想法不会长久时。

sentences.en: And they're right every single time, except for the one time that matters when you hit it big.
sentences.zh: 他们每次都对，除了那一次至关重要的时刻，当你大获成功时。

sentences.en: And so it's one of those things where they are right more times, but they are not more right.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是那种情况，他们对的次数更多，但他们并不更正确。

sentences.en: So good. Yeah, I wonder whether it's a function of all of our opinions being permanently etched in stone on social media, that it's very easy to seem smart, to have a heterodox idea if you go against the mainstream, because it's romantic.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。是的，我不知道这是否是因为我们在社交媒体上所有观点都被永久刻在石头上，显得聪明、有异端思想、反主流非常容易，因为这很浪漫。

sentences.en: Oh, I had this alternative. I had this negative opinion.
sentences.zh: 哦，我有这个替代方案。我有这个负面观点。

sentences.en: I'm not like one of those sheep. I'll believe that things are going to be worse than they are.
sentences.zh: 我不像那些羊群。我相信事情会比现在更糟。

sentences.en: And then if it turns out better, guess what?
sentences.zh: 然后如果结果更好，猜猜怎么着？

sentences.en: I say your expectation is super low. Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 我说你的期望值太低了。恭喜你。

sentences.en: You can thank me later. You're like, that is distilled down.
sentences.zh: 你以后可以感谢我。你就像是说，那被提炼出来了。

sentences.en: British culture at its worst is low expectations.
sentences.zh: 英国文化最糟糕的一面就是低期望值。

sentences.en: Low expectations delivered through satirical cynicism.
sentences.zh: 通过讽刺性的愤世嫉俗传递的低期望值。

sentences.en: Why are you doing that? That's lame. That's for losers.
sentences.zh: 你为什么要那样做？那很烂。那是给失败者做的。

sentences.en: That's something that we wouldn't do. You should stop doing the different thing.
sentences.zh: 那是我们不会做的事情。你应该停止做那些与众不同的事情。

sentences.en: Tall poppy, you're the one that gets cut down. and it's all that it's like all it shows to me now is a kind of groupthink almost like the worst kind of mental telepathy where everybody believes the most unuseful thoughts that everybody else has yeah at scale and all it does is lower the bar that you need to get up?
sentences.zh: “高罂粟花”，你就是那个被砍掉的人。对我来说，现在这一切只显示出一种群体思维，几乎是最糟糕的那种心灵感应，每个人都相信其他人拥有的最无用的想法，而且规模很大，它所做的只是降低了你需要达到的门槛。

sentences.en: I think it's that you're right thing, which is someone says, that's lame, that sucks, blah, blah, blah.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是那个“你是对的”的事情，即有人说“那很烂，那很糟糕，巴拉巴拉”。

sentences.en: And you say like, you're right. It does.
sentences.zh: 而你说：你是对的。确实如此。

sentences.en: You just keep punking the game. When anyone comes to trying, they're playing a different game than you.
sentences.zh: 你只是继续破坏游戏。当任何人试图尝试时，他们玩的游戏和你不同。

sentences.en: So you shouldn't try and play by their rules because they're going to try and get you to play their game so that they can beat you at the game, which is the status game of that little circle. but you're playing a much wider game that includes more players.
sentences.zh: 所以你不应该试图按照他们的规则玩，因为他们会试图让你玩他们的游戏，这样他们就可以在那个游戏中打败你，也就是那个小圈子的地位游戏。但你玩的是一个更广阔的游戏，包含更多的玩家。

sentences.en: And so even though locally you have these, your incoming information that you're taking in is disproportionate from people that you're not actually playing against.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在局部你有这些，你接收到的输入信息与你实际上没有与之竞争的人不成比例。

sentences.en: And so it's basically just noise. It's irrelevant.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上只是噪音。它是无关紧要的。

sentences.en: Because if you look on a long enough time horizon, the likelihood that you're like, I mean, again, I think about death a lot, but the idea that...
sentences.zh: 因为如果你看足够长的时间跨度，你像……我的意思是，再次，我经常思考死亡，但那个想法……

sentences.en: When I die, people will be dividing up my assets, arguing over who gets what.
sentences.zh: 当我死的时候，人们会瓜分我的资产，争论谁得到什么。

sentences.en: There's going to be a caterer at my funeral.
sentences.zh: 我的葬礼上会有餐饮服务商。

sentences.en: Some people won't make it because something came up and they got busy.
sentences.zh: 有些人不会来，因为有事耽搁了，他们很忙。

sentences.en: And then the few people that are there are probably no one that I have in my life right now.
sentences.zh: 然后在那里的少数几个人，可能都不是我现在生活中的任何人。

sentences.en: And the fact that every single person that I have in my life might not even make it to the funeral to speak over me while I'm dead.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我生命中的每一个人甚至可能都不会出现在葬礼上为我致辞。

sentences.en: It's like, why on earth would I listen to them while I'm alive.
sentences.zh: 就像，为什么我还要听他们的，当我活着的时候？

sentences.en: Like they can't even make it to probably the single most important personal day of someone's life is someone's funeral, right?
sentences.zh: 他们甚至可能无法参加一个人一生中最重要的一天，也就是葬礼，对吧？

sentences.en: The one time you can pay your last respect and they don't even do that.
sentences.zh: 唯一一次你可以表达最后的敬意，他们甚至都不做。

sentences.en: And so it's like, why would I give any weight to what these people are doing when they're not even going to be there on the day that matters most?
sentences.zh: 所以这就像，为什么我要给这些人的行为任何权重，当他们甚至不会出现在最重要的一天时？

sentences.en: And six months later, they're not even remember who I was.
sentences.zh: 六个月后，他们甚至不记得我是谁了。

sentences.en: And anybody who's had a death in their family recently knows that in the moment, it's terrible for you.
sentences.zh: 任何最近家里有亲人去世的人都知道，在那一刻，这对你来说很糟糕。

sentences.en: And then six months later, life moves on.
sentences.zh: 然后六个月后，生活继续。

sentences.en: But the thing is, is that we just never paint ourselves as the person who dies.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，我们从来没有把自己描绘成那个死去的人。

sentences.en: But to me, that's incredibly freeing because then it's like, if six months after I'm dead, no one is going to say my name.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，这非常令人自由，因为那样的话，如果我死后六个月，没有人会说我的名字。

sentences.en: No one is going to remember what I did. Then no one's going to, then it doesn't matter what I do today.
sentences.zh: 没有人会记得我做了什么。那么没有人会……那么我今天做什么并不重要。

sentences.en: And I think that some people see it as really hopeless, but I see it as very hopeful because it means we have absolute freedom and we can do crazy shit.
sentences.zh: 我认为有些人觉得这很绝望，但我认为这很有希望，因为它意味着我们拥有绝对的自由，我们可以做疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: Like why have fuck you money if you can't say fuck you?
sentences.zh: 就像，如果你不能说“去你的”，为什么还要有“去你的”钱？

sentences.en: Yeah. Learning isn't a spectator sport. It comes from doing, which means if you're not doing the stuff you consume every day, you're not learning. you're just procrastinating.
sentences.zh: 是的。学习不是一项观众运动。它来自于做，这意味着如果你每天不去做你消费的东西，你就不是在学习。你只是在拖延。

sentences.en: Ooh, this is fun. All right. So I'm going to define some terms.
sentences.zh: 哦，这很有趣。好吧。所以我要定义一些术语。

sentences.en: Learning, let me say this way.
sentences.zh: 学习，让我这样说。

sentences.en: Intelligence means rate of learning. Like that's what, that's how, remember I talk about operationalizing words.
sentences.zh: 智力意味着学习率。就像那是……记得我谈论操作化词汇吗？

sentences.en: So rate of learning is intelligence. So then you, which means it's a rate, not a, not an attribute as an aside, which then means you have to define learning.
sentences.zh: 所以学习率就是智力。所以那么你……这意味着它是一个比率，而不是一个属性，顺便说一句，这意味着你必须定义学习。

sentences.en: Learning means same condition, new behavior.
sentences.zh: 学习意味着：相同条件，新行为。

sentences.en: So if I hold up a red card and then I slap you and then I'll hold a red card again and then you duck, you've learned.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我举起一张红牌，然后我扇你一巴掌，然后我再次举起红牌，然后你躲开了，你就学会了。

sentences.en: If you wake up every day and life shows you a red card and then you don't duck and you don't change, then you have learned nothing.
sentences.zh: 如果你每天醒来，生活给你看一张红牌，然后你不躲，也不改变，那么你就什么都没学到。

sentences.en: And so if you go to a weekend and you go to a workshop and then the next day you go back and you do the exact same activities in the same conditions and you have no new behavior, it means you learned nothing. it also means you're stupid because it means your rate of learning is slow.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你去参加一个周末，去参加一个研讨会，然后第二天你回去，在相同的条件下做完全相同的活动，并且没有新的行为，这意味着你什么都没学到。这也意味着你很笨，因为这意味着你的学习率很慢。

sentences.en: So if someone is intelligent, I can show them the red card.
sentences.zh: 所以如果一个人很聪明，我可以给他们看红牌。

sentences.en: And on the first go, they change their behavior.
sentences.zh: 在第一次尝试时，他们就改变了行为。

sentences.en: And so by defining intelligence that way and defining learning that way, it allowed me to start thinking, well, I want to be smart.
sentences.zh: 所以通过那样定义智力和定义学习，它让我开始思考，好吧，我想变得聪明。

sentences.en: And this circumstance had this outcome last time.
sentences.zh: 这种情况上次有这个结果。

sentences.en: And so the next time I see this circumstance, this red card, I'm going to change my behavior.
sentences.zh: 所以下次我看到这种情况，这张红牌，我要改变我的行为。

sentences.en: And so when we consume the information that you have on this podcast or whatever it is, There's probably a circumstance, whether it's a conversation that you're supposed to have, but you're aren't having.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们消费你在播客上拥有的信息或任何东西时，可能有一种情况，无论是你应该进行但没有进行的对话。

sentences.en: It's a decision that you need to make, but you're putting off.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你需要做出但一直在推迟的决定。

sentences.en: That's the red card. It comes up again. And the question is whether you're going to get slaps or you're going to duck.
sentences.zh: 那是红牌。它再次出现。问题是你会被扇巴掌还是会躲开。

sentences.en: And that's whether you know whether you learned or not.
sentences.zh: 这就是你知道你是否学会了。

sentences.en: And every time you get shown the red card and you do the same exact thing, you just proved to yourself that your rate of learning is slower.
